Impression: Large chronic left subdural hematoma with associated mass effect and midline shift. Neurosurgical evaluation for potential decompression is indicated.

Brain MRI demonstrates marked enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal prominence, which is relatively preserved over the high convexities (DESH sign). No aqueductal stenosis is identified, and there is a prominent flow void in the aqueduct of Sylvius.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to cortical atrophy, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence is recommended.

Time-of-flight MR angiography (MRA) of the circle of Willis demonstrates normal caliber and course of the bilateral internal carotid, middle cerebral, anterior cerebral, basilar, and vertebral arteries. There is no evidence of aneurysmal dilation, stenosis, or vascular malformation. Brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology without focal defects.

Impression: Unremarkable MR angiogram of the brain. No intracranial aneurysm or vascular anomaly identified.

High-resolution T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 brain imaging shows an intensely enhancing, well-circumscribed mass measuring 1.8 x 1.4 cm located in the right cerebellopontine angle. The lesion extends into the internal auditory canal, causing widening of the canal. The adjacent brainstem and cerebellum are minimally compressed.

Impression: Right vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with intra- and extra-canalicular components. ENT/neurosurgery follow-up is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation shows normal cerebral cortical development. The sulcation pattern is entirely congruent with late second-trimester standards, demonstrating early superior temporal sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium of the right lateral ventricle measuring 5.7 mm and the left measuring 5.6 mm. The interhemispheric structures are normal.

The chest demonstrates symmetrical lungs with high T2 signal relative to the liver, representing normal lung fluid. Impression: Structurally unremarkable fetal MRI with appropriate development of the central nervous system and major organ systems.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 47-year-old female with a history of ventricular tachycardia of left bundle branch block morphology. The right ventricle is severely dilated (RVEDV 152 mL/m²) with regional dyskinesis and microaneurysms noted in the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and the free wall ('triangle of dysplasia'). The right ventricular ejection fraction is significantly reduced at 31%. The left ventricle is normal in size and function (LVEF 58%) without regional abnormalities. Late gadolinium enhancement is noted along the RV free wall.

Impression: Features highly characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major Task Force criteria based on severe RV dilation, localized RV dyskinesis, and reduced RVEF.

Evaluation of the dural venous sinuses reveals a complete absence of the normal flow void within the posterior half of the superior sagittal sinus and the right transverse sinus, replaced by high T1 and T2 signal. Following contrast administration, a distinct "empty delta sign" is visualized on coronal and transverse images, demonstrating a filling defect. Mild localized cortical edema is present in the right parietal lobe without parenchymal hemorrhage.

Impression: Extensive dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal and right transverse sinuses. No associated hemorrhagic infarction is seen on the current study.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows severe cystic enlargement of the posterior fossa. There is marked hypoplasia and rotation of the cerebellar vermis, which is upwardly displaced by a large fluid collection in the posterior fossa that communicates widely with the fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and torcular herophili are abnormally elevated. Mild bilateral ventriculomegaly is noted, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 10.5 mm on both sides. Cortical migration and sulcation appear appropriate for gestational age.

The rest of the fetal spine and thorax appear normal. Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of a Dandy-Walker malformation, characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, an enlarged posterior fossa cystic space communicating with the fourth ventricle, and torcular elevation.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe skeletal dysplasia. There is marked shortening and bowing of all long bones, with a characteristic 'telephone receiver' morphology of the femora. The thoracic cavity is extremely narrow and bell-shaped with short ribs, leading to secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Intracranial anatomy shows normal ventricular measurements, with the lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.9 mm.

Sulcal development is normal for 27 weeks. Polyhydramnios is present. Impression: Severe micromelic skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with Thanatophoric Dysplasia Type I, with severe pulmonary hypoplasia and associated polyhydramnios.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 12.8 mm on the left and 12.2 mm on the right, indicating moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly. The third ventricle is minimally dilated. The corpus callosum is intact, though thin. The cortical sulcation and operculization patterns are appropriate for 29 weeks gestation. No intra-axial hemorrhage, subependymal heterotopia, or other cerebral parenchymal lesions are seen.

The posterior fossa and somatic structures are normal. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. No secondary intracranial anomalies or structural brain lesions identified. Recommend follow-up and pediatric neurology consultation.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates age-appropriate, normal development of the fetal brain. Sulcation is normal, with well-formed parieto-occipital, calcarine, and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricular atrial widths are symmetric at 6.3 mm, and the posterior fossa is normal.

Fetal chest, abdominal viscera, and spine are normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with normal brain development and appropriate sulcation for 30 weeks.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks 2 days gestation. The fetal brain shows normal development. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.5 mm bilaterally, which is well within normal limits. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Sulcation is appropriate for 30 weeks, with visible central and parietal sulci.

The fetal chest, abdomen, and spine are normal. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating healthy development of the central nervous system and major internal organs.

MRI brain and MRA shows an acute subarachnoid hemorrhage with prominent blood products tracking in the suprasellar, prepontine, and ambient cisterns. MRA of the circle of Willis demonstrates a focal, 5.2 mm outpouching arising from the anterior communicating artery (ACOM) consistent with a saccular aneurysm.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage secondary to a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Urgent endovascular or neurosurgical intervention is indicated.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 2.2 cm in maximal diameter. There is a significant left-to-right shunt, with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 1.9. Moderate right ventricular and right atrial dilation is present, with preserved right ventricular systolic function (RVEF 52%). The pulmonary valve is anatomically normal.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect causing significant left-to-right shunt and right-sided cardiac volume overload. Recommend clinical correlation for potential closure.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 68-year-old female with known coronary artery disease and prior stenting. There is a regional wall motion abnormality involving the mid-to-apical anterior and anteroseptal walls, characterized by akinesis. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals a subendocardial scar in the anterior and anteroseptal segments, extending to approximately 50-75% transmurality, matching a left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery territory. The left ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 38%.

Impression: Ischemic heart disease with an established subendocardial myocardial infarction in the LAD distribution. The degree of transmural scar suggests partial viability of the affected anterior myocardium.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a dense, transmural late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) pattern involving the mid and apical inferior and inferolateral walls of the left ventricle. There is associated severe hypokinesis to akinesis of these segments, with significant thinning of the affected myocardium. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is elevated, and the ejection fraction is reduced at 35%.

Impression: Chronic, transmural myocardial infarction in the right coronary artery territory with significant adverse remodeling and depressed left ventricular systolic function.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain is performed for persistent post-dural puncture headache. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are entirely unremarkable. There is no evidence of intracranial hypotension (such as dural pachymeningeal enhancement, subdural fluid collections, or pituitary engorgement) and no signs of intracranial hemorrhage.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, vascular, or secondary signs of intracranial hypotension identified to account for postpartum spinal-related headaches.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient presenting with acute dyspnea three weeks postpartum. The left ventricle is severely dilated, with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 112 mL/m2, and demonstrates globally reduced systolic function with an estimated LVEF of 28%. Mild functional mitral regurgitation is noted secondary to annular dilation. No focal myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of peripartum cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction. Clinical follow-up and medical management are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis associated with a markedly enlarged posterior fossa cystic space that communicates directly with the fourth ventricle. This is accompanied by an elevated tentorium cerebelli. The left and right lateral ventricles show mild ventriculomegaly, measuring 11.5 mm and 11.8 mm at the level of the atrium, respectively. Cerebral sulcation is early but normal for 24 weeks.

The remainder of the fetal survey, including the fetal thorax, abdomen, and spine, is structurally normal. Impression: Brain findings are highly characteristic of Dandy-Walker malformation with associated mild ventriculomegaly. Prenatal counseling and pediatric neurology consultation are recommended.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior portion (rostrum and genu) is present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. There is mild dilation of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), with the left atrium measuring 10.5 mm and the right measuring 10.2 mm. Sulcation pattern is appropriate for 25 weeks gestation.

Remaining intracranial structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are unremarkable. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large zone of restricted diffusion involving the right insular cortex, temporal-parietal operculum, and deep gray nuclei, with corresponding ADC hypointensity. FLAIR imaging shows loss of normal cortical sulcal effacement and mild edema in the same distribution, suggesting hyperacute to acute infarction. MR angiography shows occlusion of the distal M1 segment of the right middle cerebral artery.

Impression: Acute right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory ischemic stroke with associated M1 occlusion. Immediate neurological intervention is indicated.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) with fusion of the left and right coronary cusps. The valve exhibits restricted opening in systole, leading to an eccentric flow jet. The calculated aortic valve area by planimetry is 0.9 cm2, representing severe aortic stenosis. There is moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with a septal thickness of 15 mm.

Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an LVEF of 55%. No late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the myocardium. Impression: Congenital bicuspid aortic valve with severe aortic stenosis and associated moderate concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

Brain MRI performed for postpartum headache evaluation demonstrates no evidence of acute infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, or dural venous sinus thrombosis. The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and configuration for the patient's age. Intracranial flow voids are fully preserved and no abnormal extra-axial fluid collections are identified.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural etiology identified to explain the patient's acute postpartum headaches. Paranasal sinuses are clear.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular size, volume, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are identified. T2-weighted imaging shows no signs of myocardial edema, and late gadolinium enhancement imaging is entirely negative for focal myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, or myocardial infarction to explain the patient's postpartum palpitations.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates bilateral, symmetric areas of high T2 and FLAIR signal intensity within the subcortical white matter of the parieto-occipital lobes, without associated restricted diffusion. These findings are highly suggestive of vasogenic edema. There is no evidence of hemorrhage or mass effect, and the ventricles are normal in size. The patient is noted to be 5 days postpartum.

Impression: Bilateral parieto-occipital subcortical white matter changes compatible with Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES), likely secondary to postpartum preeclampsia/eclampsia. Clinical correlation and close blood pressure monitoring are recommended.

High-resolution brain MRI of the cerebellopontine angles (CPA) demonstrates a well-circumscribed, "ice cream cone" shaped enhancing mass centered in the left internal auditory canal with extension into the CPA cistern. The lesion measures 1.6 x 1.1 cm, widening the porus acusticus. There is mild mass effect on the left cerebellar peduncle, but no brainstem displacement.

Impression: Left-sided intracanalicular and extracanalicular vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with mild mass effect on the adjacent cerebellar peduncle. No hydrocephalus is present.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chambers. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) is 135 mL and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 62%, reflecting normal global and regional systolic function. Right ventricular size and systolic performance are within normal limits with an ejection fraction (RVEF) of 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal thinning are observed.

Following administration of gadolinium, there is no evidence of late myocardial enhancement to suggest focal scar, fibrosis, or infiltration. Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. No anatomical or functional abnormalities identified.

MR of the brain shows a large area of restricted diffusion on DWI and corresponding ADC hypointensity involving the right insular cortex and frontoparietal operculum. High T2/FLAIR signal is also noted in this distribution, representing early vasogenic edema. The major intracranial arteries show a signal void abnormality in the right MCA segment.

Impression: Acute-to-subacute ischemic stroke in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory. Urgent vascular neurology evaluation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate progressive dyspnea in a 27-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. Imaging demonstrates normal biventricular chamber sizes and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 59%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 55%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, pericardial effusion, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No maternal structural heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or active myocarditis identified to explain the dyspnea, which may represent physiological dyspnea of pregnancy.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows normal, mature fetal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate highly advanced sulcation and gyration, with deep and well-defined central and secondary sulci, appropriate for 36 weeks gestation. The ventricular system is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.3 mm at the atria. The corpus callosum and brainstem are structurally perfect.

The fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and extremities are fully visualized and free of any structural abnormalities. Amniotic fluid volume and placental appearance are normal. Impression: Completely normal, near-term fetal MRI demonstrating advanced, age-appropriate structural development.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 36-year-old female for cardiotoxicity screening during her ongoing post-mastectomy breast cancer surveillance program. Multiplanar cine imaging demonstrates completely normal left ventricular size and geometry. Left ventricular ejection fraction is well-maintained at 59% (stable compared to baseline echocardiography), without evidence of wall motion abnormality.

No myocardial edema is identified on T2 mapping, and no late gadolinium enhancement is present to suggest subclinical necrosis or fibrosis. Right ventricular function is preserved (EF 54%). Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular systolic function and no evidence of chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity.

Brain MRI performed with and without intravenous contrast demonstrates normal gray-white matter differentiation. No areas of restricted diffusion, acute parenchymal hemorrhage, or intracranial mass lesions are identified. The ventricles, sulci, and basal cisterns are normal in caliber. No abnormal enhancement is visualized.

Impression: Completely normal MR imaging of the brain. No acute or chronic intracranial pathology detected.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a complete absence of both kidneys in the renal fossae. No identifiable renal parenchymal tissue or renal arteries are visualized. The urinary bladder is not distended and is virtually empty. There is severe, near-total oligohydramnios (anhydramnios), which limits detailed resolution of the extremities and face, but the thoracic cavity appears compressed and lung volumes are extremely small.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. This constellation of findings is consistent with classic Potter's sequence.

MR imaging shows a tightly packed cluster of dilated vascular channels (flow voids) in the right parietal lobe measuring approximately 2.5 x 2.1 x 1.8 cm, with a prominent dilated draining vein heading toward the superior sagittal sinus. Surrounding brain tissue shows localized gliosis but no acute hemorrhage or ischemic change. Susceptibility-weighted imaging shows significant blooming, reflecting past microhemorrhages.

Impression: Arteriovenous malformation (AVM) of the right parietal lobe. Neurosurgical and interventional neuroradiology referral is recommended.

MRI of the brain shows a wedge-shaped area of restricted diffusion (hyperintense on DWI, hypointense on ADC map) in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule and the lentiform nucleus. Corresponding T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is noted, consistent with acute to subacute infarction.

Impression: Acute to subacute ischemic infarct in the left MCA territory (deep perforating branches). No hemorrhagic transformation is observed on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI).

Cardiac MRI reveals pronounced dilation and regional dyskinesis of the right ventricular free wall, with multiple microaneurysm formations within the RV outflow tract and apex. Right ventricular ejection fraction is severely depressed at 34%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging confirms extensive transmural enhancement of the right ventricular free wall, indicating fibrofatty replacement of the myocardium.

Impression: Findings strongly diagnostic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on Task Force criteria, presenting a major risk factor for ventricular tachyarrhythmias.

Cardiac MRI was obtained for the evaluation of persistent ventricular ectopy. The right ventricle is significantly dilated with an end-diastolic volume index of 118 mL/m2 and exhibits regional dyskinesis of the right ventricular free wall. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows focal areas of mid-myocardial hyperenhancement along the right ventricular outflow tract. Left ventricular size and systolic function are preserved (LVEF 55%).

Impression: Morphological features and enhancement patterns highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC). Correlation with electrophysiological study is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of bilateral kidneys in the renal fossae. The urinary bladder is not visualized, and there is profound, severe oligohydramnios resulting in compression of the fetal trunk. The adrenal glands are present but are oriented horizontally ('lying down sign') within the empty renal beds. There is secondary mild compression of the thorax and limbs.

Intracranial structures are poorly visualized due to lack of amniotic fluid pocketing, but gross ventricular size appears normal, and no open spinal dysraphism is detected. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe oligohydramnios (classic Potter sequence phenotype).

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation shows partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with absence of the splenium and body. There is mild colpocephaly, with posterior lateral ventricular horns measuring 11.2 mm. Early opercularization and sulcation are otherwise appropriate for 31 weeks, showing well-developed parieto-occipital fissures.

The spine is intact. The chest and abdomen appear normal. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild ventriculomegaly (colpocephaly). Follow-up imaging and postnatal clinical correlation are advised.

Cardiac MRI performed for atypical, postpartum chest tightness. The myocardium is of normal thickness with no evidence of focal edema, regional hypokinesis, or ischemia. Left ventricular cavity size is normal, and global systolic function is well-preserved with an ejection fraction of 65%. Right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows no abnormal enhancement.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal chamber sizes and systolic function, with no objective findings of peripartum cardiomyopathy, acute myocarditis, or ischemia.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 35-year-old female with a history of repaired coarctation of the aorta, undergoing pre-pregnancy counseling. There is mild residual narrowing of the distal aortic arch at the prior repair site, measuring 1.6 cm, with an estimated peak gradient of 18 mmHg across the obstruction. The left ventricle is mildly hypertrophied with an end-diastolic wall thickness of 12 mm, and LVEF is preserved at 58%.

Impression: Mild residual aortic coarctation with stable left ventricular hypertrophy and preserved systolic function. These findings represent a stable baseline prior to planned conception.

3D TOF MR angiography (MRA) of the circle of Willis demonstrates a focal, saccular outpouching arising from the anterior communicating artery, measuring 4.5 x 3.8 mm. The neck of the aneurysm is relatively narrow, measuring approximately 2.0 mm. No other vascular anomalies or stenoses are identified within the major intracranial vessels. The brain parenchyma is otherwise normal.

Impression: Unruptured saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery. Neurosurgical or endovascular consultation is recommended for further evaluation.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates herniation of the stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe into the left hemithorax. This herniation causes a significant mediastinal shift to the right and marked compression of the right and left lungs. Lung volumes are reduced, with the observed-to-expected lung volume (O/E LHR) measured at 35%. Intracranial structures are normal with a lateral ventricle atrium of 5.1 mm.

Normal sulcation of the cerebral cortex is seen for 30 weeks. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with associated severe lung hypoplasia and mediastinal shift.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a dilated left ventricle with a calculated ejection fraction of 38%. There is severe hypokinesis localized to the apex and the anterior and anteroseptal walls. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals a transmural pattern of hyperenhancement involving the mid-to-apical anterior wall and the apex, which corresponds precisely to a left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery distribution.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with non-viable myocardium in the LAD territory, consistent with a prior large anterior myocardial infarction. Left ventricular systolic dysfunction is moderate-to-severe.

Dedicated pituitary protocol MRI demonstrates a small, hypo-enhancing lesion measuring 6 mm in the left lateral aspect of the anterior pituitary gland on dynamic post-contrast imaging. The pituitary stalk is minimally deviated to the right, and the optic chiasm is structurally normal with no signs of compression. The cavernous sinuses are bilaterally intact.

Impression: Pituitary microadenoma measuring 6 mm. Clinical correlation with serum prolactin levels and endocrine function is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates entirely normal cerebral cortical development. Sulcation, gyration, and opercularization are normal for gestational age. The ventricular system is normal, with lateral ventricles measuring 5.8 mm in the left atrium and 5.9 mm in the right atrium. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are structurally intact.

The fetal spine, lungs, diaphragm, and solid organs within the abdomen are unremarkable. No skeletal or body wall abnormalities are seen. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate growth and brain development.

Brain MR imaging shows a broad-based, extra-axial mass arising from the left sphenoid wing, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The lesion is homogeneously hyperintense to gray matter on T2, hypointense on T1, and demonstrates intense, uniform enhancement following gadolinium administration with a classic dural tail sign. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent left temporal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Extra-axial mass arising from the left sphenoid wing, highly characteristic of a meningioma. Mild surrounding mass effect and edema in the left temporal lobe are noted.

Cardiac MRI performed to evaluate frequent premature ventricular contractions in a 29-year-old female during her second trimester of pregnancy. The left ventricular volumes are within normal physiological limits for gestational state (LVEDV 130 mL, LVESV 50 mL), with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 61%. Right ventricular size, morphology, and systolic function are normal with an ejection fraction of 56%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are identified, and there is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI showing normal biventricular size and function. No structural heart disease, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement is observed to account for cardiac symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks 1 day gestation demonstrates completely normal fetal intracranial and extracranial anatomy. The brain shows appropriate secondary sulcation and gyral patterns for this stage of development. The lateral ventricular system is normal in caliber, with symmetric atrial measurements of 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum and cerebellar structures are fully formed and within normal limits.

Fetal chest, heart, abdomen, kidneys, and spine are normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with age-appropriate cerebral development and no evidence of fetal anomalies.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior callosal body and genu are present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. The third ventricle is mildly elevated. The lateral ventricles show asymmetric colpocephaly, with the posterior horns measuring 12.5 mm on the left and 11.2 mm on the right.

Cortical gyration and sulcation are normal and well-developed for 35 weeks gestation. The rest of the intracranial and fetal anatomy is unremarkable. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated moderate colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral renal abnormalities. The fetal kidneys are significantly enlarged and filled with multiple, variable-sized, non-communicating cysts throughout the parenchyma. No normal renal tissue is seen. The urinary bladder is not visualized, and there is profound oligohydramnios. Due to the lack of amniotic fluid, fetal crowding is present, and thoracic volume is reduced, indicating secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial anatomy is structurally normal for 34 weeks, although assessment is challenging due to motion and crowding. Impression: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney disease with associated severe oligohydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. This constellation carries a guarded prognosis.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, located immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrowest segment of the aortic lumen measures approximately 8 mm in diameter, compared to 19 mm at the diaphragmatic level. Velocity-encoded imaging shows a peak velocity of 3.4 m/s across the stenosis, with diastolic runoff.

Left ventricular mass index is mildly increased at 88 g/m² indicating concentric hypertrophy, but global left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 62%. Large collateral vessels are visualized in the chest wall. Impression: Classic findings of coarctation of the aorta with significant hemodynamically relevant stenosis and secondary left ventricular hypertrophy.

Multiple hyperintense lesions are identified scattered throughout both cerebral hemispheres, notably at the grey-white junctions of the parietal and temporal lobes. Several of these lesions demonstrate peripheral rim enhancement, microhemorrhages on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI), and surrounding vasogenic edema. The patient has a known history of gestational choriocarcinoma.

Impression: Multiple hemorrhagic intra-axial lesions, highly suggestive of intracranial metastases from gestational choriocarcinoma.

Cardiac MRI shows severe left ventricular dilation with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 134 mL/m². There is global, diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle with a severely depressed left ventricular ejection fraction calculated at 27%. The right ventricular chamber dimensions and function are near the lower limit of normal with an ejection fraction of 47%.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate mid-wall linear enhancement within the mid-to-apical septum, a pattern classic for non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. Impression: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction, severe chamber dilation, and mid-wall fibrosis.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximum diastolic interventricular septal thickness measuring 22 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, leading to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate posteriorly directed mitral regurgitation. The left ventricular cavity size is small, but systolic function is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 72%.

Late gadolinium enhancement sequences reveal patchy, mid-myocardial hyperenhancement at the anterior and posterior RV-LV insertion points, characteristic of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Impression: Asymmetric hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant septal hypertrophy, SAM of the mitral valve, and classic insertion-point late gadolinium enhancement.

Brain MRI with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) reveals numerous punctate foci of signal void in the cerebral cortex and subcortical white matter, predominant in the parieto-occipital and temporal lobes. There are no deep basal ganglia microhemorrhages. Mild chronic microvascular ischemic white matter changes are present.

Impression: Multiple lobar microhemorrhages in a distribution strongly characteristic of Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA). No acute large-vessel ischemic stroke or macro-hemorrhage.

Cardiac MRI acquired to evaluate persistent chest discomfort following a viral syndrome. There is patchy, epicardial and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the basal and mid-ventricular inferolateral walls of the left ventricle. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates corresponding focal hyperintensity in the same segments, indicating acute myocardial edema. Biventricular volumes and systolic function are preserved (LVEF 59%).

Impression: Findings of mid-myocardial/epicardial LGE and matching T2-hyperintensity in the inferolateral wall, consistent with acute post-viral myocarditis. Preserved global left ventricular systolic function.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe are herniated into the left thoracic cavity, causing a significant mediastinal shift to the right. The left lung is compressed and severely hypoplastic, and the right lung also shows mildly reduced volumes. Intracranial anatomy is normal, with a ventricular atrial width of 5.5 mm and age-appropriate cortical sulcation.

No other structural abnormalities of the spine, extremities, or gastrointestinal tract are visualized. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with associated pulmonary hypoplasia. Calculated total fetal lung volume is severely reduced, which represents a significant prognostic indicator.

MR of the brain reveals a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass along the left sphenoid wing measuring 2.8 x 2.5 x 2.4 cm. The lesion is homogeneously hyperintense on T2, isointense on T1, and demonstrates avid, uniform enhancement following gadolinium administration, with a prominent dural tail. There is mild adjacent vasogenic edema but no significant midline shift.

Impression: Extra-axial mass along the left sphenoid wing, highly characteristic of a benign meningioma. Mild localized mass effect is noted on the adjacent temporal lobe.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 26 weeks gestation reveals bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys (MCDK). Both kidneys are markedly enlarged and replaced by multiple non-communicating, varying-sized cysts of up to 1.8 cm, with no normal renal parenchyma visible. There is severe oligohydramnios present. The fetal bladder is not visualized, indicating minimal to no urine production. The brain shows normal structural development and ventricles measure 5.8 mm.

Impression: Bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys with associated severe oligohydramnios and non-visualized urinary bladder. Prognosis is extremely poor due to high risk of pulmonary hypoplasia; maternal-fetal medicine counseling is indicated.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates moderate to severe bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.5 mm, and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 12.8 mm. There is mild thinning of the overlying cerebral cortex with a slight delay in the expected parieto-occipital sulcation pattern for 26 weeks. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in caliber. No intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular nodularity, or other parenchymal destructive lesions are visualized.

The corpus callosum is present. The cerebellum and brainstem appear morphologically intact. Impression: Bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly, left greater than right, without other associated structural brain anomalies. Recommend follow-up imaging and postnatal clinical genetics consultation.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a significantly enlarged posterior fossa with elevation of the tentorium and torcular herophili. The cerebellar vermis is severely hypoplastic and rotated upward, communicating with a large retrocerebellar fluid collection. The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with the left atrium measuring 8.5 mm. Sulcation of the cerebral hemispheres is appropriate for 26 weeks.

No other major structural abnormalities are visualized. Impression: Features highly characteristic of Dandy-Walker malformation, characterized by vermian hypoplasia, an enlarged posterior fossa, and torcular elevation.

Brain MRI demonstrates symmetric and completely normal brain parenchyma. There is no focal parenchymal signal abnormality, mass lesion, or abnormal enhancement. Cortical sulci and cerebral ventricles are normal in size and distribution. Visualized cranial nerves are intact within the CPA cisterns.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular lesion is found to explain the patient's complaints.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal left and right ventricular chambers. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 120 mL, and the end-systolic volume is 46 mL, yielding an ejection fraction of 62%. Right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No wall motion abnormalities, regional hypertrophy, or areas of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are identified to suggest scar or fibrosis. Valvular flow dynamics are normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal biventricular size and systolic function with no evidence of myocardial scarring or ischemia.

Brain MRI was performed to evaluate persistent vertigo. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass lesions. The cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, and brainstem show normal signal characteristics and architecture. The vestibulocochlear nerves are normal in course and caliber, with no cerebellopontine angle cistern abnormalities.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No retrocochlear lesion or brainstem pathology identified to account for the patient's vestibular symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced brain development with highly complex and appropriate third-trimester gyration and sulcal patterns. Primary, secondary, and tertiary sulci are well-visualized. The lateral ventricles are completely normal in size, with atrial measurements of 6.0 mm. No intracranial hemorrhage, midline shift, or callosal anomalies are identified.

All fetal visceral organs are completely intact with normal abdominal situs. Impression: Normal third-trimester fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation showing excellent and age-appropriate neurodevelopment.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe enlargement of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) of 210 mL. Diffuse, global hypokinesia is present, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 28%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals a thin, linear band of mid-wall enhancement within the basal and mid-interventricular septum, consistent with a non-ischemic etiology. Mild bilateral pleural effusions are noted.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with marked left ventricular systolic dysfunction and characteristic mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement. Features are compatible with severe congestive heart failure.

Fetal MRI performed at 23 weeks gestation shows severe anhydramnios, limiting optimal fetal positioning. Both renal fossae are empty, and no renal tissue or renal arteries are identified, highly suggestive of bilateral renal agenesis. The fetal urinary bladder is not visualized. The fetal brain appears normal despite the technical limitations; the lateral ventricular atria measure 5.5 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for gestational age.

The fetal thorax is small, and there is concern for secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and suspected pulmonary hypoplasia. Fetal intracranial structures are currently unremarkable.

Multiple punctate and ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions are identified within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, demonstrating a classic Dawson's fingers appearance. Following administration of gadolinium, two of the periventricular lesions show active nodular enhancement.

Impression: Demyelinating disease consistent with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), demonstrating both spatial dissemination and active, enhancing lesions representing temporal dissemination.

Cardiac MRI shows a circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 14 mm adjacent to the right ventricle and 11 mm posterior to the left ventricle. The pericardium appears thickened and displays intense late gadolinium enhancement, indicative of active inflammation. There is no evidence of diastole compression of the right ventricle to suggest clinical tamponade, and ventricular systolic function is preserved.

Impression: Acute pericarditis with a moderate circumferential pericardial effusion and pericardial enhancement. No imaging signs of cardiac tamponade or constrictive physiology.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates extensive trabeculation of the left ventricular apex and lateral wall, with a non-compacted to compacted myocardium ratio of approximately 2.6:1 measured at end-diastole. The left ventricular chamber is mildly dilated, and global systolic function is mildly reduced, with a calculated LVEF of 45%. No distinct focal late gadolinium enhancement is identified.

Impression: Morphological features are highly characteristic of Left Ventricular Non-Compaction (LVNC) cardiomyopathy with associated mild systolic dysfunction.

Fetal MRI performed at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. No normal renal parenchyma or renal artery structures are identified within the bilateral renal fossae or the fetal pelvis. Severe oligohydramnios is present, which significantly limits fetal movement and leads to crowding of the fetal extremities. The fetal bladder is not visualized. The fetal brain structures are normal; the lateral ventricular atrium measures 5.0 mm and sulcation is normal for 23 weeks.

No other structural spinal or cardiac anomalies are identified. Impression: Bilateral fetal renal agenesis with severe oligohydramnios (consistent with Potter sequence). Pediatric nephrology and maternal-fetal medicine counseling is indicated.

MR imaging of the brain was performed utilizing standard multiplanar and multisequence protocols. The brain parenchyma is within normal limits, with no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass, acute ischemia, or hemorrhage. Ventricles and sulci are normal in caliber and configuration for the patient's age.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No acute structural abnormalities or intracranial pathology identified to explain the clinical presentation of chronic headaches.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly, with tear-drop configuration of the lateral ventricles; the posterior horns are dilated while the anterior horns are narrowed. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated, extending into the interhemispheric fissure. Atrial width measures 11.2 mm bilaterally.

The sulcal pattern exhibits radial distribution pointing toward the third ventricle, typical for callosal agenesis. The cerebellum and brainstem structures appear normal. Impression: Complete agenesis of the fetal corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly and borderline ventriculomegaly.

MRI of the brain was obtained following the clinical presentation of a severe atypical migraine. No acute ischemic change, hemorrhage, or mass effect is noted on any sequence. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are unremarkable. Cortical sulcation and white matter tracts show no signal abnormality or pathological change.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular lesion is identified. Normal scan for complex headache/migraine workup.

Cardiac MRI reveals areas of patchy, focal, mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the mid-basal septum and the lateral wall. Associated thickening and increased signal intensity on T2-weighted sequences are noted in these areas, indicating active inflammation. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 48%. Non-contrast chest imaging confirms prominent bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.

Impression: Cardiac MRI findings consistent with active cardiac sarcoidosis. Prominent mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy is also visualized.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals a large left-sided diaphragmatic defect. The fetal stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver have herniated into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the fetal lungs. The measured total fetal lung volume is significantly reduced for gestational age, indicating a high risk of pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain is structurally normal with an atrial measurement of 5.5 mm and normal sulcation for 27 weeks.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with herniation of stomach, bowel, and partial liver, leading to mediastinal shift and severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Brain development is normal.

Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the brain was performed without and with intravenous contrast. There is no evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, mass effect, or abnormal parenchymal enhancement. The ventricular system and sulcal patterns are within normal limits for age. Visualized major intracranial vascular flow voids are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, demyelinating, or vascular etiology is identified to explain the patient's severe migraine headaches.

Cardiac MRI was performed for cardiovascular screening in a 27-year-old competitive female runner presenting with isolated premature ventricular contractions. The study demonstrates entirely normal biventricular size, morphology, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of structural heart disease, myocarditis, or arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy to explain the patient's arrhythmias.

MR imaging reveals a well-defined zone of restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, specifically involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule and adjacent lentiform nucleus. This area is hyperintense on DWI and hypointense on the ADC map, consistent with acute cytotoxic edema. Corresponding FLAIR sequences show early subtle sulcal effacement but no signal change, suggesting hyperacute status.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction in the left deep MCA territory. Rapid neurological evaluation for acute stroke management is indicated.

Brain MRI shows flattening of the posterior sclera bilaterally with protrusion of the optic nerve heads into the vitreous chambers. There is prominence of the CSF space surrounding the optic nerves and an empty sella turcica, with marked thinning/flattening of the pituitary gland against the sellar floor. Transverse venous sinuses show bilateral narrowing.

Impression: Radiographic features suggestive of increased intracranial pressure, consistent with Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri) in this clinical demographic. Suggest ophthalmologic correlation.

Cardiac MRI of a 48-year-old female who presented with acute substernal chest pain and transient ST-segment elevations following an acute emotional stressor. Cine imaging reveals severe hypokinesis to akinesis of the mid and apical segments of the left ventricle, with hyperkinesis of the basal segments, resulting in a characteristic 'apical ballooning' appearance. The overall left ventricular ejection fraction is reduced to 35%. There is no evidence of myocardial scar or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Transient apical ballooning syndrome, highly characteristic of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The absence of late gadolinium enhancement supports the reversible nature of this condition.

Cardiac MRI reveals multifocal, patchy late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) concentrated within the basal-to-mid septal and lateral walls, displaying a predominantly mid-wall and subepicardial distribution. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates corresponding focal areas of high signal intensity, indicative of localized myocardial edema. Mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy is also visualized on the thoracic scout sequences.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of cardiac sarcoidosis with active myocardial inflammation and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Correlation with clinical history and further systemic imaging is recommended.

Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the brain was performed without intravenous contrast due to the patient's active pregnancy status. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity, gray-white matter differentiation, and gyral patterns. There is no evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, mass effect, or extra-axial fluid collections. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable non-contrast MRI of the brain. No acute intracranial pathology, venous sinus thrombosis, or structural abnormalities identified to explain the patient's gestational headaches.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals bilaterally enlarged, hyperintense kidneys, occupying a large portion of the abdominal cavity. The kidneys show a diffuse, fine cystic appearance on high-resolution T2 images. There is severe oligohydramnios present, and the bladder is non-visualized, consistent with renal dysfunction.

Fetal brain imaging shows normal anatomical landmarks for 28 weeks with a ventricular atrium of 5.9 mm and normal early sulcation. Impression: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) with severe oligohydramnios.

MRI of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and morphology. There is no evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, mass effect, or midline shift. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and cortical sulci are unremarkable for the patient's age. Visually inspected cranial nerves and flow voids of the major circle of Willis vessels are intact.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No acute intracranial process, mass, or vascular anomaly is identified to account for the patient's gestational headache symptoms.

Cardiac MRI was performed at 20 weeks gestation in a 33-year-old female with a history of a childhood heart murmur. The heart is structurally normal. Both left and right ventricles show normal size, volumes, and wall thicknesses. Global and regional systolic functions are preserved, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 63% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 57%. Valvular leaflets appear thin and mobile, and no significant regurgitant jets are visualized.

No focal areas of myocardial edema or injury are detected. Impression: Normal maternal cardiac MRI with no structural or functional cardiac abnormalities identified.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a large, irregularly enhancing mass centered in the right temporal lobe, measuring 4.5 x 3.8 cm. The lesion shows thick, nodular peripheral enhancement with central non-enhancing necrosis. Extensive surrounding vasogenic edema is present, causing compression of the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle and 6 mm of left-sided midline shift.

Impression: Aggressive right temporal lobe intra-axial mass with imaging features highly suggestive of high-grade glioma, such as glioblastoma. Neurosurgical consultation is urgently requested.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of both fetal kidneys in the renal fossae. Symmetrical, empty renal fossae are occupied by flat, elongated adrenal glands (lying down sign). There is profound oligohydramnios present, severely limiting the assessment of peripheral fetal structures. The fetal bladder is not visualized.

The fetal lungs are hypoplastic and small for gestational age due to the severe lack of amniotic fluid. The cerebral sulcation and ventricular atrium (6.1 mm) are normal. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence).

Fetal MRI evaluated at 32 weeks gestation reveals excellent anatomical development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit normal, well-defined sulcation patterns and deep parieto-occipital fissures appropriate for 32 weeks. Symmetrical lateral ventricles are noted, measuring 6.4 mm at the atria bilateral. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal in size and signal intensity.

Fetal chest, abdominal situs, and bowel development are unremarkable. No abnormalities are detected. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body development at 32 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral renal anomalies. Both kidneys appear severely enlarged, hyperechoic, and filled with numerous tiny, non-communicating cysts, which is highly suggestive of autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). The bladder is small and empty, and there is profound oligohydramnios present, severely limiting the visualization of peripheral extremities.

Fetal brain structures show symmetric morphology but are compressed; ventricular atrial size measures 6.0 mm. Impression: Bilateral cystic renal dysplasia with severe oligohydramnios, highly suspicious for ARPKD. Pulmonary hypoplasia is likely secondary to oligohydramnios.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced tertiary sulcation and gyral formation appropriate for a late third-trimester fetus. The brain parenchyma shows expected signal characteristics without evidence of ischemic insult or hemorrhage. The bilateral lateral ventricles measure 5.4 mm at the atrium, indicating no ventriculomegaly. The corpus callosum is intact and fully matured.

There is no evidence of diaphragmatic, spinal, or gastrointestinal tract abnormalities. Fetal lie is cephalic, and amniotic fluid is normal. Impression: Normal third-trimester fetal MRI showing well-developed fetal anatomy without any detectable malformations.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced gyral and sulcal development, including well-defined secondary and tertiary sulci appropriate for late third trimester. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with symmetric atria measuring 5.2 mm. The corpus callosum is fully formed, and the brainstem and cerebellum show normal morphologic development.

No facial clefts, thoracic, abdominal, or skeletal anomalies are seen. Normal amniotic fluid and intact placenta. Impression: Unremarkable late third-trimester fetal MRI showing normal brain maturation and normal fetal anatomy.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe dilation of the left ventricle, with an end-diastolic diameter of 6.8 cm and volume index of 145 mL/m2. Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle is observed, with a severely reduced LVEF of 22%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals a faint, linear mid-wall pattern of hyperenhancement in the basal-to-mid ventricular septum, characteristic of a non-ischemic etiology.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction. The linear mid-wall septal late gadolinium enhancement is characteristic of a non-ischemic cardiomyopathy process.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with a history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot who is planning a pregnancy. There is severe pulmonary regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 45%. The right ventricle is severely dilated, with an end-diastolic volume index of 158 mL/m². Right ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced (RVEF 44%). The left ventricle demonstrates normal size and preserved systolic function with an ejection fraction of 57%.

Impression: Status post-surgical repair of Tetralogy of Fallot with severe pulmonary valve regurgitation, marked right ventricular dilation, and mild RV dysfunction. These findings represent a moderate maternal cardiovascular risk profile.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks 6 days gestation demonstrates normal structural development. Cortical folding patterns are appropriate for 30 weeks, including deep, well-developed central and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricles are normal in caliber, with atria measuring 6.3 mm on the left and 6.1 mm on the right. The brainstem, cerebellum, and posterior fossa structures are normal, and the cavum septum pellucidum is present and of normal size.

The fetal thoracic and abdominal organs, including both kidneys, stomach, and liver, are normal in position and signal. The spine is intact, and the long bones show appropriate length. Impression: Completely normal, unremarkable fetal MRI study with normal brain and visceral development.

MRI of the brain reveals a well-defined area of restricted diffusion involving the left insular cortex and frontotemporal operculum, demonstrating bright signal on DWI and corresponding signal dropout on the ADC map. High-resolution T2/FLAIR images demonstrate early sulcal effacement in this region. MR angiogram reveals abrupt occlusion of the M1 segment of the left middle cerebral artery.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction of the left middle cerebral artery territory, associated with acute occlusion of the left M1 segment.

There is marked dilation of the lateral and third ventricles, which is out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. High-convexity and midline sulci are crowded, while the sylvian fissures are disproportionately patulous. A prominent flow void is noted within the cerebral aqueduct on T2-weighted imaging, consistent with hyperdynamic cerebrospinal fluid flow.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to cortical atrophy, presenting a pattern highly consistent with Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH). Recommend correlation with clinical triad.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. In addition, there is a large, well-circumscribed, simple interhemispheric cyst measuring 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.1 cm. This cyst is causing mild mass effect and displacement of the surrounding medial cerebral parenchyma. Colpocephaly is present, with the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles dilated to 12.0 mm. Cortical migration and sulcation are normal for 27 weeks gestation outside the areas of mass effect.

The posterior fossa, spine, and abdominal organs are normal. Impression: Agenesis of the corpus callosum associated with a large interhemispheric cyst and colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates an enlarged posterior fossa with a hypoplastic cerebellar vermis. There is superior rotation of the vermis, and a large cystic collection in the posterior fossa is noted communicating with the fourth ventricle. This is highly characteristic of a Dandy-Walker malformation or its variant. The supratentorial ventricles are mildly prominent, with the lateral ventricles measuring 8.8 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 25 weeks.

The fetal spine is normal, and there are no thoracic or abdominal anomalies. Fluid volumes are normal. Impression: Posterior fossa malformation consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. Recommend fetal neurodevelopmental follow-up.

Brain MRI reveals multiple well-defined oval lesions demonstrating T2/FLAIR hyperintensity oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles (Dawson's fingers). Following administration of gadolinium, a prominent 8mm ring-enhancing lesion is noted in the left periventricular white matter, demonstrating restricted diffusion consistent with active demyelination.

Impression: Demyelinating disease consistent with active Multiple Sclerosis, showing a newly enhancing active plaque in the left periventricular white matter.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a dorsal defect in the lumbosacral spine extending from L4 through S1. There is a protruding fluid-filled sac containing neural placode elements, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Intracranial evaluation reveals features of an Arnold-Chiari II malformation, including effacement of the cisterna magna, caudal displacement of the cerebellar vermis (banana sign), and mild frontal bone scalloping (lemon sign). The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, measuring 10.5 mm.

The remainder of the fetal survey is unremarkable. Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with characteristic Arnold-Chiari II malformation and mild ventriculomegaly. Neurosurgical and maternal-fetal medicine consultations are indicated.

Brain MRI performed postpartum following severe preeclamptic seizure activity. Bilateral, relatively symmetric cortical and subcortical FLAIR hyperintensities are identified within the parieto-occipital regions. These lesions represent vasogenic edema with corresponding normal or increased ADC values; no restricted diffusion is present.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) in the clinical context of postpartum preeclampsia. Clinical monitoring is recommended, as these findings typically resolve with blood pressure control.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks 5 days gestation. The fetal skeletal system exhibits severe diffuse micromelia, with all long bones measuring significantly below the 5th percentile for gestational age. There is marked shortening and bowing of the femora (telephone receiver femur appearance). The thoracic cavity is severely narrowed and bell-shaped, with short ribs, leading to severe pulmonary hypoplasia. The skull shows a mild cloverleaf deformity (kleeblattschädel) with prominent temporal bulging.

The intracranial structures show mild ventriculomegaly (atria measuring 10.5 mm) but are otherwise intact. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, highly characteristic of thanatophoric dysplasia. Associated severe pulmonary hypoplasia is noted.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates herniation of stomach and multiple small bowel loops into the left hemithorax through a posterior defect. The mediastinum is displaced to the right, causing compression of the heart and severe hypoplasia of the left lung. The right lung volume is also slightly reduced but better preserved than the left. Atrial measurements of the fetal brain are within normal limits (6.1 mm).

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant mediastinal shift and severe left-sided pulmonary hypoplasia. Fetal lung volume calculation is detailed in the accompanying sheet.

Sagittal MR sequences demonstrate cerebellar tonsils herniating approximately 7.5 mm below the plane of the foramen magnum. The craniocervical junction shows moderate anatomical crowding. No syrinx formation is visualized within the imaged upper cervical spinal cord on the sagittal sequences.

Impression: Chiari I malformation. No associated syrinx or hydrocephalus identified on current brain MR imaging.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates progressive ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium is dilated, measuring 14.5 mm, while the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.2 mm. There is mild thinning of the posterior corpus callosum, though the overall structure is visualized. The cortical sulcation pattern is appropriate for 26 weeks.

No other intracranial anomalies, hemorrhage, or extra-axial fluid collections are identified. Visualized fetal chest and abdominal organs are unremarkable. Impression: Prominent asymmetric ventriculomegaly, moderate on the left and mild on the right. Clinical follow-up with serial ultrasound is recommended.

Brain and dedicated sellar MR imaging reveals a well-defined, hypoenhancing sellar mass measuring 1.8 x 1.5 x 1.4 cm, causing expansion of the sella turcica. The mass abuts and superiorly displaces the optic chiasm, with mild narrowing of the bilateral cavernous internal carotid arteries but no signs of invasion. The posterior pituitary bright spot is normal.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension causing mild compression of the optic chiasm. Correlation with endocrine panel and visual field testing is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates features consistent with skeletal dysplasia. There is marked shortening and bowing of all long bones, with the femur and humerus lengths falling below the 3rd percentile for gestational age. The fetal chest is small and narrow (bell-shaped thorax), and the ribs appear shortened. The head circumference is relatively large with frontal bossing. Fetal brain maturation shows normal, well-defined gyration and sulcation for 34 weeks, and the lateral ventricular atrium is within normal limits at 6.9 mm.

No internal visceral herniation is present. Polyhydramnios is noted. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with characteristics of thanatophoric dysplasia or achondroplasia. Significant pulmonary hypoplasia risk given the small thoracic volume.

An extra-axial, dural-based mass is noted along the right frontoparietal parasagittal convexity, measuring 3.1 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The lesion is intensely and homogeneously enhancing post-contrast and exhibits a prominent 'dural tail' sign. There is mild remodeling of the overlying inner table of the skull and minimal compression of the adjacent cortex.

Impression: Right parasagittal extra-axial mass, characteristic of a benign meningioma. No invasion of the superior sagittal sinus is seen on current sequences.

MRI of the brain demonstrates marked dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles, out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. High signal intensity on FLAIR is observed along the margins of the lateral ventricles, consistent with transependymal CSF migration. There is also a narrowing of the sulci at the high convexities.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal atrophy, characteristic of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH). Recommend correlation with clinical gait and cognitive testing.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates symmetric, massive enlargement of both kidneys. Both kidneys exhibit a diffusely high T2-weighted signal with innumerable microscopic cystic lesions, consistent with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). The bladder is small, and there is severe oligohydramnios present, precluding optimal lung evaluation.

Cranial anatomy is gross-structurally preserved with an atrial width of 6.2 mm. Impression: Bilateral enlarged polycystic kidneys and severe oligohydramnios, highly suggestive of ARPKD. There is an associated high risk of neonatal pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal dimensions of all four cardiac chambers. The left ventricular myocardium is uniform in thickness, with no localized wall thinning or hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 61% with no regional wall motion defects. Multi-echo sequences demonstrate normal native T1 and T2 relaxation times. No evidence of myocardial infarction or scar is present on late gadolinium enhancement images.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Unremarkable biventricular structure and function with no tissue-level evidence of ischemia or fibrosis.

MR imaging of the brain reveals a large, heterogeneous, ring-enhancing mass centered within the left temporal lobe, measuring 4.5 x 4.2 cm. The lesion exhibits central non-enhancing necrosis, thick irregular peripheral enhancement, and extensive surrounding FLAIR hyperintensity consistent with vasogenic edema. There is moderate mass effect, resulting in 8 mm of rightward midline shift and compression of the left lateral ventricle.

Impression: Aggressive intra-axial left temporal lobe mass with extensive surrounding edema and mass effect, highly suspicious for high-grade glioma (such as glioblastoma). Urgent neurosurgical consult is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation for an ultrasound-reported suspected anomaly. Current MR imaging shows entirely normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal laminar pattern, with expected development of the insula and Sylvian fissure for 24 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, measuring 5.7 mm in the atrium bilaterally. The corpus callosum and brainstem are structurally intact.

The fetal spine is intact, and the fetal chest and abdomen show normal, age-appropriate organogenesis. The kidneys and urinary bladder are normal in appearance and position. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with no structural abnormalities identified at 24 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI was performed for familial screening in a 33-year-old female who is a known carrier of a genetic mutation associated with dilated cardiomyopathy. The imaging reveals entirely normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions. Global biventricular systolic function is well-preserved, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 62%. No late gadolinium enhancement or areas of myocardial fibrosis are demonstrated.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI. Currently, there is no phenotypic evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy or myocardial fibrosis. Continued clinical surveillance is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral hydronephrosis with massive dilation of both renal pelvises and proximal ureters. The bladder is profoundly distended and shows thick wall trabeculation with a dilated posterior urethra, forming a classic 'keyhole' sign. There is severe oligohydramnios present. The fetal brain shows normal, age-appropriate cortical sulcation with a ventricular atrial width of 5.2 mm.

No other intracranial or skeletal abnormalities are identified. Impression: Severe bilateral hydronephrosis and megacystis with a keyhole sign, highly suggestive of posterior urethral valves (PUV) and associated oligohydramnios.

Brain MRI performed for workup of optic neuritis. No areas of abnormal signal or demyelinating plaques are seen in the periventricular, juxtacortical, or infratentorial regions. Visualized optic nerves show symmetric caliber and normal signal on fat-suppressed contrast-enhanced sequences.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No evidence of demyelinating disease or acute structural brain pathology.

MR imaging of the brain shows a well-defined area of restricted diffusion within the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, involving the right insular cortex and frontoparietal region. This area demonstrates high DWI signal and corresponding low ADC values, consistent with acute ischemic injury. Mild sulcal effacement is noted over the right hemisphere.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction of the right middle cerebral artery territory. No hemorrhagic transformation is observed on susceptibility-weighted imaging.

Cardiac MRI evaluated a 38-year-old female with chronic mitral regurgitation. There is significant bileaflet mitral valve prolapse, most pronounced in the posterior leaflet (P2 segment), demonstrating a 4 mm displacement into the left atrium during systole. Phase-contrast flow analysis demonstrates a severe mitral regurgitant volume of 52 mL and a regurgitant fraction of 44%. The left ventricle is dilated (LVEDV 165 mL/m²), reflecting volume overload, with preserved global systolic function (LVEF 60%).

Impression: Severe mitral valve prolapse with severe mitral regurgitation and secondary left ventricular dilation. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 7.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. There is crowding of the craniocervical junction. The remainder of the brain parenchyma, ventricular system, and vascular structures are unremarkable. Visualized sagittal spine views demonstrate no evidence of a cervical syrinx.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with cerebellar tonsillar herniation measuring 7.5 mm. No associated cervical syringomyelia or obstructive hydrocephalus is identified.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows early primary sulcation patterns, including the sylvian fissure and parieto-occipital sulcus, completely appropriate for 24 weeks. The ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 5.4 mm on the left and 5.5 mm on the right. The cerebellum, pons, and brainstem appear completely normal in structure and signal.

The chest demonstrates normal lung volumes and a centrally positioned heart. Abdominal organs, kidneys, and extremities are structurally unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing expected intracranial development and normal thoracic/abdominal structures.

A multiplanar, multisequence cardiac MRI was completed. Left ventricular chambers are within normal size limits with normal systolic wall thickening. The left ventricular ejection fraction is computed at 60%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or delayed hyperenhancement areas are seen. Valves are structurally thin and mobile with no significant stenosis or regurgitation.

Impression: Structurally normal heart with normal biventricular size and function. No MRI evidence of myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, or ischemic injury.

Brain MRI performed for transient dizziness in a patient currently at 20 weeks gestation. No abnormal intracranial signal intensity is seen within the brain parenchyma. The ventricles, sulci, and extra-axial spaces are normal. The major intracranial flow voids are preserved, and there is no evidence of acute ischemia, mass lesion, or hemorrhage.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no acute intracranial pathology or structural abnormalities detected to explain the patient's symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks 4 days gestation reveals severe enlargement of the posterior fossa. The cerebellar vermis is hypoplastic and elevated, associated with a large posterior fossa fluid collection communicating with a dilated fourth ventricle. The torcula and transverse sinuses are superiorly displaced. Bilateral lateral ventricles are prominent, measuring 11.2 mm at the atria.

The remaining fetal intracranial and extracranial structures appear within normal limits. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation. Pediatric neurology and neurosurgery counseling is advised.

MR brain with and without contrast, including MR venogram, performed for evaluation of postpartum headache and papilledema. There is an absence of the normal flow void within the superior sagittal sinus and the left transverse sinus. T1 and T2 weighted sequences demonstrate hyperintense thrombus within these venous structures. There is no associated venous infarction or intraparenchymal hemorrhage.

Impression: Extensive dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal sinus and left transverse sinus. No secondary venous congestion, edema, or hemorrhage is currently observed.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation shows cerebellar vermian hypoplasia with mild enlargement of the cisterna magna, pointing to Dandy-Walker variant. The supratentorial anatomy is preserved; the ventricular atria are normal and measure 7.0 mm. Normal early cerebral sulcation and normal brainstem morphometry are seen.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant at 22 weeks gestation. Supratentorial brain structures are otherwise unremarkable.

Brain MRI reveals disproportionate ventriculomegaly affecting the lateral and third ventricles, without corresponding enlargement of the cerebral cortical sulci (DESH pattern: disproportionate enlarged subarachnoid space hydrocephalus). Flow-sensitive sequences demonstrate a prominent CSF flow void through the aqueduct of Sylvius.

Impression: Structural features suggestive of Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH). Recommend correlation with clinical triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence.

Cardiac MRI shows a moderately dilated left ventricle with regional wall motion abnormalities, characterized by severe hypokinesis of the anterior wall, septum, and apex. Evaluation for viability demonstrates near-transmural late gadolinium enhancement (approximately 75-80% wall thickness) in the mid to apical anterior and anteroseptal walls, consistent with a prior myocardial infarction in the left anterior descending artery distribution.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with non-viable myocardium in the anterior and anteroseptal territories. Overall left ventricular ejection fraction is depressed at 38%.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates asymmetric dilation of the lateral ventricles. The right lateral ventricular atrium is dilated, measuring 13.5 mm, consistent with moderate ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 7.8 mm, which is within the normal limits. The cerebral cortex shows normal sulcation patterns corresponding to 26 weeks, and there is no evidence of periventricular nodular heterotopia or porencephaly. The corpus callosum is present and demonstrates normal thickness throughout.

Impression: Moderate isolated right-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. No other intracranial anomalies or midline defects visualized.

Cardiac MRI reveals asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 21 mm in the mid-ventricular segment. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve causing dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, with a peak resting gradient of 35 mmHg on phase-contrast sequences. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy, mid-myocardial fibrosis at the right ventricular insertion points. Left ventricular systolic function is hyperdynamic with an LVEF of 72%.
