The brain shows normal lateral ventricles (atrial diameter 6.8 mm) and normal sulcation for 30 weeks.

No other structural abnormalities of the brain or spine are detected. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia, with phenotypic features highly suggestive of heterozygous achondroplasia.

Non-contrast MRI of the brain shows acute hyperintense subarachnoid blood within the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and anterior interhemispheric fissure. Dedicated MR angiography (MRA) of the circle of Willis demonstrates a 6 mm lobulated aneurysm arising from the anterior communicating artery (ACoA).

Impression: Acute aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage secondary to rupture of an anterior communicating artery berry aneurysm. Immediate neurosurgical or endovascular intervention is required.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks 6 days gestation demonstrates normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex is appropriately smooth with very early primary sulcation/sylvian fissure indentation, perfectly normal for early second-trimester development. The lateral ventricular system is symmetric and measures 5.1 mm at the level of the atrium. The corpus callosum and cerebellar structures are well-visualized and anatomically correct.

The spine is intact, and fetal chest and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating completely normal fetal anatomy and appropriate early brain development.

Maternal cardiac MRI was performed at 28 weeks gestation to evaluate persistent palpitations and atypical chest pain. Cine imaging demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions without hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 60%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 55%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities or evidence of late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scarring or fibrosis.

Impression: Completely normal maternal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or myocardial injury to account for the patient's palpitations.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates severe, bilateral renal abnormalities. The left kidney is markedly enlarged and shows multiple large cortical cysts, typical of multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The right kidney is hypoplastic and shows increased signal on T2-weighted imaging, consistent with severe dysplastic change. Oligohydramnios is severe, resulting in marked uterine crowding.

The fetal brain shows mature third-trimester sulcal patterns, and the ventricular atrium measures 7.1 mm. Impression: Severe bilateral renal dysplasia (left MCDK, right renal hypoplasia) with profound oligohydramnios and associated risk of pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI displays severe, diffuse dilatation of both the left and right ventricles. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 224 mL/m2, and global left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with an ejection fraction of 28%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows a linear band of mid-wall enhancement along the basal-to-mid ventricular septum, characteristic of a non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy process.

Impression: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) characterized by severe biventricular enlargement, profound systolic dysfunction, and mid-wall septal fibrosis.

Brain MRI with MR venography (MRV) reveals an absence of normal flow void and persistent filling defects within the superior sagittal sinus and right transverse sinus, compatible with acute dural venous sinus thrombosis. Secondary small, non-hemorrhagic venous infarctions with mild vasogenic edema are noted in the bilateral paramedian parietal cortex.

Impression: Superior sagittal sinus and right transverse sinus thrombosis with associated small, non-hemorrhagic venous infarctions in the bilateral parietal lobes. Urgent neurological management is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates findings highly suggestive of skeletal dysplasia. There is severe rhizomelic shortening of the bilateral femurs and humeri, with mild bowing of the long bones. The fetal thorax is narrow and bell-shaped, with significantly shortened ribs. Intracranial structures demonstrate normal morphology. The lateral ventricular atrium measures 7.2 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 30 weeks gestation, with well-defined central and cingulate sulci.

The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal. Spine alignment is intact. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe rhizomelic limb shortening and a narrow, bell-shaped thorax. Normal intracranial structures.

Cardiac MRI reveals marked, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, with a uniform maximal diastolic wall thickness of 16 mm. This is associated with severe degenerative stenosis and calcification of the aortic valve, characterized by a severely restricted systolic leaflet excursion. The calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 55% with a hyperdynamic baseline contraction.

Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is normal. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows mid-wall patch-like hyperenhancement in the mid-septum, consistent with pressure-overload induced interstitial fibrosis. Impression: Severe calcific aortic stenosis with adaptive moderate-to-severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy and associated focal myocardial fibrosis.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation shows normal intracranial development. The brain demonstrates symmetric cerebral hemispheres, and early primary sulcation is developing along the medial hemispheric walls as expected. The lateral ventricles are completely normal in size, with both atria measuring 5.9 mm. Midline structures, including the corpus callosum and optochiasmatic region, are fully intact.

The chest, abdomen, and spine are normal without structural defects. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study showing completely normal anatomy and age-appropriate brain development at 25 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI of a 24-year-old female evaluated for non-specific chest wall pain and dynamic T-wave changes on ECG. Multiplanar, multisequence cine and tissue characterization imaging demonstrate normal cardiac chambers with appropriate myocardial thicknesses. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of regional hypokinesis, myocardial edema, or abnormal late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or tissue characterization abnormalities are identified.

MRI of the brain demonstrates ventriculomegaly involving the lateral and third ventricles that is disproportionate to the degree of cerebral sulcal atrophy. There is narrowing of the sulci at the high frontoparietal convexities and enlargement of the sylvian fissures. No focal obstructive lesion of the ventricular system is identified.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal enlargement, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence is recommended.

Cardiac MRI of the maternal heart performed as baseline surveillance due to a family history of congenital cardiac issues. Assessment demonstrates normal left ventricular (LVEF 60%) and right ventricular (RVEF 57%) systolic parameters. All four cardiac chambers are normal in volume, and there is no evidence of intra-atrial or intra-ventricular shunts.

Impression: Unremarkable maternal cardiac MRI. No congenital or acquired structural heart abnormalities visualized.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe dilatation of the left atrium, with a calculated volume index of 62 mL/m2. There is dynamic prolapse of the posterior leaflet (P2 segment) of the mitral valve into the left atrium during systole. Phase-contrast velocity mapping demonstrates a significant mitral regurgitant jet, with a regurgitant fraction calculated at 48%. The left ventricle is mildly dilated but retains a normal ejection fraction of 61%.

Impression: Myxomatous mitral valve disease with severe mitral regurgitation, posterior leaflet prolapse, and associated left atrial dilation. Ventricular systolic function remains preserved.

Cardiac MRI evaluated for suspected multi-system disease. Multiple nodular areas of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are identified within the basal septum, anterior, and lateral walls of the left ventricle in a non-coronary distribution. T2 map sequences and STIR imaging reveal focal areas of active edema. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced, with an ejection fraction of 47%.

Impression: Patchy, non-ischemic mid-myocardial LGE with active myocardial inflammation, highly suggestive of cardiac sarcoidosis. Mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction is present.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal ventricular size and configuration. The cerebral and cerebellar sulci, cisterns, and major dural venous sinuses are within normal limits. There is no evidence of restricted diffusion, intracranial hemorrhage, extra-axial collections, or abnormal parenchymal enhancement. Visualized orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid cells are clear.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain. No focal intracranial lesion, vascular compromise, or acute pathologic process identified to account for the patient's tension headaches.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 33-year-old female at 3 months postpartum following severe gestational preeclampsia. The study reveals a normal-sized left ventricular cavity with normal systolic function and a calculated ejection fraction of 63%. There is no regional wall motion abnormality. The right ventricular size, geometry, and function are likewise normal (EF 58%).

T2-weighted sequences show no evidence of edema, and late gadolinium enhancement sequences show no focal or diffuse myocardial scar. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with well-preserved biventricular function and no signs of gestational or postpartum cardiomyopathy or hypertensive-induced focal myocardial damage.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a midline defect in the occipital bone, through which a large, CSF-filled sac herniates. This occipital encephalocele measures 2.4 x 2.1 x 1.8 cm and contains a small amount of dysplastic cerebellar tissue. There is secondary distortion of the posterior fossa structures, with elongation of the fourth ventricle. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with the left atrium measuring 12.2 mm and the right measuring 11.9 mm. Cerebral sulcation is otherwise appropriate for 23 weeks.

The spine, thoracic, and abdominal cavities are normal. Impression: Occipital encephalocele containing herniated meninges and minor cerebellar tissue, with associated ventriculomegaly. High risk of neurodevelopmental delays; recommend neurosurgical consultation.

MR venography and brain imaging demonstrate a filling defect within the superior sagittal sinus and left transverse sinus, consistent with acute dural venous sinus thrombosis. There is associated venous congestion and a small area of non-hemorrhagic venous infarction in the left parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Acute dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal and left transverse sinuses with a small left parietal venous infarct. This is a critical finding, particularly in this postpartum patient; clinical correlation and immediate anticoagulation therapy are recommended.

Cardiac MRI shows a markedly dilated left ventricular cavity with an end-diastolic volume index of 142 mL/m2. Left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 22% with diffuse hypokinesis. There is no evidence of subendocardial or transmural late gadolinium enhancement, arguing strongly against an ischemic etiology. Diffuse mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the basoseptal region.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. Mild functional mitral regurgitation is present, secondary to annular dilation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates areas of subepicardial and mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement involving the basal to mid-lateral and inferolateral left ventricular walls. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates corresponding hyperintensity in these same regions, indicative of active myocardial edema. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 50%, with localized hypokinesis of the lateral wall segments. The right ventricle is normal in size and function.

Impression: Findings satisfy the Lake Louise criteria for acute myocarditis, demonstrating myocardial injury, edema, and localized systolic dysfunction. Correlation with clinical markers and serial imaging is recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates mild generalized cortical volume loss and ventricular prominence, appropriate for the patient's age. No acute territorial infarction, hemorrhage, or mass is identified. There is no evidence of parkinsonian-related brainstem atrophy, and the neuromelanin-sensitive sequences show preserved signal in the substantia nigra. Chronically stable microvascular white matter changes are present.

Impression: Age-appropriate brain MRI. No acute intracranial findings or structural correlates for clinically suspected parkinsonian syndrome.

Fetal MRI performed at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a large defect in the left hemidiaphragm. The stomach, loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver have herniated into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe mediastinal shift to the right and marked compression of the fetal lungs. The calculated total lung volume is severely reduced, measuring below the 5th percentile for 34 weeks.

The fetal brain shows normal age-appropriate tertiary sulcation and symmetrical lateral ventricles measuring 5.2 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with significant intrathoracic herniation of the stomach and liver, leading to severe mass effect and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI performed as part of a pre-IVF evaluation due to a family history of early myocardial infarction and cardiomyopathy. The study demonstrates completely normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions and wall thicknesses. Calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of focal myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocardial scar, or active inflammatory process. This is a reassuring baseline prior to initiating fertility treatments.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a regional wall motion abnormality consisting of severe hypokinesis to akinesis of the basal and mid inferior myocardial walls. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows a subendocardial scar in these segments involving approximately 40% of the wall thickness, consistent with a prior ischemic event in the right coronary artery (RCA) territory. LVEF is calculated at 48%.

Impression: Subendocardial myocardial infarction of the basal-to-mid inferior wall with partial viability remaining. Mild global left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI shows marked ballooning of the left ventricular apex with severe regional hypokinesis to akinesis of the apical and mid-ventricular segments. Conversely, there is hyperkinesis of the basal segments. This results in a severely reduced global left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%. There is no evidence of myocardial late gadolinium enhancement, which rule out acute myocardial infarction.

Impression: Classic regional wall motion pattern of stress-induced (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy. No viable myocardial scar tissue is identified.

Cardiac MRI performed for workup of high-burden premature ventricular contractions (PVCs). Left and right ventricular chamber dimensions, volume indexes, and wall thicknesses are completely normal. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal fatty infiltration are noted on black-blood sequences, and late gadolinium enhancement is negative.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with no structural substrate, scarring, or arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy findings identified to explain the PVC burden.

Cardiac MRI shows severe, generalized ventricular dilation with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 145 mL/m2. Global left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with an calculated LVEF of 22%. Minimal, non-specific mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the basal interventricular septum, suggesting non-ischemic etiology.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. Right ventricular systolic function is also mildly reduced with an RVEF of 41%.

Cardiac MRI performed in a postpartum female presenting with progressive dyspnea 3 weeks after delivery. Evaluation of the ventricles reveals marked left ventricular dilation and severe global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) is increased at 112 mL/m2. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 28%. No focal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed to suggest myocardial infarction or active scar, though mild diffuse interstitial fibrosis cannot be excluded.

Impression: Clinical and imaging findings are highly consistent with peripartum cardiomyopathy. There is severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction (EF 28%) and chamber dilation without evidence of ischemic scar.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe is visualized within the left hemithorax. This results in severe mass effect with a rightward mediastinal shift and severe compression of the left lung tissue. Calculated total fetal lung volume is reduced at 14.2 mL.

Intracranial structures are normal with an atrial width of 6.2 mm and normal cerebral sulcation. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation ('liver-up') and associated pulmonary hypoplasia. Maternal-fetal medicine consultation is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The liver and gallbladder are herniated into the right thoracic cavity, resulting in a leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart. The left lung volume is significantly compressed and the total lung-to-head ratio is reduced. Intracranial structures are normal with a lateral ventricle atrium of 5.8 mm.

Cerebral sulcation and cortical migration are normal for 28 weeks. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and associated pulmonary hypoplasia.

MRI of the brain demonstrates multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Several of these lesions involve the corpus callosum and the juxtacortical white matter. Following gadolinium administration, two active lesions in the right parietal lobe show rim-like enhancement.

Impression: Demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, demonstrating dissemination in space and time, consistent with multiple sclerosis. Active enhancing lesions are present.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced gyral development for gestational age, featuring prominent central and precentral sulci. Both lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the right atrium measuring 5.8 mm and the left atrium measuring 6.0 mm. The corpus callosum is fully developed and normal in length and thickness.

Fetal thoracic, abdominal, and spinal structures are normal. No extra-axial fluid collections are identified. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrating normal, age-appropriate cortical sulcation and brain biometry.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomical development. The cerebral structures, including the developing cortex and deep grey nuclei, are normal in morphology. The lateral ventricles are thin and symmetric, with the atria measuring 4.8 mm. The cisterna magna and posterior fossa structures are normal, and the spine is intact with no overlying subcutaneous defects. Normal fetal situs is confirmed.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation, demonstrating normal neuroanatomy and normal systemic structural development.

Cardiac MRI reveals a dilated left ventricle with subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the mid-to-apical anterior and anteroseptal walls, encompassing approximately 50-75% of the wall thickness. There is associated severe hypokinesis to akinesis in this coronary distribution. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is increased, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 38%.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with subendocardial myocardial infarction in the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery territory. Mild to moderate residual viability in the affected segments.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomical development of the fetal brain. Visualized sulcation patterns and cortical plate development are highly advanced and entirely appropriate for 32 weeks, showing well-developed parieto-occipital and calcarine sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely within normal limits, with the atrium measuring 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum is well-defined, and the cavum septum pellucidum is present. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and cisterna magna, are normal.

The fetal chest, abdomen, and spine are evaluated and demonstrate no structural anomalies. Amniotic fluid volume is subjectively normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 32 weeks gestation, with no intracranial or spinal pathology identified.

MRI and MR venography of the brain demonstrates an absence of normal flow void within the superior sagittal sinus and the dominant right transverse sinus. T1 and T2 sequences show an abnormal hyperintense clot within these venous sinuses, associated with a focal zone of venous infarction and localized edema in the right parietal cortex, containing tiny petechial hemorrhages.

Impression: Superior sagittal sinus and right transverse sinus dural venous thrombosis, associated with a non-hemorrhagic right parietal venous infarction. Prompt anticoagulation is clinically suggested.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates bilateral, relatively symmetric areas of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity involving the subcortical white matter and cortex of the parieto-occipital lobes. No evidence of acute infarction on diffusion-weighted imaging. These findings are highly characteristic of vasogenic edema.

Impression: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES), commonly associated with preeclampsia/eclampsia in this clinical context. Close clinical correlation and blood pressure monitoring is recommended.

Brain MRI utilizing a dedicated internal auditory canal (IAC) protocol demonstrates normal facial and vestibulocochlear nerve complexes bilaterally. There is no evidence of cerebellopontine angle masses or vestibular schwannomas. The cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, and brainstem are structurally normal, with no acute ischemia or hemorrhage.

Impression: Completely normal brain and IAC MRI. No structural or vestibulocochlear pathway abnormality to account for the patient's symptoms of episodic dizziness.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates marked shortening of all long bones, particularly the femurs and humeri, consistent with rhizomelic micromelia. The thorax is narrow and bell-shaped with shortened ribs, raising concern for pulmonary hypoplasia. Brain development is structurally normal, with age-appropriate sulcation and atrial measurements of 5.9 mm.

Impression: Skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe rhizomelic micromelia and a narrow thorax.

Cardiovascular MRI demonstrates normal biventricular dimensions and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of focal myocardial hypertrophy. T2-weighted mapping shows no signs of active myocardial edema, and late gadolinium enhancement imaging is completely negative for fibrosis or scarring.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI demonstrating normal chamber volumes and preserved biventricular systolic function. No evidence of myocardial scar, inflammation, or peripartum pathology.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left ventricular chamber dimensions with a mildly reduced ejection fraction of 51%. T2-weighted mapping shows increased T2 relaxation times in the lateral and epicardial regions of the left ventricular wall, indicating active myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging confirms patchy, non-ischemic, subepicardial hyperenhancement involving the basal-to-mid lateral wall.

Impression: Acute myocarditis characterized by active myocardial edema and subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement in a non-coronary distribution. Follow-up is recommended to assess resolution of inflammation.

Cardiac MRI performed for familial screening of dilated cardiomyopathy. The study demonstrates completely normal left and right ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and geometry. The calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%, without regional wall motion abnormalities. No focal myocardial fibrosis or edema is seen on late gadolinium enhancement or T1/T2 mapping sequences.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal cardiac structure and function, with no phenotypic expression of cardiomyopathy in this patient.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 23 weeks gestation shows complete bilateral renal agenesis. No renal tissue or renal arteries are identified in either renal fossa or within the pelvis. This is associated with severe anhydrous conditions (absence of amniotic fluid), causing severe crowding of fetal parts. The fetal lungs are extremely hypoplastic, with volumes significantly below the expected range.

No gross intracranial lesions are observed, and ventricular size is normal (5.1 mm). Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis accompanied by severe anhydramnios and severe pulmonary hypoplasia. This is a highly lethal condition, and family counseling is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates robust structural development. The sulcation is mature, showing deep and well-defined central, precentral, and postcentral sulci, entirely appropriate for a 35-week fetus. The lateral ventricles measure 5.8 mm, with no asymmetry or expansion. The posterior fossa, including cerebellar hemispheres and brainstem, is normal.

Fetal chest, abdominal visceral organs, and spinal tract are completely within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating mature, age-appropriate brain development and normal systemic anatomy at 35 weeks.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles show colpocephaly with dilated posterior horns measuring 12.8 mm. The normal configuration of the cingulate gyrus is absent, and the sulci show a radial pattern pointing toward the third ventricle, which is elevated. The cavum septi pellucidi is not visualized.

The remainder of the fetal brain parenchyma and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Gyration matches 26-week gestational parameters. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI reveals massive, bi-atrial and bi-ventricular dilation, with the left ventricular end-diastolic volume measuring 230 mL/m². The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely depressed at 28%, demonstrating diffuse, global hypokinesis. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume is also elevated, with a reduced right ventricular ejection fraction of 31%.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows mid-wall linear hyperenhancement in the mid-ventricular septum, characteristic of a non-ischemic dilated etiology. No subendocardial infarctions are noted. Impression: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with severe biventricular systolic dysfunction and mid-wall septal fibrosis.

Fetal MRI performed at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The normal midline callosal structure is not visualized on sagittal or coronal sequences. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated. Colpocephaly is present, with dilation of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles; the ventricular atrium measures 12.1 mm. The cortical sulcation pattern is abnormal, showing radial arrangement of the gyri surrounding the elevated third ventricle, typical for this pathology.

The cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, and brainstem appear normal. Spine and facial structures are intact. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly and characteristic radial sulcation pattern. Neurosurgical and genetic counseling are recommended.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain performed for postpartum vision changes demonstrates no structural abnormalities. The cerebral cortex, deep gray nuclei, and white matter are normal in appearance. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and subarachnoid spaces are normal. The optic nerves and chiasm are normal in caliber and signal.

Impression: Unremarkable postpartum brain MRI. No evidence of cortical venous thrombosis, demyelinating disease, or intracranial mass.

Brain MRI demonstrates normal ventricular size and sulcal pattern without evidence of mass effect, midline shift, or abnormal extra-axial fluid collections. There are no areas of restricted diffusion to suggest acute ischemia, and no foci of susceptibility artifact to indicate hemorrhage. Visualized dural venous sinuses demonstrate normal flow voids.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No acute intracranial pathology, major vessel occlusion, or venous sinus thrombosis is identified.

Adult patient with a history of surgically repaired Tetralogy of Fallot presenting for surveillance MRI. The right ventricle is severely dilated, with an end-diastolic volume index of 158 mL/m2. Phase-contrast flow assessment over the main pulmonary artery demonstrates severe, free pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 46%. There is dyskinesia of the RV outflow tract patch and mild global right ventricular systolic dysfunction (RVEF 38%).

The left ventricle is normal in size and demonstrates preserved global systolic function with a LVEF of 58%. No significant residual ventricular septal defects are identified. Impression: Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot with severe pulmonary valve regurgitation, severe RV dilation, and mild RV systolic dysfunction. Findings meet clinical criteria for considering pulmonary valve replacement.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals signs of Chiari II malformation. There is herniation of the cerebellar tonsils below the level of the foramen magnum and a banana-shaped cerebellum. An open spinal dysraphism is noted in the lumbosacral region with a distinct placode-sac. Bilateral lateral ventriculomegaly is noted with an average atrial width of 11.5 mm.

Impression: Findings of a lumbar myelomeningocele with secondary Chiari II malformation. Cortical sulcation and remaining visceral anatomy are otherwise within normal limits.

Fetal MRI performed at 20 weeks gestation. The primary cerebral fissures (lateral and parieto-occipital) are beginning to form, which is completely appropriate for this early gestational age. The lateral ventricles are prominent, as is normal for 20 weeks, but measure within normal limits with an atrial width of 6.0 mm. No midline shift or asymmetric dilation is seen.

The brainstem, cerebellum, and posterior fossa are clear of abnormalities. Visualized fetal organs including lungs, kidneys, and liver appear structurally intact. Impression: Normal early second-trimester fetal MRI study with appropriate intracranial development.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 30-year-old female 6 weeks postpartum presenting with acute onset heart failure. The left ventricle is moderately dilated (LVEDVI 102 mL/m2) with severe global hypokinesis; the calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is significantly reduced at 30%. The right ventricle is at the upper limit of normal in size with mild hypokinesis and an ejection fraction of 45%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows a patchy mid-wall enhancement pattern in the mid-anteroseptal segment, consistent with non-ischemic injury.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of peripartum cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular dysfunction and associated non-ischemic myocardial fibrosis. Close clinical management and follow-up imaging are indicated.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks 4 days gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and extracranial development. The brain exhibits age-appropriate sulcation with a clearly defined Sylvian fissure and early parieto-occipital sulcus. The cerebral ventricles are normal in caliber, with the atrium of the left lateral ventricle measuring 5.8 mm and the right measuring 5.6 mm. The cavum septum pellucidum is identified and normal. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis, are intact, and the cisterna magna is normal at 6.1 mm.

The fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and limbs are normal in appearance, with age-appropriate biometry. The placenta is anterior and well-positioned relative to the cervix, and the amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing expected anatomical development for 22 weeks gestation, without demonstrable intracranial or extracranial anomalies.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked bi-ventricular dilation with severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction, yielding an ejection fraction (LVEF) of 32%. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is elevated at 180 mL/m2. There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no areas of focal myocardial replacement fibrosis or scar.

Impression: Clinical picture and imaging characteristics are highly consistent with peripartum cardiomyopathy. Close outpatient cardiology follow-up is recommended to monitor left ventricular function and guide medical therapy.

MRI of the brain shows a large, heterogeneous, ring-enhancing mass centered within the right temporal lobe, measuring approximately 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. The lesion is surrounded by an extensive zone of vasogenic edema causing compression of the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle and 6 mm of leftward midline shift. Central necrosis is noted within the mass.

Impression: Aggressive, ring-enhancing right temporal lobe mass, highly suspicious for glioblastoma multiforme. Neurosurgical consultation and MR spectroscopy are recommended.

Dedicated thin-section sagittal and coronal MR imaging of the sella turcica demonstrates a small, hypoenhancing lesion in the left lateral wing of the anterior pituitary gland measuring approximately 4.5 mm. There is no evidence of suprasellar extension, optic chiasm compression, or invasion of the cavernous sinuses. The pituitary stalk is midline.

Impression: Left-sided pituitary microadenoma, measuring 4.5 mm, demonstrating characteristic delayed enhancement. This finding correlates clinically with the patient's history of hyperprolactinemia and secondary amenorrhea.

MRI and MR venography of the brain show a lack of flow void and a hyperintense T1/T2 signal within the superior sagittal sinus and the left transverse sinus, consistent with acute thrombosis. There is mild associated localized cortical edema in the left parietal lobe, but no frank hemorrhagic venous infarction is observed.

Impression: Extensive dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal and left transverse sinuses. This finding in a postpartum female warrant urgent anticoagulation therapy and hematology consultation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 37-year-old female with an echocardiographically suspected atrial septal defect. Velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging and anatomical sequences demonstrate a large, 2.1 cm ostium secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) with a significant left-to-right shunt. The calculated pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp:Qs) is 1.8:1. Marked right ventricular dilatation is present with an end-diastolic volume index of 118 mL/m2, though right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is preserved at 53%.

Impression: Large ostium secundum atrial septal defect resulting in a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and consequent right-sided chamber enlargement. No pulmonary hypertension or irreversible ventricular failure is identified on the current examination.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 29-year-old female presenting 4 weeks postpartum with progressive dyspnea. The left ventricle is moderately dilated (LVEDV 185 mL/m²) with diffuse global hypokinesis. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is severely reduced at 28%. No focal myocardial scar or late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed. The right ventricle is normal in size with preserved systolic function (RVEF 52%). There is a small, hemodynamically insignificant pericardial effusion.

Impression: Severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction and dilation in the postpartum period, characteristic of peripartum cardiomyopathy. No evidence of myocardial infarction or myocarditis on tissue characterization sequences.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderate circumferential pericardial effusion, which measures up to 14 mm in diastole posterior to the left ventricle. The pericardium itself is thickened and demonstrates intense late enhancement, measuring 4 mm, consistent with active inflammation. There is no evidence of diastolic collapse of the right atrium or ventricle to suggest tamponade.

Ventricular volumes and contractility are normal, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 61% and no regional wall motion abnormalities. Impression: Findings are consistent with acute pericarditis and associated moderate-sized circumferential pericardial effusion. No signs of cardiac tamponade on the current study.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates mild, borderline ventriculomegaly of the lateral ventricles. The left atrial width measures 10.5 mm and the right measures 9.8 mm. Cortical sulcation is within normal limits, showing expected opercular development and parieto-occipital sulcation for 27 weeks. The corpus callosum is present and normal in length.

Posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are within normal parameters. Impression: Mild, borderline left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Otherwise normal fetal brain development for 27 weeks gestation; follow-up ultrasound is suggested.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals bilateral fetal hydronephrosis. The renal pelvis on the left is dilated to 14 mm and on the right to 12 mm. There is mild thinning of the renal cortex, but the parenchyma is otherwise homogeneous. The ureters are not significantly dilated, and the urinary bladder is well-visualized and normal in size. Intracranial structures demonstrate normal morphology. The lateral ventricular atrium measures 6.2 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 33 weeks.

The chest, spine, and limbs show no abnormalities. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal hydronephrosis with preserved renal cortex. Intracranial structures are completely normal for gestational age.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates a single, large, central monoventricle in the brain, with fused thalami and absent midline structures including the septum pellucidum, corpus callosum, and interhemispheric fissure. There is severe ventriculomegaly with the single ventricle measuring 24 mm. Sulcation is highly aberrant and delayed for 31 weeks gestation.

Fetal facial structures were difficult to assess but suggest midface hypoplasia. The remainder of the fetal torso is normal. Impression: Semilobar holoprosencephaly with severe monoventriculomegaly, fused thalami, and delayed, abnormal cortical migration.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal ventricular size and configuration. The cerebral and cerebellar sulci and cisterns are within normal limits. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass, acute territorial infarction, or hemorrhage. The internal acoustic canals are symmetric, and the vestibulocochlear nerves are normal in appearance.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural abnormality, cerebellopontine angle mass, or acute ischemic change is present to explain the patient's complaints of vertigo.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a large occipital encephalocele. A midline bony defect in the occipital bone is identified, through which there is herniation of meninges and a small portion of dysplastic cerebellar tissue into a CSF-filled sac. Microcephaly is present, and there is distortion of the brainstem and posterior fossa anatomy. The supratentorial brain shows mildly dilated ventricles (atrium 10.2 mm).

The fetal spine is otherwise intact, and no other anomalies are detected. Impression: Occipital encephalocele with herniated dural and cerebellar elements, associated with secondary microcephaly and mild ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI performed on a 41-year-old female with a known history of systemic sarcoidosis, presenting with new-onset heart block. The left ventricle demonstrates mild global hypokinesis with an ejection fraction of 44%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows patchy, nodular mid-myocardial and subepicardial hyperenhancement within the basal to mid-interventricular septum and lateral free wall, typical of granulomatous infiltration. Edema is present in these regions on T2-weighted imaging.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with active cardiac sarcoidosis, showing myocardial edema and extensive non-ischemic scar/fibrosis.

Brain MRI demonstrates acute subarachnoid hemorrhage with hyperintense signal on FLAIR sequences and corresponding susceptibility artifact on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) within the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and cerebral sulci. No underlying parenchymal hemorrhage or acute territorial infarction is seen. The cerebral ventricles are mildly prominent, suggesting early acute communicating hydrocephalus.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage centered in the basal cisterns and sylvian fissures. Mild early ventriculomegaly; urgent digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or CT angiography is indicated to evaluate for intracranial aneurysm.

Brain MRI reveals diffuse, moderate-to-severe periventricular and deep white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, consistent with chronic microvascular ischemic disease. Prominent cerebral and cerebellar sulci and ventriculomegaly are noted, consistent with age-appropriate parenchymal loss. No acute ischemic stroke or hemorrhage is detected.

Impression: Moderately advanced chronic microvascular white matter ischemic disease and age-appropriate brain atrophy. No acute territorial infarction or mass.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates complete bilateral renal agenesis. No identifiable renal tissue or renal arteries are visualized in either renal fossa or within the pelvis. This is associated with severe oligohydramnios, causing fetal crowding and limiting diagnostic resolution in some areas. The fetal bladder is not visualized, indicating absence of urine production.

Intracranial anatomy is intact with a normal atrial measurement of 6.2 mm. Early primary sulcation appears appropriate. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe anhydramnios/oligohydramnios, indicating a highly guarded prognosis.

Evaluation of the heart with multiplanar MR imaging demonstrates normal cardiac chambers and myocardial thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 64% with normal concentric contraction. Right ventricular end-diastolic volumes are normal and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%.

No delayed hyperenhancement is present to suggest scar tissue. Pericardium is of normal thickness and no pericardial effusion is seen. Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular chamber size and function with no pathological scar tissue.

MR study of the brain demonstrates normal ventricular size and sulcation pattern. The gray-white matter junction is preserved throughout the cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres. No focus of restricted diffusion is identified to suggest acute stroke. The major dural venous sinuses show normal flow voids and patency.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain postpartum. No etiology for the patient's acute-on-chronic headaches identified on the current structural exam.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 2.4 cm in diameter. Phase-contrast flow quantification indicates a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 1.9. There is moderate dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, with preserved right ventricular systolic function (RVEF 52%). The left-sided chambers are normal in size.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and consequent right-sided chamber enlargement, meeting criteria for evaluation for closure.

Fetal MR imaging at 25 weeks gestation evaluates for severe skeletal shortening. The fetus demonstrates severe, symmetric micromelia of all long bones. The femur and humerus are bowed and markedly short. The fetal chest is extremely narrow and bell-shaped with severe pulmonary hypoplasia, while the abdomen is protuberant. The fetal skull shows frontal bossing, but the intracranial anatomy is normal for 25 weeks. The lateral ventricles measure 7.1 mm and the brain displays appropriate opercularization.

Polyhydramnios is present with a high amniotic fluid volume. Spine elements are intact but show general osteopenia. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with thoracic hypoplasia, highly characteristic of a lethal dysplasia such as thanatophoric dysplasia. Pediatric genetics and neonatology consultation is advised.

Cardiac MRI highlights significant bileaflet mitral valve prolapse. The posterior leaflet exhibits notable posterior displacement beyond the mitral annulus of 4.5 mm, associated with a large eccentric regurgitant jet directed anteriorly, consistent with severe mitral regurgitation. The left atrium is dilated (volume index of 48 mL/m2), while the left ventricle is upper limit of normal in size with preserved systolic function (EF 60%).

Impression: Myxomatous mitral valve disease with severe mitral regurgitation and left atrial enlargement. Left ventricular function remains preserved; close clinical monitoring for surgical intervention indices is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe are herniated into the left hemithorax. This causes a pronounced mediastinal shift to the right and severe compression of the right lung. The calculated total lung volume is significantly reduced, indicating severe pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable with age-appropriate sulcation and normal lateral ventricles (atrium 5.9 mm). Impression: Large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic liver herniation and severe secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy with a maximal septal wall thickness of 2.2 cm. There is associated systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy, mid-myocardial hyperenhancement within the hypertrophied septal segments, indicating myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Classic phenotypic features of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with focal septal fibrosis. Ventricular systolic function is hyperdynamic with an LVEF of 72%.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation for evaluation of fetal intracranial anatomy. High-resolution single-shot fast spin-echo images demonstrate normal brain development for the stated gestational age. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate early sulcation and migration patterns, with symmetric opercularization beginning. The ventricular system is normal in caliber, with the bilateral lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.5 mm. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellum are intact and normal in morphologic appearance.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study at 22 weeks gestation with normal intracranial anatomy and expected structural development for gestational age.

Cardiac MRI shows severe regional wall motion abnormalities, characterized by akinesis of the apical, anterior, and anteroseptal walls of the left ventricle. Global left ventricular systolic function is reduced with an ejection fraction of 35%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals a transmural pattern of hyperenhancement (exceeding 75% wall thickness) in the mid-to-distal LAD coronary artery territory.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with a large, non-viable subendocardial to transmural myocardial scar in the LAD distribution. Moderate-to-severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction is present.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates a poorly-demarcated, non-enhancing mass involving the cortex and subcortical white matter of the right frontal lobe. The lesion is hyperintense on T2/FLAIR and demonstrates hypointensity on T1-weighted images. There is minimal mass effect with subtle effacement of the surrounding cortical sulci and no significant midline shift.

Impression: Left frontal lobe infiltrative intra-axial lesion, most consistent with a low-grade astrocytoma. Follow-up imaging and neurosurgical stereotactic biopsy are recommended for definitive histological characterization.

A large, acute parenchymal hematoma is identified centered in the left basal ganglia, measuring 3.5 x 2.8 cm, displaying characteristic T1-isointense and T2-hypointense signal indicating acute deoxyhemoglobin stage. Surrounding vasogenic edema is noted with associated mass effect and compression of the left lateral ventricle, leading to a 4 mm midline shift. No intraventricular extension of the hemorrhage is seen.

Impression: Acute left basal ganglia/lobar intracerebral hemorrhage with moderate local mass effect. Hypertension is the most likely etiology.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal brain development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate primary sulcation for this stage, with well-defined Sylvian fissures. The ventricular system is normal in size, with the atrium of the lateral ventricles measuring 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is visible and intact, and the posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are unremarkable.

No extracranial anomalies are identified. The fetal chest, abdomen, and skeletal structures are normal for 22 weeks. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate intracranial and extracranial development.

Cardiac MRI shows a moderate circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 1.6 cm adjacent to the right ventricle and 1.2 cm adjacent to the left ventricular apex. There is no diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle to suggest active cardiac tamponade. The cardiac chambers are normal in size, and biventricular systolic function is well-preserved (LVEF 64%, RVEF 55%). Myocardial T1/T2 mapping values are within normal ranges with no LGE.

Impression: Moderate circumferential pericardial effusion without diagnostic MRI evidence of tamponade. The underlying myocardium is normal in size, function, and tissue characteristics.

Brain MRI performed to rule out intracranial pathology in a young female patient presenting with severe, localized, throbbing headaches and visual aura. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or pathologically enhancing lesions. The venous sinuses are patent and ventricles are of normal caliber.

Impression: Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular abnormalities seen to account for patient's migraine symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation. The left kidney is markedly enlarged and replaced by multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, with no identifiable normal renal parenchyma. The right kidney appears structurally normal with appropriate parenchymal thickness and normal corticomedullary differentiation. Amniotic fluid volume is within the normal range. Intracranial evaluation shows normal ventricles (5.9 mm) and mature sulculation.

Impression: Left-sided multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a normal, compensating right kidney and normal amniotic fluid volume.

MRI of the heart demonstrates completely normal biventricular size, morphology, and systolic function. LVEF is calculated at 65% and RVEF is 60%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement. Heart valves are structurally normal with physiological flow.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with preserved ventricular volume and function. No evidence of myocardial scarring, ischemia, or cardiomyopathy.

MR of the brain shows an ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion in the left frontal lobe white matter, measuring approximately 3.5 x 3.0 cm. There is minimal mass effect on the adjacent sulci and no evidence of surrounding vasogenic edema, restricted diffusion, or internal necrosis. No abnormal contrast enhancement is observed.

Impression: Non-enhancing infiltrative left frontal lobe lesion, most suggestive of a low-grade diffuse astrocytoma. Recommend clinical correlation and serial surveillance imaging.

Dedicated imaging of the pituitary gland reveals a well-circumscribed sellar mass measuring 1.8 x 1.4 x 1.5 cm with extension into the suprasellar cistern. This mass causes superior displacement and compression of the optic chiasm. There is no invasion into the bilateral cavernous sinuses, and the internal carotid arteries remain patent.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension resulting in optic chiasm compression. Correlation with prolactin and thyroid panels is recommended, along with visual field testing.

Multiplanar MRI brain scans are unremarkable. No structural abnormalities, intracranial mass lesions, or acute ischemia are seen. The ventricular system and sulci are normal for the patient's age, and the major cerebral blood vessels demonstrate normal signal voids without evidence of aneurysm or vascular malformation.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No focal intracranial pathology is demonstrated to account for the patient's sensory symptoms.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked, diffuse, symmetric thickening of the left ventricular myocardium (maximum thickness 1.8 cm) and interatrial septum. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences show diffuse, subendocardial hyperenhancement that does not conform to any single coronary artery territory, along with abnormal myocardial and blood pool gadolinium kinetics. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 44%.

Impression: High suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis given the classic diffuse subendocardial enhancement and marked biventricular and biatrial wall thickening. Correlate with hematological and tissue biopsy findings.

Cardiac MRI was obtained for follow-up of adult congenital heart disease in a patient with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. The right ventricle is severely dilated (RVEDVI 165 mL/m2) with dyskinesis of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) patch. Phase-contrast imaging of the main pulmonary artery demonstrates severe, free pulmonary regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 42%. The left ventricular size is normal with a preserved ejection fraction of 56%.

Impression: Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot demonstrating severe pulmonary regurgitation and significant right ventricular volume overload. These findings warrant consideration for pulmonary valve replacement.

High-resolution T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 images of the internal auditory canals reveal a well-circumscribed, intensely enhancing "ice cream cone" shaped mass centered in the right cerebellopontine angle, measuring 2.1 x 1.4 cm. The lesion extends into and widens the right internal auditory canal, causing mild compression on the adjacent right cerebellar hemisphere and brainstem.

Impression: Right vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with intracanalicular and extracanalicular components.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced fetal development. The cerebral cortex shows extensive, complex sulcation and gyration patterns appropriate for a near-term 36-week fetus, with deep secondary and tertiary sulci visualized. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and measure 5.4 mm. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellum are normal.

Fetal anatomy is grossly intact with appropriate subcutaneous fat deposition and normal visceral development. Impression: Completely normal late third-trimester fetal MRI.

MRI of the brain shows prominent enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, which is out of proportion to the mild degree of cortical sulcal thinning. There is a decreased callosal angle and a visible CSF flow void through the aqueduct of Sylvius. No mass lesion is causing this obstructive pattern.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to atrophy. Findings are highly suggestive of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with gait, cognition, and continence is advised.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development of the fetal brain. The lateral ventricles are normal, with the atrium measuring 6.0 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks, with well-formed parieto-occipital, calcarine, and cingulate sulci, and beginning development of the superior temporal sulcus. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum and optic chiasm, are normal.

The posterior fossa is normal, with the cerebellar vermis fully formed and an appropriate transverse cerebellar diameter. Chest and abdomen are within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation, demonstrating healthy structural and cortical development.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The right hepatic lobe and portion of the small bowel have herniated through a posterior-lateral diaphragmatic defect, resulting in moderate leftward mediastinal shift. The left lung volume is mildly reduced. Brain examination reveals appropriate cortical sulcation and normal ventricular sizes (atrial width 6.2 mm).

The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are structurally intact. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation, leading to moderate mediastinal shift and secondary mass effect on the lungs.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows normal, symmetric intracranial development. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrial diameter measuring 5.5 mm bilaterally. The sulcation and gyration patterns, including the sylvian fissures and superior temporal sulci, are well-defined and highly appropriate for 32 weeks. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are normal.

Visualized chest anatomy shows symmetric lung volumes and a centrally positioned heart. Abdominal organs, kidneys, and fetal spine are completely unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with appropriate intracranial and extracranial development for 32 weeks of gestation.

Cardiovascular MRI demonstrates a discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrowest segment measures 11 mm in diameter, with post-stenotic dilatation of the downstream aorta measuring 24 mm. Prominent intercostal collateral arteries are visualized. Left ventricular mass is mildly elevated, but systolic function is preserved (LVEF 60%).

Impression: Coarctation of the aorta with characteristic post-stenotic dilation and collateralization. This study was performed as part of a preconception risk assessment; the finding warrants surgical or percutaneous intervention planning.

MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals shows symmetric, normal appearance of the CPA cisterns and IACs bilaterally. The 7th and 8th cranial nerve complexes are intact and free of compression or pathologically increased enhancement. The brain parenchyma is unremarkable, and there are no vascular loops compressing the auditory nerves.

Impression: Unremarkable MR examination of the brain and internal auditory canals, with no evidence of acoustic neuroma or retrocochlear pathology to account for subjective tinnitus.

MRI demonstrates a large, heterogeneous, infiltrative mass in the right temporal lobe measuring 4.5 x 4.2 x 3.8 cm. The lesion shows thick, irregular ring enhancement following gadolinium administration, surrounding a central necrotic region. Pronounced vasogenic edema surrounds the mass, causing subfalcine herniation of 6 mm to the left.

Impression: Aggressive intra-axial right temporal mass, highly characteristic of glioblastoma or solitary necrotic metastasis. Prominent mass effect and midline shift require urgent neurosurgical evaluation.

Cardiac MRI was requested for screening in a 23-year-old collegiate runner with a single episode of exercise-associated lightheadedness. The left ventricular chamber exhibits mild, symmetric enlargement (LVEDVI of 95 mL/m2) and mild concentric wall thickening (maximum wall thickness 11 mm), which is consistent with physiological remodeling of an athletic heart. Left and right ventricular ejection fractions are normal at 61% and 55%, respectively.

No late gadolinium enhancement, focal fibrosis, or myocardial edema is identified. Normal coronary origins are confirmed. Impression: Athlete's heart with expected physiological left ventricular remodeling. No features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or other pathology to account for syncope.

MR venogram and brain MRI reveal a lack of normal flow void and a filling defect in the left transverse and sigmoid sinuses, consistent with acute thrombosis. There is mild venous congestion and a small focal area of petechial hemorrhage in the adjacent left temporal-occipital lobe without significant mass effect or herniation.

Impression: Acute left transverse and sigmoid dural venous sinus thrombosis, associated with a small localized venous congestion/petechial hemorrhage. Clinically correlate with hypercoagulable risk factors or recent obstetric/contraceptive history.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation performed for maternal systemic lupus erythematosus. The fetal brain shows normal structural appearance. Cortical sulcation and gyration are well-developed and appropriate for 33 weeks gestation, demonstrating clear secondary and tertiary sulci. The ventricular system is normal, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.9 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal.

Fetal thoracic, abdominal, and skeletal structures are normal, and amniotic fluid volume is adequate. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study at 33 weeks gestation. No cerebral or somatic anomalies seen.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation shows appropriate anatomical development for early second trimester. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate smooth cortical surfaces with early sylvian fissure definition, normal for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.5 mm bilaterally, and the ventricles are symmetric. The corpus callosum is early in development but visible.

The fetal musculoskeletal system, spine, and chest are normal in appearance. Impression: Normal early fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation for parental anxiety. Multiplanar T2-weighted sequences show normal brain maturation. The hemispheric sulcation is smooth, exhibiting early sylvian fissure closure appropriate for 24 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atria measuring 6.2 mm. Midline structures and posterior fossa are intact.

Fetal abdominal organs, chest, and spine are fully normal. Amniotic fluid volume is physiologic. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating entirely age-appropriate central nervous system and visceral development.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and extracranial anatomy. Cerebral hemispheric sulcation patterns, including the sylvian and parieto-occipital fissures, are appropriate for 28 weeks. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.4 mm symmetrically. The corpus callosum is fully formed, and the brainstem is normal.

Fetal lungs show normal volume and signal intensity relative to the liver on T2-weighted sequences. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation showing normal structural development and age-appropriate brain maturation.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation for evaluation of fetal anatomy. Multiplanar, ultrafast T2-weighted and T1-weighted sequences demonstrate normal intracranial structure. The fetal brain shows age-appropriate development with normal early operculization and smooth cerebral cortex. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with an atrial width measuring 5.5 mm on the left and 5.7 mm on the right. The corpus callosum is visible and fully intact. No posterior fossa abnormalities are noted; the cerebellar vermis and brainstem are structurally intact.

Fetal viscera, thoracic anatomy, and spine are normal. Visualized fetal extremities show normal alignment. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study at 22 weeks gestation. No structural anomalies or CNS malformations are identified.

Cardiac MRI obtained for workup of unexplained syncopal episodes. Cine and structural imaging demonstrate normal cardiac chamber morphology. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume and ejection fraction (60%) are within the normal range. Right ventricular volumes and systolic function are also normal (RVEF 55%). No evidence of myocardial hypertrophy, localized wall motion abnormalities, or late gadolinium enhancement is present.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular size and function, and no evidence of structural myocardial pathology or scar tissue.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates cerebellar hypoplasia. The cerebellar vermis is present but significantly hypoplastic and rotated upward, with a large retrocerebellar fluid collection communicating with the fourth ventricle. There is mild bilateral ventriculomegaly with the atrial measurements of 9.5 mm.

The rest of the brain anatomy, including the corpus callosum and cortical migration patterns, is normal for 26 weeks. Impression: Cerebellar hypoplasia and prominent retrocerebellar cyst, consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant (cerebellar vermian hypoplasia).

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows typical opercularization and sulcation progress for late second/early third trimester. The ventricular atria measure 6.1 mm bilaterally, which is within the normal range. The corpus callosum is present and fully formed. The brainstem, cerebellum, spine, chest, and abdominal organs are completely normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation, with age-appropriate brain development and no evidence of intracranial or systemic structural defects.

Cardiac MRI evaluates severe mitral regurgitation. There is significant bileaflet mitral valve prolapse, particularly prominent in the posterior leaflet (P2 segment), which demonstrates superior displacement of approximately 4 mm above the mitral annulus during systole. The regurgitant jet is large, eccentric, and directed anteriorly. The left atrium is severely dilated with a volume index of 62 mL/m2. Left ventricular dimensions are at the upper limit of normal, with an LVEF of 68%.

Impression: Severe mitral valve prolapse (primarily involving P2) resulting in severe, eccentric mitral regurgitation. This is associated with significant left atrial enlargement and early left ventricular remodeling.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates elevated T2 relaxation times and increased early gadolinium enhancement within the mid-myocardium and subepicardium of the lateral wall, indicating active localized myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging confirms non-ischemic, patchy enhancement patterns in these same regions. Overall left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly depressed at 49%, with associated mild regional hypokinesia of the lateral wall segments.

Impression: Findings are strongly diagnostic of acute myocarditis matching Lake Louise criteria. Mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction is noted.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large cystic and solid mass in the lower lobe of the left fetal lung. The mass contains multiple small cysts, the largest measuring 1.2 cm, and displays high signal intensity on T2-weighted imaging. There is associated mass effect, with mild rightward displacement of the mediastinum and heart. The remaining right lung tissue is normal in volume. No signs of fetal hydrops are present; there is no pleural effusion or ascites.

Fetal brain anatomy is normal, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.2 mm. Impression: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM/CCAM), type II, involving the left lower lobe. Mild mediastinal shift without evidence of fetal hydrops.

Cardiac MRI shows severe dilatation and global dysfunction of the right ventricle, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 160 mL/m2 and an RVEF of 34%. Cine sequences demonstrate focal dyskinesis and micro-aneurysmal outpouchings in the right ventricular outflow tract and free wall (the triangle of dysplasia). The left ventricle is normal in size and function, with an ejection fraction of 59%.

Late gadolinium enhancement sequences demonstrate patchy, mid-myocardial to subepicardial hyperenhancement within the right ventricular free wall, indicative of fibrofatty replacement. Impression: Features are highly characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) meeting multiple major Task Force criteria.

Brain MRI demonstrates progressive ventriculomegaly involving the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, which is disproportionate to the mild degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. There is rounding of the frontal horns and a prominent flow void in the aqueduct of Sylvius on T2-weighted imaging, with narrowing of the sulci at the high convexities.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal prominence, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and preserved systolic function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 73 mL/m² and the ejection fraction is 65%. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 70 mL/m² with an ejection fraction of 59%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities or signs of ventricular hypertrophy.

Tissue characterization by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is negative for focal scar or fibrosis. T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) measurements are within normal limits. Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with preserved ventricular function and no evidence of structural or tissue pathology.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates isolated, mild right unilateral ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.8 mm. The left lateral ventricular atrium is normal, measuring 6.3 mm. No evidence of periventricular leukomalacia, subependymal cysts, or germinal matrix hemorrhage is seen. The cerebral sulcation and myelination match the 34-week gestational age.

The posterior fossa and somatic structures are unremarkable. Impression: Mild, isolated right-sided unilateral ventriculomegaly. Close monitoring with serial ultrasounds is suggested.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar and multisequence protocols. The cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum demonstrate normal signal intensity and morphology. There is no evidence of acute infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, or abnormal extra-axial fluid collections. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for the patient's age.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural or vascular abnormality is seen to account for the patient's chronic migraines.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). A significant portion of the liver and gall bladder, along with loops of small bowel, have herniated into the right thoracic cavity, resulting in a severe shift of the mediastinum to the left. The right lung is nearly completely compressed, and the left lung is significantly reduced in volume, with a calculated total fetal lung volume below the 5th percentile for 29 weeks. Intracranial structures and sulcation are normal.

The fetal heart is structurally normal but heavily compressed. Impression: Severe right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with massive liver herniation, severe mediastinal shift, and secondary bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a small, restrictive ventricular septal defect (VSD) located in the perimembranous septum, measuring approximately 4.5 mm. Velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging confirms a localized, high-velocity left-to-right shunt jet during systole. The shunt ratio (Qp/Qs) is calculated at 1.15, indicating hemodynamically insignificant shunting.

Left and right ventricular cavity sizes are normal, and left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 60%. There is no evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy or elevated pulmonary artery pressures. Impression: Small, hemodynamically restrictive perimembranous ventricular septal defect with negligible left-to-right shunt and preserved biventricular dimensions and performance.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrates mild, age-appropriate diffuse cortical atrophy and minimal, nonspecific deep white matter microvascular changes. There is no hippocampal atrophy, acute territorial infarct, hemorrhage, or mass lesion. The ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are prominent but appropriate for age.

Impression: No acute intracranial pathology. Mild cerebral atrophy and minor microvascular ischemic disease, within expected limits for age, with no focal lesions explaining cognitive decline.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows appropriate development, with clearly visible central and lateral sulci in alignment with 28-week development. The ventricular system is normal, with the atrium measuring 6.1 mm. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum and septum pellucidum, are normal and intact.

The spine, thorax, abdomen, and limbs show no abnormalities. Normal amniotic fluid is present. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation, demonstrating normal structural development.

The cerebral hemispheres show normal morphological and signal characteristics. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, acute hemorrhage, cerebral edema, or abnormal contrast enhancement. The orbital structures, including optic nerves, are normal in course and appearance.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or demyelinating process seen to explain the patient's new-onset visual aura.

Cardiac MRI was performed for surveillance during anthracycline-based chemotherapy for breast cancer. The left ventricle demonstrates normal internal cavity dimensions with no regional wall motion abnormalities. The global left ventricular ejection fraction is stable at 58% (previously 59%), and global longitudinal strain remains within normal limits. There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2 mapping or focal fibrosis on LGE sequences.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study showing preserved biventricular systolic function and no tissue characteristics of anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity. Continued clinical monitoring is recommended.

MR imaging reveals a broad-based, extra-axial dural-tailed mass along the left frontal convexity measuring 3.1 x 2.8 x 2.6 cm. The mass is homogeneously hyperintense to gray matter on T2-weighted sequences and demonstrates intense, uniform enhancement following contrast administration. There is mild adjacent vasogenic edema and local mass effect on the left frontal cortex.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with a benign left frontal convexity meningioma. No midline shift is observed; ventricular system remains patent and symmetric.

Dedicated pituitary protocol MR imaging demonstrates a well-defined, hypoenhancing focus in the left aspect of the adenohypophysis measuring 6 mm. The pituitary stalk is minimally deviated to the right, and the optic chiasm is structurally completely free from any superior mass effect.

Impression: Findings are diagnostic of a pituitary microadenoma. Findings are stable with no extension into the cavernous sinuses or optic pathway compression.

Brain MRI was obtained at 32 weeks gestation due to sudden onset of seizures and severe preeclampsia. There are symmetric areas of increased T2/FLAIR signal intensity in the subcortical white matter of the bilateral occipital and parietal lobes. These lesions show no associated diffusion restriction, consistent with vasogenic edema.

Impression: Magnetic resonance findings of the brain are highly characteristic of Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) in the setting of severe preeclampsia. No intracranial hemorrhage or acute infarction is identified.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The stomach, multiple loops of small and large bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe are herniated into the left thoracic cavity. This has caused a significant rightward mediastinal shift, with the heart displaced into the right hemithorax. The left lung is severely compressed and virtually non-visualized, and the right lung is moderately hypoplastic. Total fetal lung volume is calculated at 11.4 mL, which is significantly reduced for 28 weeks gestation.

The fetal intracranial anatomy is normal, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.0 mm and age-appropriate sulcation. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic herniation of stomach, bowel, and liver. Associated mediastinal shift and severe bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate a 31-year-old female with a family history of unexplained sudden cardiac death. The left ventricle is normal in size, wall thickness, and function (LVEDV 118 mL, LVEF 64%). Right ventricular volumes and systolic function are also normal (RVEDV 125 mL, RVEF 55%). Multiplanar cine sequences show no regional wall motion abnormalities or focal aneurysms.
