Myocardial perfusion is normal, and there is no late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or tissue characterization findings suggestive of cardiomyopathy or arrhythmogenic disorders.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks 4 days gestation reveals features highly characteristic of severe skeletal dysplasia, likely Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type II. There is generalized osteopenia with compressible calvarium and marked shortening and bowing of all long bones. Multiple healed and acute fractures of the ribs are seen, causing a narrow, hypoplastic, bell-shaped thoracic cage. Fetal lung volumes are significantly reduced.

The fetal brain shows normal cortical sulcation patterns for age; the ventricular system is unremarkable with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 5.9 mm. Impression: Lethal skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type II, with severe rib fractures and pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI shows marked dilatation of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m2. There is global hypokinesis of the left ventricle with a severely reduced ejection fraction of 32%. Visualized myocardial walls show normal thickness without focal thinning. No late gadolinium enhancement is noted, and native T1 and T2 mapping are mildly, diffusely elevated, reflecting diffuse interstitial congestion/edema.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of peripartum cardiomyopathy in this postpartum patient. There is severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction without evidence of ischemic scar or focal myocarditis.

Brain MRI and MR venography (MRV) performed to investigate persistent postpartum headaches. There is normal signal intensity and morphology within all cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres. MRV shows complete patency and normal flow voids within the superior sagittal, transverse, and sigmoid dural venous sinuses.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI and MR venogram. No evidence of dural venous sinus thrombosis or intracranial hypertension.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation. High-resolution imaging demonstrates mature brain anatomy with fully developed, complex sulcation and gyration patterns appropriate for the late third trimester. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and normal, with atrial diameters measuring 5.2 mm. Visualized thoracic and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Normal fetal biometry and subcutaneous fat thickness are noted.

Impression: Unremarkable late third-trimester fetal MRI, demonstrating normal development.

Cardiac MRI evaluates cardiac morphology and function. The left and right ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and systolic function are completely normal (LVEF 64%, RVEF 59%). There are no regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema, or pathological late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No diagnostic features of structural heart disease or active myocardial inflammation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked dilation and regional dyskinesis of the right ventricular free wall, with microaneurysms noted in the RV outflow tract and inferior wall. There is extensive fibrofatty infiltration of the right ventricular myocardium, supported by matching signal characteristics on T1-weighted imaging. The right ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 29%.

Impression: Highly characteristic features of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major task force criteria.

Brain MRI was performed utilizing high-resolution sequences. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial space-occupying lesion, midline shift, or hydrocephalus. The gray-white matter junction is well-differentiated, and the myelination pattern is normal. Visualized orbital structures and paranasal sinuses are unremarkable. No restricted diffusion is seen to suggest acute ischemic stroke.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or demyelinating abnormalities identified to account for the patient's primary headaches.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation. The fetal brain demonstrates normal architecture. The lateral ventricles measure 6.5 mm bilaterally, and the third and fourth ventricles are normal in size. The posterior fossa, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, is normal. Fetal lungs, spine, and abdominal wall are intact with no evidence of herniation or masses.

Impression: Normal second-trimester fetal MRI with no visible structural anomalies.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple well-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. There are multiple 'black holes' representing T1 hypointensities. No lesions show active enhancement on post-contrast sequences.

Impression: Chronic demyelinating disease consistent with Multiple Sclerosis. No signs of active demyelination or enhancing plaques on the current study.

Magnetic resonance angiography and cardiac MRI demonstrate a discrete, severe narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, characteristic of aortic coarctation. Extensive dilated collateral arterial vessels, including the internal mammary and intercostal arteries, bypass the obstruction. The left ventricle demonstrates concentric hypertrophy (mass index 115 g/m2) with a preserved ejection fraction of 61%.

Impression: Severe discrete coarctation of the aorta with extensive collateralization and compensatory left ventricular concentric hypertrophy. Surgical or transcatheter intervention is indicated.

MR imaging of the brain shows bilateral flattening of the posterior sclera and tortuosity of the optic nerves, with prominent CSF perineural sheaths. The optic nerve heads demonstrate mild intraocular protrusion, consistent with papilledema. The pituitary gland is flattened against the floor of the sella, presenting an 'empty sella' appearance. The dural venous sinuses are patent but narrow.

Impression: MRI findings are highly suggestive of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH / Pseudotumor Cerebri). Recommend clinical correlation with lumbar puncture opening pressures and ophthalmologic evaluation.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal left and right ventricular cavity sizes. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities or focal thinning. Left ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 64%. First-pass perfusion shows no inducible perfusion deficits or delayed enhancement. Visualized cardiac valves are structurally and functionally normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular function and no evidence of macrovascular ischemia or structural disease. This study is reassurance for suspected microvascular dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with previous childhood repair of aortic coarctation. There is mild narrowing at the site of the prior repair in the distal aortic arch, with a peak pressure gradient estimated at 18 mmHg. Minimal collateral vessels are seen. Left ventricular wall thickness is at the upper limit of normal (septum 1.1 cm), and LVEF is normal at 60%.

Impression: Status post coarctation of the aorta repair with mild residual/recurrent stenosis at the anastomosis site, not meeting criteria for severe restenosis. Left ventricular structure and function are well preserved.

Brain MRI demonstrates preserved intracranial volume with sulcal and ventricular size appropriate for a 61-year-old. No abnormal areas of restricted diffusion, parenchymal signal intensity, or mass effect are observed. The orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal age-appropriate MRI of the brain. No acute pathology, neoplastic process, or signs of intracranial hypertension.

MRI of the brain reveals a severely flattened pituitary gland against the floor of the sella turcica, demonstrating an 'empty sella' configuration. Additional findings include mild flattening of the posterior sclera bilaterally, prominent distention of the perioptic subarachnoid spaces, and mild tortuosity of the optic nerves. There is no venous sinus stenosis or mass lesion.

Impression: Radiographic features consistent with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri). Clinical correlation with fundoscopy for papilledema is recommended.

Cardiac MRI performed during the second trimester of pregnancy to evaluate recurrent palpitations. Normal left and right ventricular volumes and systolic function are demonstrated, with a calculated LVEF of 62% and RVEF of 56%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or myocardial edema are present. Myocardial perfusion sequences and tissue characterization show no late gadolinium enhancement or scarring.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, or structural heart disease to account for the patient's palpitations.

Brain MRI demonstrates entirely normal intracranial structures without evidence of focal cerebral pathology. The ventricular system and sulci are normal for the patient's age. No areas of restricted diffusion, intracranial hemorrhage, or pathologically enhancing masses are seen. The brainstem and cerebellum are completely normal.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality is present to explain the patient's clinical symptoms of essential tremor.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks 6 days gestation evaluated for suspected fetal anomalies. Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable for this early gestational age. The cerebral mantle is smooth, with early parieto-occipital fissure formation visible, which is appropriate for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricles are normal, with atrial measurements of 5.2 mm. The corpus callosum is partially visible, consistent with early development. Posterior fossa is normal.

Fetal chest and abdomen are well-visualized and demonstrate no structural abnormalities. Spine is intact. Impression: Normal, unremarkable fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI performed at 36 weeks gestation for persistent severe oligohydramnios and suspected renal anomalies. There is a complete absence of identifiable fetal kidney tissue in either renal fossa, and the fetal bladder is not visualized. There is virtual absence of amniotic fluid (anhydramnios). The fetal lungs appear hypoplastic, with volumes severely reduced for gestational age.

The fetal brain demonstrates mature sulcation appropriate for 36 weeks, and the ventricular atrium measures 6.2 mm. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and severe secondary pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence).

Cardiac MRI was performed on this 29-year-old pregnant patient (30 weeks gestation) presenting with sinus tachycardia and frequent palpitations. The examination demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are identified. T2-weighted imaging shows no evidence of myocardial edema, and myocardial perfusion sequences demonstrate no inducible perfusion defects.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with normal biventricular volumes and systolic function. No evidence of gestational cardiomyopathy, acute myocarditis, or ischemia to account for the patient's symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development of the fetal central nervous system. The cerebral cortex shows appropriate sulcal depth and opercularization for gestational age. The ventricular system is normal, with an atrial width of 6.1 mm. The midline structures, posterior fossa, and cerebellum are well-formed.

The fetal chest, spine, and abdomen are unremarkable, and amniotic fluid is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural development and brain maturation at 26 weeks gestation.

MR imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar, multisequence techniques. No area of restricted diffusion, acute parenchymal hemorrhage, or intracranial mass is identified. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are normal in caliber and morphology. There is no abnormal intracranial leptomeningeal or dural enhancement.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or ischemic abnormalities are seen to account for the patient's symptoms.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates patchy, epicardial and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) along the lateral and inferior walls of the left ventricle. T2-weighted STIR imaging shows hyperintensity in the corresponding regions, indicating localized myocardial edema. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced with an LVEF of 48%. Right ventricular function is preserved (RVEF 54%). A tiny trace pericardial effusion is present.

Impression: Findings satisfy Lake Louise criteria for acute myocarditis, characterized by epicardial/mid-wall LGE and corresponding myocardial edema.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows age-appropriate development of the cerebral cortex. The sulcation and gyration pattern is normal, with expected opercularization of the parietal and temporal lobes. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, measuring 6.0 mm in the left atrium and 5.8 mm in the right atrium. The posterior fossa structures and corpus callosum are fully formed and unremarkable.

No chest, abdominal, or skeletal anomalies are seen. The spine is completely intact. Impression: Normal third-trimester fetal MRI. No morphological or structural anomalies of the brain or body are identified.

Maternal cardiac MRI performed at 30 weeks gestation for workup of progressive dyspnea. The left and right ventricular chambers demonstrate normal internal diameters and wall thicknesses. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. No late gadolinium enhancement, regional wall motion abnormalities, or myocardial edema can be identified.

Impression: Completely normal maternal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of peripartum cardiomyopathy or myocardial inflammation is present.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows completely normal intracranial anatomy. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with normal atrial width of 5.9 mm. Early sulcation, including the formation of the parieto-occipital sulcus and Sylvian fissures, is normal and appropriate for 24 weeks' development. The posterior fossa structures are normal.

Chest, abdomen, and spine are intact. Normal volume of amniotic fluid is present. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body development at 24 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals severe shortening of all long bones, with curved femur morphology ('telephone receiver' shape), consistent with Thanatophoric Dysplasia. The chest is extremely narrow and pear-shaped, indicating severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Marked macrocephaly with frontal bossing is present. The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated at 10.4 mm.

Fetal brain sulcation is otherwise appropriate for 24 weeks. Impression: Thanatophoric dysplasia, characterized by severe micromelia, narrow chest, and characteristic craniofacial features. This is a lethal skeletal dysplasia.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates mild, isolated unilateral ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium is dilated, measuring 11.2 mm, while the left atrium is within normal limits at 6.8 mm. The ventricular margins are smooth, and there is no evidence of periventricular nodularity, intraventricular hemorrhage, or synechiae.

Cortical sulcation is normal and age-appropriate. All other intracranial and extracranial organs appear intact. Impression: Mild, isolated right-sided unilateral ventriculomegaly. No other structural abnormalities or signs of intracranial hemorrhage are visualized. Follow-up imaging is recommended.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation reveals bilateral, asymmetric ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.5 mm (severe ventriculomegaly), while the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 12.1 mm (moderate ventriculomegaly). There is mild stretching of the corpus callosum over the dilated ventricles, though the callosal structure is present in its entirety. Cortical sulcation pattern is appropriate for the gestational age.

No other intracranial masses, hemorrhage, or midline shifts are demonstrated. Visualized fetal organs and skeletal structures appear unremarkable. Impression: Bilateral moderate-to-severe ventriculomegaly. Recommend postnatal clinical correlation and prenatal neurosurgical consultation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a young female patient presenting with acute chest pain and elevated troponins following a viral syndrome. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences demonstrate focal areas of high signal intensity in the subepicardium of the lateral and basal left ventricular walls, consistent with acute myocardial edema. Corresponding late gadolinium enhancement is observed in a non-ischemic, subepicardial and mid-wall distribution in these same territories.

Impression: Acute myocarditis satisfying the updated Lake Louise criteria. Mild global left ventricular systolic dysfunction is noted with an ejection fraction of 52%.

Sagittal MR sequences demonstrate cerebellar tonsillar herniation extending approximately 8.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear peg-like and pointed. There is associated effacement of the CSF spaces at the craniocervical junction. Evaluation of the cervical spine reveals a small syrinx cavity extending from C2 to C4.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with cerebellar tonsillar descent of 8.5 mm and associated cervical syringomyelia. Referral to a neurosurgeon for evaluation and management is recommended.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a broad-based, extra-axial mass arising from the right parietal dura, measuring 2.5 x 2.2 cm. The lesion is isointense to cortex on T1 and T2 sequences and demonstrates homogeneous, intense enhancement following gadolinium administration, with a classic dural tail. There is mild adjacent vasogenic edema within the parietal lobe and slight compression of the adjacent sulci.

Impression: Extra-axial enhancing mass in the right parietal region, characteristic of a benign dural-based meningioma. Mild local mass effect without midline shift.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate post-viral pericarditis. There is a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion, measuring up to 1.8 cm adjacent to the right ventricle, without signs of diastolic chamber collapse on real-time cine sequences. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows intense, diffuse enhancement and thickening of both the visceral and parietal pericardium. The underlying myocardium appears normal with preserved biventricular function (LVEF 59%).

Impression: Subacute pericarditis with a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion and active pericardial inflammation. There is no evidence of associated myocardial involvement (myopericarditis).

Brain MRI reveals a well-defined, ring-enhancing lesion in the left temporal lobe measuring 2.4 x 2.2 cm. The lesion exhibits central restricted diffusion (marked hyperintensity on DWI and hypointensity on ADC) and is surrounded by a thick, smooth, regular wall. There is extensive surrounding vasogenic edema with compression of the left lateral ventricle temporal horn.

Impression: Ring-enhancing left temporal lobe lesion with central restricted diffusion, highly characteristic of a pyogenic brain abscess. Neurosurgical and infectious disease consultation is urgently indicated.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a single fetus in breech presentation. The cerebral cortex shows normal sulcation patterns for late second trimester, with developing sylvian and parieto-occipital fissures. The ventricles are normal with a lateral ventricular atrial width of 5.8 mm. The brainstem, vermis, corpus callosum, and face are completely unremarkable. Fetal chest and abdominal organs are anatomically intact.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation without evidence of central nervous system or somatic anomalies.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks 2 days gestation. The fetal brain demonstrates normal development for gestational age. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and measure 6.1 mm at the atria. The corpus callosum and cerebellar vermis are intact and normally configured. The sulcation is appropriate, with early temporal lobe operculization.

No extra-axial fluid collections are seen. The thoracic and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MR study with completely normal intracranial and extracranial structures.

Cardiac MRI reveals localized bulging, thinning, and dyskinesia of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and inferior RV wall. Right ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 35% with significant RV dilation. High-resolution T1-weighted images show focal areas of fatty infiltration in the RV free wall, with corresponding late gadolinium enhancement. The left ventricle has normal dimensions and function.

Impression: Features are highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on regional wall motion anomalies, RV dilation, and tissue characterization.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation. Normal early fetal anatomy is demonstrated. Early sulcation is progressing appropriately with a smooth cortical plate and primary sulci beginning to appear. The lateral ventricles measure 5.2 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum is present and appropriate for 20 weeks. Normal positioning of abdominal viscera, intact fetal spine, and normal amniotic fluid volume are noted.

Impression: Completely normal early second-trimester fetal MRI study.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates near-complete absence of the cerebral hemispheres. The cerebral parenchyma is replaced by a large fluid collection containing cerebrospinal fluid. Portions of the occipital lobes and lower temporal lobes are partially spared. The falx cerebri is intact. The thalami, brainstem, and cerebellum are preserved and structurally normal within the posterior fossa. The head size is normal for gestational age.

The fetal chest and abdomen are unremarkable. Impression: Hydranencephaly. This represents severe destruction of the cerebral hemispheres, likely due to a bilateral internal carotid artery occlusion or severe intrauterine insult.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient post-chemotherapy for cardiotoxicity screening. The study demonstrates entirely normal left ventricular volumes and morphology. Global systolic function is preserved with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 57%. There are no focal wall motion abnormalities, and T1 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are normal.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular size, functioning, and tissue characterization with no signs of chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy.

Brain MRI was performed using multiplanar multi-echo sequences. The cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, brainstem, and cerebellum are normal in appearance and signal intensity. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are normal in caliber. No focus of abnormal intracranial enhancement, restricted diffusion, or susceptibility artifact is seen.

Impression: Completely unremarkable brain MRI study. No acute or chronic intracranial pathology is identified.

Cardiac MRI shows normal chamber dimensions. Left and right ventricular volumes, wall thicknesses, and systolic parameters are within the expected physiological range for age. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of ischemia, rest perfusion abnormalities, or late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scarring.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI examination. No structural, tissue-characterization, or functional abnormalities are identified.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation for evaluation of ventriculomegaly. There is partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with the posterior portion (splenium and body) absent, while the anterior genu and rostrum are partially formed. Mild colpocephaly is present, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles dilated; the left atrium measures 11.8 mm and the right atrium measures 12.1 mm. The cortical sulcation is otherwise appropriate for 31 weeks, showing expected secondary and tertiary sulci.

The posterior fossa, spine, and fetal chest/abdomen are within normal limits. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild bilateral colpocephaly/ventriculomegaly.

MR study reveals an ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense mass measuring 3.5 x 3.2 cm within the right temporal lobe white matter. The lesion demonstrates no significant mass effect or surrounding vasogenic edema, and there is no evidence of restricted diffusion or contrast enhancement.

Impression: Low-grade intra-axial neoplasm, highly suggestive of a diffuse astrocytoma. Follow-up advanced imaging (MR spectroscopy/perfusion) or tissue biopsy is recommended for definitive grading.

Brain MRI demonstrates hyperintense T2/FLAIR lesions involving the periependymal regions surrounding the third and fourth ventricles, as well as the dorsal medulla. A prominent, longitudinal lesion is also visualized extending from the upper cervical cord. There is no significant mass effect or midline shift.

Impression: Periependymal and dorsal medulla brainstem lesions in conjunction with cervical cord involvement, highly characteristic of Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD). Clinical correlation with aquaporin-4 (AQP4-IgG) serology is recommended.

The study demonstrates a wedge-shaped area of restricted diffusion with matching T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the left frontoparietal cortex, corresponding to the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory. There is mild associated local mass effect and sulcal effacement, with no hemorrhagic transformation identified on SWI sequences.

Impression: Acute ischemic stroke in the distribution of the left MCA. No signs of intracranial hemorrhage.

MRI of the brain demonstrates an absent flow void within the superior sagittal sinus and right transverse sinus, associated with hyperintense thrombus on T1-weighted sequences. Additionally, there is a small zone of hemorrhagic venous infarction in the right parasagittal parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Acute dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal and right transverse sinuses, resulting in a localized right parietal lobe hemorrhagic venous infarction.

Brain MRI performed using a standard multiplanar, multisequence protocol without contrast demonstrates symmetric ventricles and sulci, appropriate for the patient's age. No areas of restricted diffusion, acute hemorrhage, or mass effect are identified. Visualized intracranial arterial flow voids are intact.

Impression: Unremarkable MR imaging of the brain. No structural or acute intracranial pathology identified to account for patient's complaints.

High-resolution sequences targeting the internal auditory canals reveal an intensely enhancing, ice-cream cone shaped mass centered in the left cerebellopontine angle, measuring approximately 1.8 x 1.4 cm. The mass widens the internal auditory canal and exerts mild mass effect on the adjacent pons and cerebellar peduncle.

Impression: Enhancing left cerebellopontine angle mass characteristic of a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma). No contralateral lesions identified; no evidence of neurofibromatosis type II.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals a large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the right hepatic lobe, gallbladder, and portions of the small intestine is noted into the right thoracic cavity, compressing the heart and shifting the mediastinum to the left. The left lung is compressed, showing severely decreased lung volumes.

The fetal brain shows normal cortical development and sulcation corresponding to 33 weeks. The lateral ventricles measure 5.8 mm. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation, severe mediastinal shift, and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI reveals asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the interventricular septum measuring 2.1 cm compared to a posterior wall thickness of 1.1 cm. Systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet is observed, creating a dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates patchy mid-wall enhancement at the insertion points of the right ventricular free wall into the septum.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with dynamic LVOT obstruction and classic focal fibrosis at right ventricular insertion points. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with hyperdynamic LVEF of 74%.

Dedicated MRI of the internal auditory canals shows an enhancing, ice-cream cone-shaped mass centered in the right cerebellopontine angle, measuring 2.1 x 1.6 cm. The mass extends into the internal auditory canal, causing widening of the canal. There is mild compression of the adjacent right cerebellar hemisphere and brainstem, without significant hydrocephalus.

Impression: Right cerebellopontine angle dural-based enhancing mass with extension into the internal auditory canal, highly characteristic of a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma).

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging reveals normal ventricular chambers. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 74 mL/m2, with a calculated ejection fraction of 62%, showing normal global and regional wall motion. The right ventricle is also normal in size and function (ejection fraction 58%). There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T1 or T2 mapping, and late gadolinium enhancement imaging is entirely negative for focal myocardial fibrosis or scarring.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, or ischemic change to account for postpartum atypical chest wall pain.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate ventricular function in a 30-year-old female with a history of severe gestational hypertension in her recent pregnancy. The myocardium demonstrates normal thickness and signal intensity on all sequences. Quantitative biventricular volume analysis is within normal limits, with an LVEF of 59% and an RVEF of 55%. No late gadolinium enhancement or edema is observed.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with normal biventricular dimensions and preserved systolic function. No evidence of myocardial scarring or subclinical hypertensive cardiomyopathy.

Cardiac MRI was performed on a 34-year-old pregnant female at 26 weeks gestation presenting with intermittent palpitations. Left ventricular dimensions are within normal limits for pregnancy (LVEDV 122 mL, LVESV 48 mL) with normal global and regional systolic function. The LVEF is calculated at 61%. Right ventricular size and function are likewise normal (RVEF 56%). There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging and no pathological late gadolinium enhancement is identified.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No structural heart disease, myocarditis, or localized myocardial injury identified to explain the patient's palpitations.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising from the right parietal dura, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The lesion is homogeneously hyperintense to gray matter on T2 sequences and demonstrates avid, uniform enhancement with a classic 'dural tail' sign. There is mild localized compression of the adjacent cerebral cortex and minimal surrounding edema.

Impression: Large, extra-axial, avidly enhancing right parietal mass, highly characteristic of a benign meningioma. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent parenchyma without midline shift.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a significantly enlarged posterior fossa. There is marked hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis, and a large CSF-density cyst communicates with the fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and torcular herophili are elevated. Sulcation patterns in the cerebral cortex are otherwise typical for 28 weeks. The lateral ventricles measure 10.2 mm at the atrium.

No other central nervous system anomalies are identified. The rest of the fetal body appears normal. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation. Recommend neurosurgical and genetic consultations to discuss prognosis and delivery planning.

Brain MRI reveals multiple well-defined, ovoid hyperintense lesions on T2 and FLAIR sequences within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several periventricular lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, demonstrating a classic Dawson's fingers morphology. Mild active enhancement is noted in two of the left frontal lobe lesions.

Impression: Demyelinating plaques demonstrating dissemination in space and time, consistent with active Multiple Sclerosis.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates symmetric and normal intracranial anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate opercularization of the sylvian fissures and normal primary sulcation for this age. The lateral ventricles are completely normal in caliber, with the atrial width measuring 6.0 mm. The corpus callosum and brainstem are fully intact.

Fetal abdomen, skeletal structures, and diaphragmatic contour are normal. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation showing normal cranial and extracranial organ development.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a distinct pattern of regional wall motion abnormality characterized by severe akinesis to dyskinesis of the mid-to-apical left ventricular segments with hyperkinesis of the basal segments. Left ventricular ejection fraction is acutely reduced at 38%. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates diffuse apical myocardial edema, but there is an absence of late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Classic apical ballooning syndrome (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy). The absence of late gadolinium enhancement suggests myocardial viability and supports the high likelihood of complete functional recovery.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation shows a single live fetus in cephalic presentation. The fetal brain demonstrates normal development, with sulcation and gyration patterns appropriate for a 28-week fetus. The lateral ventricular atrium measures 6.0 mm bilaterally, and the corpus callosum is intact and well-formed. The posterior fossa structures are normal.

The fetal chest and abdomen reveal normal visceral situs, with a well-expanded stomach and normal-appearing kidneys. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 28 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI reveals patchy, multifocal areas of subepicardial and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the lateral and inferolateral segments of the left ventricle. High signal intensity is also present in these regions on T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences, consistent with acute myocardial edema. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced (LVEF 49%) with regional hypokinesis matching the areas of LGE.

Impression: Findings are diagnostic of acute myocarditis. Given patient's history of systemic lupus erythematosus, this represents active lupus-associated cardiac involvement.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 30-year-old female for follow-up of peripartum cardiomyopathy diagnosed six months ago. There is notable improvement in left ventricular systolic function with LVEF now at 48% (previously 28%), and decreased left ventricular chamber volumes (LVEDD has decreased from 5.8 cm to 5.1 cm). No persistent myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement is visualized on current sequences.

Impression: Significant improvement in peripartum cardiomyopathy with resolving left ventricular dilation and recovery of systolic function, now demonstrating only mild residual left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, irregularly marginated mass in the right temporal lobe measuring 4.2 x 3.8 cm. The lesion shows thick, irregular rim enhancement with a central non-enhancing necrotic cavity. There is substantial surrounding vasogenic edema causing compression of the temporal horn of the right lateral ventricle and 6 mm of leftward midline shift.

Impression: High-grade necrotic mass in the right temporal lobe, highly suspicious for glioblastoma. Neurosurgical consultation is urgently indicated.

Cardiac MRI was performed on a 36-year-old female presenting with acute chest pain and dyspnea three days postpartum following a highly stressful delivery. There is severe hypokinesis to akinesis of the mid-to-apical segments of the left ventricle with hyperkinesis of the basal segments, resulting in a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%. T2-weighted imaging shows intense edema in the apical segments, but there is no late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) visualized.

Impression: Findings are classic for stress-induced (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy with transient apical ballooning, apical myocardial edema, and moderate-to-severe systolic dysfunction without focal necrosis or scarring. This represents a postpartum presentation of stress-induced cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal development of the fetal brain, spine, and chest. The cerebral cortex shows appropriate sylvian fissure opercularization and parieto-occipital sulcation expected for 24 weeks. The ventricles are normal in size, with symmetric atria measuring 6.1 mm. The posterior fossa, brainstem, and spinal cord are intact. No thoracic, cardiac, abdominal wall, or genitourinary abnormalities are noted.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 24 weeks gestation showing age-appropriate brain development and no identifiable structural anomalies.

High-resolution brain and internal auditory canal MR imaging was performed. The brain parenchyma is normal without focal lesions, mass effect, or signal anomalies. The eighth cranial nerve complexes are symmetric and normal in caliber within the internal auditory canals. Cerebellopontine angles are completely clear.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain and internal auditory canals. No mass lesion, acoustic neuroma, or ischemic changes identified.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced fetal cerebral maturation. Deep sulci and complex tertiary branching patterns are visualized throughout the frontal, temporal, and parietal lobes, entirely consistent with late third-trimester gestation. The ventricular atrium measures 6.5 mm on the left and 6.2 mm on the right, well within normal limits. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal.

The fetal visceral organs are in normal anatomical locations. Normal amounts of amniotic fluid are present. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate structural development and mature cortical folding for 36 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI demonstrates a dural-based, homogeneously enhancing extra-axial mass along the left cerebellopontine angle, measuring 2.3 x 2.0 cm. A prominent dural tail sign is identified. The mass exerts mild mass effect on the adjacent cerebellar hemisphere without significant fourth ventricular compression or hydrocephalus.

Impression: Left cerebellopontine angle dural-based mass, characteristic of a benign meningioma. Recommended management includes neurosurgical consultation and periodic follow-up imaging to monitor for interval growth.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. There is herniation of the liver, gallbladder, and loops of bowel into the right hemithorax, resulting in leftward mediastinal shift. The total fetal lung volume is reduced, with an observed-to-expected ratio of 42%. Fetal intracranial anatomy is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricles (atrium measuring 6.0 mm) and normal sulcation for 27 weeks.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant intrathoracic herniation of the liver, resulting in mediastinal shift and pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart size and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 75 mL/m² and the right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 72 mL/m², both of which are within normal range. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 66%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%.

No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal scars are demonstrated on cine or late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences. Intracardiac anatomy, including the atrial and ventricular septa, is fully intact. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation shows a morphologically normal fetus. The cerebral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 6.0 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum is intact. The cortical sulcation pattern is entirely normal for 30 weeks, demonstrating well-developed central and cingulate sulci with appropriate progress in operculization of the Sylvian fissures.

The posterior fossa structures, spine, and major organs of the chest, abdomen, and retroperitoneum are structurally normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 30 weeks gestation with normal intracranial architecture and appropriate sulcation development.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks 1 day gestation demonstrates bilateral symmetric ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 13.5 mm, and the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 13.2 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly. There is mild thinning of the posterior corpus callosum, though the structure is intact. The sulcation and gyral patterns are within normal limits for 30 weeks gestation, with normal operculization of the Sylvian fissures.

The fetal face, chest, abdominal organs, spine, and limbs are normal. Amniotic fluid volume is unremarkable. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly without secondary anomalies or cortical migration defects.

Cardiac MRI evaluates ischemic cardiomyopathy. There is severe global dilatation of the left ventricle with a large region of transmural myocardial infarction involving the apex, anterior, and anteroseptal segments. Cine imaging shows marked akinesis in these segments. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals greater than 75% transmural hyperenhancement in the LAD coronary territory.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with a large, transmural anterior and apical myocardial infarction. Overall left ventricular systolic function is severely reduced with an ejection fraction of 31%.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced third-trimester fetal brain development. Extensive secondary and tertiary sulci are visible, reflecting normal cortical maturation. The ventricular system is symmetric with lateral ventricular atrium measuring 6.0 mm. Brainstem and cerebellum are normal.

Fetal chest, kidneys, stomach, and bladder are well-visualized and within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with age-appropriate neurodevelopment and somatic anatomy.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks gestation shows completely normal fetal brain development. Symmetrical bilateral lateral ventricles are noted, with atrial widths measuring 5.8 mm on the left and 6.0 mm on the right. Appropriate early sulcation and opercularization for this stage of gestation are visualized, with no evidence of migration abnormalities.

The posterior fossa, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, is intact. Visualized fetal thorax and abdominal organs show normal anatomical relationships. Impression: Normal fetal brain and systemic anatomy for 22 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a severe focal narrowing of the descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, consistent with aortic coarctation. Flow-encoded velocity mapping shows high-velocity jetting across the coarctation site with a peak velocity of 3.8 m/s. Extensive collateral vessels are visualized arising from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries. The left ventricle shows mild concentric hypertrophy with normal systolic function (LVEF 58%).

Impression: Severe native coarctation of the descending thoracic aorta with significant collateralization. Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present with preserved systolic function.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a completely normal study. The cerebral structures, including the developing corpus callosum and cortical plates, show no anomalies. The temporal and sylvian opercularization are progressing normally for 24 weeks. The bilateral lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with an atrial width measuring 6.1 mm.

The fetal heart, chest, abdominal organs, spine, and bladder are fully developed and structurally intact. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 24 weeks with no structural, central nervous system, or abdominal anomalies.

Fetal magnetic resonance imaging was conducted at 26 weeks 0 days gestation to evaluate suspected intracranial anomalies. There is complete absence of the corpus callosum with classic colpocephaly, demonstrating teardrop-shaped configuration of the lateral ventricles and wide spacing of the frontal horns. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated. Gyral folding patterns appear normal for gestational age.

No other structural or thoracic abnormalities are noted. The abdominal anatomy is unremarkable. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. Postnatal developmental follow-up is recommended.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation shows normal structural development. The cerebral cortex shows robust and age-appropriate sulcation, including well-defined sylvian fissures, parieto-occipital sulci, and calcarine fissures. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrium measuring 5.8 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and vermis are normal in appearance and size.

All extracranial organs, including the fetal heart, stomach, kidneys, and bladder, demonstrate normal signal and morphology. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation with normal neurodevelopmental milestones.

Cardiac MRI was obtained to evaluate a 32-year-old postpartum female with new-onset heart failure symptoms. The left ventricle is severely dilated (end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m²) and demonstrates global hypokinesis, with a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 34%. Mild eccentric mitral regurgitation is noted, secondary to annular dilation. The right ventricle is at the upper limits of normal in size, with a mildly reduced ejection fraction of 45%.

T2-weighted and mapping sequences demonstrate subtle, diffuse myocardial edema without focal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Impression: Findings are highly consistent with acute peripartum cardiomyopathy. The absence of late gadolinium enhancement suggests a favorable prognosis for potential myocardial recovery with optimal medical therapy.

MRI of the brain shows unremarkable cerebral parenchyma. There are no abnormal areas of restricted diffusion, parenchymal signal abnormality, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are normal for the patient's age. Cranial nerve complexes and posterior fossa structures are normal, and major intracranial blood vessels demonstrate appropriate flow voids.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No evidence of demyelinating disease, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or intracranial mass lesions.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates entirely normal fetal development. The intracranial ventricular system is symmetric and non-dilated, with the lateral ventricular atrium measuring 5.2 mm. The corpus callosum is intact and appropriately configured for gestational age. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 20 weeks, presenting a mostly smooth cerebral surface with early sylvian indentations.

Fetal limbs, abdomen, spine, and chest show no morphological anomalies. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation showing expected intracranial anatomy and gestational-age-appropriate sulcation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked global dilation of the left ventricle with diffuse thinned walls and severe, global hypokinesis. The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 22%. Mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement is noted in the basal interventricular septum, typical for non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a reduced ejection fraction of 41%.

Impression: Severe bi-ventricular dilated cardiomyopathy of non-ischemic etiology, characterized by severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, chamber dilation, and mid-wall fibrosis.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals a right-sided diaphragmatic defect. The liver is partially herniated into the right thoracic cavity, displacing the heart and mediastinum to the left. The right lung is severely compressed and hypoplastic, with the left lung also showing mild compression. Intracranial anatomy is intact with appropriate sulcation for 31 weeks; the lateral ventricular atrium measures 6.5 mm.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with partial liver herniation and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

DWI and ADC maps show a large region of restricted diffusion involving the left insular cortex, frontoparietal operculum, and deep corona radiata, indicative of an acute ischemic stroke. T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is present but subtle, suggesting the infarct is within the subacute phase. Mass effect on the left lateral ventricle is mild.

Impression: Acute-to-subacute ischemic infarction in the distribution of the superior division of the left middle cerebral artery (MCA). No associated hemorrhagic transformation is visualized.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks 2 days gestation reveals normal anatomical structures. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate age-appropriate cortical sulcation and migrating neural elements. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric with an atrial width of 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum, brainstem, cerebellar vermis, and posterior fossa are normally developed.

Fetal chest, abdominal viscera, kidneys, and extremities appear intact and structurally appropriate. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 22 weeks 2 days gestation, showing normal cranial and extracranial development.

Evaluation of cardiac sarcoidosis. There is multi-segmental patchy late gadolinium enhancement involving the mid-myocardium and epicardium of the basal septum and anterior wall. T2-weighted imaging shows corresponding elevated signal in these areas, indicating active inflammation. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced (LVEF 47%).

Impression: Findings consistent with active cardiac sarcoidosis showing inflammation and associated myocardial scarring. Clinical correlation with extracardiac findings is recommended.

Brain MRI shows extensive subarachnoid hemorrhage within the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures, and anterior interhemispheric fissure. A companion magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) demonstrates a 6 mm lobulated aneurysm arising from the anterior communicating artery, projecting anteriorly.

Impression: Acute, diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage secondary to a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Urgent endovascular or neurosurgical intervention is required.

Cardiac MRI was performed for clinical screening due to a strong family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Cine imaging shows normal left ventricular wall thickness throughout, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 9 mm. The left ventricular cavity size is within normal limits, and the ejection fraction is calculated at 65% with no regional wall motion abnormalities or cavity obliteration.

Late gadolinium enhancement sequences are completely negative for myocardial scarring or focal fibrosis. Left and right atria are normal in size. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with no phenotypic features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. No scar or perfusion abnormalities identified.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks 4 days gestation reveals a significantly enlarged posterior fossa. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis, which is associated with a massive cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle communicating with the enlarged posterior fossa. The transverse cerebellar diameter is small for gestational age. Bilateral lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with the right atrium measuring 12.1 mm and the left measuring 11.9 mm.

The supratentorial brain is otherwise structurally intact. Visceral anatomy appears normal. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation. Associated moderate ventriculomegaly is present.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the interventricular septum measuring up to 2.1 cm in end-diastole, compared to a posterior wall thickness of 1.1 cm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. LVEF is hyperdynamic at 72%.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with prominent asymmetric septal hypertrophy and SAM of the mitral valve.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development. The lateral ventricular atrial widths are symmetric, measuring 5.9 mm, indicating no ventriculomegaly. Cortical folding and sulcation are entirely appropriate for 28 weeks, displaying well-developed sylvian fissures and early secondary sulci. The corpus callosum is intact and normal in thickness.

Fetal organs within the thorax and abdomen, including the lungs, heart, kidneys, and liver, are structurally unremarkable. The fetal spine is intact. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate anatomical and neurological maturation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates significant dilation of the lateral ventricles bilaterally. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.5 mm, and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 13.8 mm, indicative of moderate ventriculomegaly. There is associated thinning and mild stretching of the corpus callosum, though the structural pathway remains intact. The overlying cerebral cortex shows appropriate sulcal development and operculization for 28 weeks.

The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are unremarkable. No other fetal anomalies are identified. Impression: Bilateral moderate ventriculomegaly with secondary thinning of the corpus callosum. Suggest clinical follow-up and postnatal neurodevelopmental counseling.

Brain MRI demonstrates normal cerebral parenchymal signal intensity without evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for age. The major vascular flow voids are completely preserved, and there is no evidence of intracranial venous thrombosis or dural sinus abnormality.

Impression: Completely normal MRI of the brain. No structural or vascular pathology to explain the patient's gestational headaches.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe bileaflet mitral valve prolapse (Barlow's disease) with redundant, thickened leaflets. There is a prominent mitral annular disjunction (MAD) measuring 8.5 mm in the posterior mitral annulus. Quantitative flow analysis demonstrates a severe mitral regurgitant volume of 45 mL with a regurgitant fraction of 40%. The left atrium is severely dilated (volume index of 55 mL/m²), and the left ventricular ejection fraction is 60%.

Impression: Severe mitral valve prolapse with high-volume mitral regurgitation and significant mitral annular disjunction. Recommend close follow-up for potential surgical repair.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced fetal development. The cerebral cortex shows normal, extensive tertiary sulcation and gyration pattern appropriate for late third trimester. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with the atrium measuring 6.3 mm on both sides. The posterior fossa, corpus callosum, and brainstem are completely unremarkable.

All fetal thoracic and abdominal organs, including the lungs, heart, kidneys, bowel, and urinary bladder, are normal. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural and central nervous system development.

Cardiac MRI evaluating a systolic murmur in a pregnant female at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal cardiac structures. Left ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes are slightly elevated, consistent with normal maternal cardiovascular adaptation of pregnancy, and the LVEF is preserved at 60%. There is no evidence of valvular stenosis, and only trace physiologic regurgitation is observed at the mitral and tricuspid valves.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI showing expected physiological changes of pregnancy. No structural cardiac anomalies, shunt flow, or significant valvular pathologies are identified.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe skeletal dysplasia. All visualized fetal long bones (femur, humerus, radius, tibia) show severe, symmetric shortening (micromelia) and moderate bowing. The fetal thorax is narrow, bell-shaped, and severely constricted, with shortened ribs. Fetal lung volumes are mildly reduced secondary to thoracic constriction. 

Intracranial imaging is normal. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 27 weeks. The corpus callosum and ventricles (6.2 mm) are normal. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe micromelia and thoracic constriction, suspicious for thanatophoric dysplasia or osteogenesis imperfecta.

Cardiac MRI evaluated utilizing cine, perfusion, and viability sequences. The myocardium shows no abnormal signal intensity on T1-weighted, T2-weighted, or late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging. Normal left ventricular cavity size and wall thickness are noted. Global LV systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 60%. The right ventricle is normal in size and function (RVEF 56%). There is no evidence of valvular dysfunction or pericardial disease.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. There is no structural heart disease, myocardial ischemia, or scar tissue identified to explain the patient's atypical chest pain.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals skeletal findings highly suggestive of osteogenesis imperfecta or a skeletal dysplasia. There is marked shortening and angulation of all long bones, particularly the femurs and humeri, consistent with severe micromelia. Multiple rib fractures are identified, resulting in a narrow, bell-shaped thorax. Decreased skull mineralization is suspected due to extreme compressibility during imaging.

Intracranial anatomy demonstrates normal ventricular atria of 5.8 mm, with age-appropriate brain development. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe micromelia, narrow chest, and probable fractures, most suspicious for osteogenesis imperfecta type II or thanatophoric dysplasia.

Brain MRI demonstrates herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 8 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is effacement of the CSF space at the craniovertebral junction. Assessment of the cervical spine on sagittal scout views shows no evidence of syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with cerebellar tonsillar herniation measuring 8 mm. No associated cervical syrinx identified on these sequences.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation performed due to maternal obesity limiting ultrasound resolution. High-resolution multiplanar MR imaging demonstrates normal late-third-trimester fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows advanced sulcation, including deep secondary sulci matching expectations for 35 weeks. The ventricles are normal, with ventricular atria measuring 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is mature. The skull and intracranial spaces are unremarkable.

Fetal abdomen, thoracic structures, and extremities are fully visualized and morphologically normal. Amniotic fluid volume is within normal parameters. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation. No structural or developmental fetal anomalies detected.

MRI demonstrates a bicuspid aortic valve with fusion of the right and left coronary cusps. The valve leaflets are thickened and calcified with restricted systolic opening, giving a restricted aortic valve area of 0.9 cm2, indicative of severe aortic stenosis. There is post-stenotic dilatation of the ascending aorta, which measures 4.2 cm at its maximal diameter. The left ventricle is concentrically hypertrophied, with an LVEF of 60%.

Impression: Congenital bicuspid aortic valve with severe aortic stenosis. Dilatation of the ascending aorta and compensatory concentric left ventricular hypertrophy are present.

Cardiac MRI performed for clinical evaluation of ventricular arrhythmias and to rule out cardiac sarcoidosis. Biventricular chamber sizes, wall thickness, and regional wall motions are normal. Global systolic function is completely preserved with an LVEF of 61% and an RVEF of 54%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate no areas of myocardial scar, and T2 mapping reveals no evidence of active myocardial edema.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No structural features, regional dysfunction, or late gadolinium enhancement identified to support a diagnosis of cardiac sarcoidosis or other infiltrative cardiomyopathies.

Comprehensive cardiovascular MRI was performed. The ventricular morphology, myocardial thickness, and cavity sizes are all within normal limits. Both right and left ventricular contractility are robust, with a calculated LVEF of 64% and RVEF of 60%. There is no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement or abnormal myocardial signal on T2 mapping.

Impression: Entirely normal cardiac MRI. Normal structural anatomy and biventricular function, reassuring for clearance for athletic participation.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks 1 day gestation reveals significant dilation of both lateral ventricles. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 16.2 mm and the right measures 15.8 mm, indicating severe bilateral ventriculomegaly. There is secondary thinning of the white matter tracts and mild compression of the surrounding parenchyma. The third ventricle is minimally dilated, but the fourth ventricle and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Sulcation and gyral patterns are within expected limits for 32 weeks.

No underlying intracranial mass, hemorrhage, or neural tube defects are identified. Impression: Severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly without associated intracranial anomalies. Close clinical monitoring and postnatal pediatric neurosurgical evaluation are recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing cortical and subcortical mass within the right frontal lobe. The lesion is hyperintense on T2/FLAIR, hypointense on T1, and measures approximately 3.5 x 3.2 x 2.8 cm. There is minimal mass effect, with no midline shift. MR spectroscopy shows an elevated choline/creatine ratio and a depressed NAA peak.

Impression: Non-enhancing right frontal lobe intra-axial mass, highly suggestive of a low-grade glioma such as an oligodendroglioma or astrocytoma. Neuro-oncology referral is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a large lumbosacral myelomeningocele with an associated neural tube defect, extending from L3 to S2. There is posterior herniation of meninges and neural placode. Secondary intracranial features of Arnold-Chiari II malformation are present, including downward herniation of the cerebellar vermis, a small posterior fossa, and moderate ventriculomegaly with the atrial width measuring 11.5 mm.

Fetal extremities and skeletal elements demonstrate clubfoot deformities bilaterally. Impression: Open lumbosacral neural tube defect (myelomeningocele) and associated Chiari II malformation. Recommend multidisciplinary fetal care team evaluation.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI reveals multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, demonstrating a classic Dawson's fingers appearance. Following administration of gadolinium, two active lesions in the left frontal lobe demonstrate nodular enhancement, indicating areas of active, acute neuroinflammatory demyelination.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of a demyelinating process, meeting the McDonald criteria for dissemination in space and time. These findings strongly support a diagnosis of active Multiple Sclerosis. Correlation with cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large, circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 24 mm in maximum thickness adjacent to the posterolateral left ventricular wall. There is early diastolic collapse of the right atrium and transient diastolic flattening of the right ventricular free wall, indicative of elevated intrapericardial pressure. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 56%. No abnormal myocardial late gadolinium enhancement is identified.

Impression: Large, hemodynamically significant circumferential pericardial effusion with MRI features suggesting early cardiac tamponade. Immediate clinical evaluation is warranted.

Cardiac MRI shows a bicuspid aortic valve (type 1 configuration with fusion of the left and right coronary cusps). There is mild restriction of valvular opening, with planimetry demonstrating an aortic valve area of 1.7 cm2, and mild central aortic regurgitation is visualized. The ascending aorta is dilated, measuring 4.1 cm at the mid-ascending level. Left ventricular size, wall thickness, and systolic function are within normal limits (LVEF 60%).

Impression: Congenital bicuspid aortic valve with mild stenosis, mild regurgitation, and associated moderate dilation of the ascending thoracic aorta. Regular surveillance of the aortic dimensions is indicated.

Cardiac MRI shows a wall motion abnormality characterized by akinesis of the basal and mid-inferior segments of the left ventricle. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates a dense, transmural band of hyperenhancement (exceeding 90% wall thickness) involving the basal and mid-inferior walls, indicating a complete loss of viability in this territory. The left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 48%.

Impression: Chronic, non-viable, transmural myocardial infarction in the right coronary artery (RCA) territory. Associated mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Cine MRI reveals prominent trabeculations along the apical and lateral segments of the left ventricle. The ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium at end-diastole is measured at 2.4, which satisfies the diagnostic threshold for non-compaction. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly compromised with an LVEF of 46%, and there is mild global hypokinesis.

Impression: Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy with mild global systolic dysfunction. Close clinical surveillance for arrhythmias and thrombus formation is indicated.

Cardiac MRI demonstrating a moderate-to-large pericardial effusion. The effusion measures up to 1.8 cm adjacent to the right ventricle and posterior left ventricular wall. There is diastasis and mild diastolic collapse of the right ventricular free wall, indicative of elevated pericardial pressures. No active myocardial edema or abnormal late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the ventricular myocardium.

Impression: Moderate-to-large pericardial effusion with early hemodynamic features suggestive of tamponade physiology. Clinical correlation and close monitoring or pericardiocentesis should be considered.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation shows a normal single fetus. Brain structures, including the midline structures, are intact. The ventricular systems are symmetric and measure 6.2 mm at the atrium. The cortical sulcation is progressing normally with clearly visible cingulate and calcarine sulci. Both fetal lungs demonstrate normal T2 signal intensity and volume.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation showing normal fetal anatomy.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chambers with appropriate volumes and mass index. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. Wall motion is normal, with no regional wall motion abnormalities or perfusion defects. No late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is seen on post-contrast imaging.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial infarction, fibrosis, or dynamic perfusion abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI shows normal left and right ventricular anatomy and function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, with an end-diastolic volume of 124 mL. The right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%, with an end-diastolic volume of 118 mL. No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal thinning of the ventricular walls are demonstrated.

Myocardial T1 and T2 mapping parameters are within normal reference ranges. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates no focal areas of hyperenhancement to suggest scar, fibrosis, or active inflammation. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study with no structural, functional, or tissue abnormalities identified.

Cardiac MRI of a pregnant patient with Marfan syndrome at 18 weeks gestation. The aortic root is dilated, measuring 4.6 cm at the level of the sinuses of Valsalva, with the tubular ascending aorta measuring 3.4 cm. Compared to pre-pregnancy imaging, there is no significant change in dimensions. Aortic valve leaflet excursion is normal, with trace aortic regurgitation on phase-contrast sequences.

Impression: Dilated aortic root in a pregnant patient with Marfan syndrome, stable relative to prior examination. Continued close clinical and echocardiographic monitoring is recommended throughout the remainder of pregnancy.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal exam. The brain structures are symmetric. The lateral ventricles measure 5.9 mm at the atrium. The corpus callosum is intact and appropriately formed. The cortical sulcation pattern shows expected early sulcation of the parieto-occipital fissures and Sylvian fissures, which is highly appropriate for 24 weeks.

The posterior fossa, face, chest, heart, abdomen, and spine show no structural abnormalities. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing expected central nervous system development and visceral anatomy for 24 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI shows multiple oval-shaped T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles (Dawson's fingers) within the periventricular and juxtacortical white matter. Several of these lesions demonstrate restricted diffusion, and two lesions in the left frontal lobe display nodular contrast enhancement post-gadolinium administration, indicating active demyelination.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with active demyelinating disease. Given the dissemination in space and time, this strongly supports a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis.

MR imaging of the sella turcica demonstrates a hypoenhancing, well-circumscribed nodule in the left lateral aspect of the anterior pituitary gland, measuring approximately 6 mm in diameter. The pituitary stalk is minimally deviated to the right. The optic chiasm is structurally normal and free of compression, and the cavernous sinuses are uninvolved.

Impression: Pituitary microadenoma measuring 6 mm, localized to the left adenohypophysis, consistent with patient's clinical history of hyperprolactinemia.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates isolated cerebellar vermian hypoplasia. The cerebellar vermis is small and abnormally rotated, but the posterior fossa itself is not significantly enlarged, which is characteristic of a Dandy-Walker variant or isolated vermian hypoplasia. The brainstem is normal in caliber. Lateral ventricular atrial measurements are normal at 7.0 mm, and the cerebral sulcation is age-appropriate.

All other fetal organs and the spine are structurally normal. Impression: Fetal cerebellar vermian hypoplasia without severe posterior fossa enlargement, consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant or isolated vermian hypoplasia.

Brain MRI performed for atypical migraine. The cerebral hemispheres are normal in signal intensity, with no evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, mass, or demyelinating process. The ventricles and extra-axial spaces are symmetric and clear. The vascular flow voids at the base of the skull are preserved without focal stenosis or occlusion.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No intracranial pathology or structural abnormality is visualized.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a dorsal neural tube defect. There is a prominent myelomeningocele sac arising from the lumbosacral region spanning from L4 to S2, with herniation of meninges and neural elements. The cranial evaluation reveals classic features of Chiari II malformation, including a small posterior fossa, herniation of the cerebellar tonsils (banana sign), and bifrontal narrowing (lemon sign). Moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly is noted, with the atria measuring 11.2 mm on the left and 10.9 mm on the right.

The remainder of the fetal visceral structures are grossy normal. Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly. Recommend referral to a maternal-fetal medicine center for consideration of prenatal repair.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation. The cerebellar vermis is hypoplastic and mildly rotated upward, with a keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and the posterior fossa fluid space. The posterior fossa is mildly enlarged, but there is no massive cystic expansion. Sulcation is normal for 28 weeks, and the lateral ventricles are normal, measuring 6.8 mm bilaterally.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (isolated inferior vermian hypoplasia) without associated ventriculomegaly.

Myocardial cine imaging shows pronounced prolapse of the posterior leaflet (P2 segment) of the mitral valve into the left atrium during systole. This is associated with a prominent, eccentric regurgitant jet. Velocity-encoded phase-contrast sequences confirm severe mitral regurgitation. The left atrium is dilated, while left ventricular systolic function remains hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 64%.

Impression: Severe mitral regurgitation secondary to posterior leaflet mitral valve prolapse (myxomatous degeneration). Left atrial dilation is present; close clinical monitoring for surgical intervention criteria is advised.

Cardiac MRI reveals marked asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal wall thickness measuring 2.3 cm. There is dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 72%. Late gadolinium enhancement is noted at the right ventricular anterior and posterior insertion points.

Impression: Classic phenotypic findings of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with hyperdynamic LV function and characteristic focal fibrosis at the insertion junctions.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The liver herniates extensively into the right hemithorax, causing a significant leftward shift of the heart and mediastinum. Left lung volume is moderately reduced; estimated total lung volume is 42% of expected for gestational age, indicative of moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial anatomy is structurally normal with appropriate late third-trimester sulcation and normal ventricular size (6.1 mm). Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 74-year-old female with worsening dyspnea on exertion. The aortic valve is trileaflet but demonstrates severe calcification and restricted leaflet excursion. Planimetry of the aortic valve orifice during systole yields an aortic valve area (AVA) of 0.7 cm². Velocity-encoded imaging across the aortic valve demonstrates a peak velocity of 4.3 m/s, consistent with severe aortic stenosis. Left ventricular mass is increased reflecting concentric hypertrophy, with preserved LVEF at 55%.

Impression: Severe calcific aortic stenosis with an aortic valve area of 0.7 cm² and concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved.

MR brain imaging obtained in a 33-year-old female post-partum patient who experienced generalized seizures. High T2 and FLAIR signal is seen predominantly within the subcortical white matter and overlying cortex of the bilateral occipital and parietal lobes. These lesions display no significant restricted diffusion on ADC maps, confirming vasogenic edema.

Impression: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), classically seen in severe preeclampsia/eclampsia. No acute cerebral infarction or intraparenchymal hemorrhage.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with a history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. There is severe, free pulmonary valve regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 42%. The right ventricle is severely dilated, with an end-diastolic volume index of 155 mL/m2. Right ventricular systolic function is moderately reduced with an ejection fraction of 39%.

Impression: Post-repair Tetralogy of Fallot presenting with severe pulmonary regurgitation and secondary severe right ventricular dilation and dysfunction. Findings are supportive of evaluation for pulmonary valve replacement.

Brain MRI and MRA demonstrate acute subarachnoid hemorrhage, characterized by hyperintense signal within the basal cisterns and right Sylvian fissure on FLAIR sequences, with corresponding susceptibility artifact on SWI. The magnetic resonance angiogram (MRA) demonstrates a 5 mm lobulated aneurysm arising from the right middle cerebral artery bifurcation.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage centered in the right Sylvian fissure and basal cisterns, secondary to a ruptured right MCA bifurcation aneurysm. Neurosurgical intervention is urgently required.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked asymmetric septal hypertrophy of the left ventricle, with a maximal septal wall thickness of 21 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, leading to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Contrast enhancement sequences show patchy mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) concentrated in the hypertrophied septal segments, suggesting myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with dynamic LVOT obstruction, significant septal hypertrophy (21 mm), and corresponding mid-myocardial fibrosis. Hyperdynamic left ventricular systolic function is noted with an EF of 72%.

Brain MRI shows patchy, bilateral, relatively symmetric areas of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity localized to the subcortical white matter and cortex of the occipital and parietal lobes.
