Impression: Constellation of findings is classic for idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH / pseudotumor cerebri). Correlation with lumbar puncture opening pressure and ophthalmologic evaluation is advised.

MRI of the brain and sella turcica demonstrates a well-circumscribed, hypo-enhancing mass measuring 1.2 x 1.4 x 1.1 cm within the left aspect of the pituitary gland. The lesion causes mild upward deviation of the optic chiasm and lateral deviation of the infundibular stalk, without invasion of the cavernous sinuses.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with mild optic chiasm compression. Correlation with prolactin and other endocrine levels is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm, and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 10.5 mm. No intraventricular hemorrhage or aqueductal obstruction is identified. The corpus callosum is intact, and the cerebellar hemispheres and vermis are normal in size and signal intensity.

Fetal chest and abdomen are unremarkable. Impression: Mild, isolated bilateral ventriculomegaly. Recommend serial follow-up ultrasounds to monitor the ventricular size and evaluate for progression.

Cardiac MRI performed for cardiac monitoring during cardiotoxic chemotherapy surveillance reveals normal left and right ventricular volumes and systolic function. The LVEF is 59%, unchanged from the baseline pre-treatment evaluation. Native T1 values are within the normal reference range, and there is no evidence of myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular function and no signs of chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity or myocardial fibrosis.

Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the brain demonstrates normal intracranial structures. The ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal physiological limits. There are no areas of abnormal enhancement or signal abnormality within the cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, or cerebellum. The pituitary gland and optic chiasm appear normal.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No evidence of focal lesions, abnormal contrast enhancement, or acute vascular territory infarction.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates findings highly suggestive of a severe skeletal dysplasia. There is marked, symmetric shortening of all long bones (micromelia), with the femurs and humeri measuring well below the 3rd percentile for gestational age. The thorax is severely narrow and bell-shaped, with significant pulmonary compression. The spine shows diffuse platyspondyly but intact alignment. Intracranial evaluation demonstrates a relatively large skull with frontal bossing, but normal brain parenchymal development. Sulcation is normal for 28 weeks, and the ventricular atrium measures 7.0 mm.

Fetal abdominal viscera are unremarkable, but polyhydramnios is noted. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, characterized by micromelia, bell-shaped narrow thorax, and frontal bossing, most consistent with a thanatophoric dysplasia or severe achondroplasia.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, with the atrial width measuring 11.5 mm. The lateral ventricles are widely spaced and run parallel to each other. The sulcation pattern demonstrates radial arrangement of the gyri along the medial hemispheric wall.

The remainder of the brain parenchymal development is age-appropriate. No associated facial or extracranial anomalies are detected. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly.

Cardiac MRI shows severe, global dilatation of the left ventricle with a diastolic diameter of 6.5 cm. Diffuse hypokinesis is present, resulting in a severely depressed left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates a thin, linear mid-myocardial stripe of hyperenhancement in the basal-to-mid interventricular septum, characteristic of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction. The pattern of mid-wall LGE is consistent with a non-ischemic etiology.

Fetal MRI performed at 36 weeks gestation for persistent breech presentation and planning of delivery. Highly detailed imaging demonstrates advanced cortical development of the fetal brain. There are deeply formed central, precentral, and postcentral sulci, as well as secondary and tertiary cortical gyration patterns perfectly appropriate for a 36-week fetus. The lateral ventricular atria measure 5.5 mm bilaterally, and the corpus callosum and posterior fossa are structurally normal.

Fetal chest, lungs, abdominal viscera, and spine are fully mature and unremarkable. Normal amniotic fluid and intact placenta are noted. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating completely normal, age-appropriate intracranial maturation and fetal visceral anatomy.

Brain MRI shows a crescent-shaped, extra-axial fluid collection along the right frontoparietal convexity, measuring approximately 1.2 cm in maximal width. The collection displays heterogeneous high T1 and T2 signal, consistent with a subacute subdural hematoma. There is a 5 mm leftward midline shift and mild compression of the right lateral ventricle.

Impression: Subacute right-sided subdural hematoma causing mild-to-moderate mass effect and midline shift. Neurosurgical consultation is advised.

High-resolution imaging of the cranial nerves demonstrates normal course, caliber, and signal intensity of the bilateral trigeminal nerves within the prepontine cistern and Meckel's cave. No vascular loops are seen abutting or distorting the root entry zones. The brainstem and cerebral hemispheres are completely normal without focal lesions.

Impression: Normal high-resolution MRI of the brain and trigeminal nerves. No evidence of neurovascular conflict or structural etiology for facial pain.

Brain MRI demonstrates moderate-to-severe bilateral, confluent FLAIR/T2 hyperintensities in the periventricular and subcortical white matter. These changes are symmetric and reflect chronic microvascular ischemic disease. There are no acute infarcts or parenchymal microhemorrhages. Prominent perivascular spaces and mild generalized cortical volume loss are also noted.

Impression: Moderate-to-severe chronic microvascular white matter changes. No acute intracranial territorial infarction or hemorrhage is identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates asymmetric septal hypertrophy, most prominent in the basal to mid-ventricular septum, with a maximum wall thickness of 21 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve leading to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, with an estimated peak instantaneous gradient of 42 mmHg. The left ventricular volume is normal, but hyperdynamic, yielding an LVEF of 74%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows patchy, mid-wall enhancement at the anterior and posterior RV insertion points.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with classic distribution of septal hypertrophy and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Pathological LGE at the RV insertion points represents myocardial fibrosis, which carries prognostic significance.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation. There is partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with the posterior body and splenium absent. The anterior rostrum and genu are present but thin. There is mild ventriculomegaly affecting the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), measuring 11.2 mm on the left and 10.5 mm on the right. Normal cortical migration and early sulcation are present.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly.

Cardiac MRI demonstrating asymmetric septal hypertrophy with a maximum interventricular septal thickness of 22 mm at the mid-ventricular level. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral leaflet causing mild left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, with a peak gradient estimated at 25 mmHg. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows patchy, non-ischemic hyperenhancement localized to the RV-LV insertion points.

Impression: Phenotypic presentation of asymmetric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with mild LVOT obstruction and focal replacement fibrosis. Left ventricular ejection fraction is elevated at 74% (hyperdynamic).

Cardiac MRI evaluates atypical chest pain in a 48-year-old female. Cine images demonstrate a significant myocardial bridge of the mid-left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery, which is compressed during systole. There is no evidence of inducible myocardial ischemia on adenosine stress perfusion imaging, and no late gadolinium enhancement is identified in the corresponding LAD territory. LVEF is preserved at 62%.

Impression: Mid-LAD myocardial bridging causing systolic compression, but without evidence of inducible myocardial perfusion defects or myocardial infarction on MRI stress testing.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates herniation of stomach and bowel loops into the left hemithorax, consistent with congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The heart is displaced into the right hemithorax. The observed lung-to-head ratio (LHR) is calculated to assess pulmonary hypoplasia risk. Fetal brain evaluation demonstrates a normal ventricular system with atrial measurements of 5.9 mm and normal early parieto-occipital sulcation matching 23 weeks.

No additional musculoskeletal abnormalities are noted. Moderate polyhydramnios is present. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with mediastinal shift and associated moderate risk for pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with the posterior body and splenium not visualized. There is mild enlargement of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), measuring 10.2 mm. Cerebral sulcation is normal. The cerebellum, vermis, and brainstem appear intact. Visualized fetal chest and abdominal viscera are structurally normal.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly.

MR imaging demonstrates a broad-based, extra-axial, dural-based mass along the left sphenoid wing measuring 2.4 x 2.2 x 2.0 cm. The mass is isointense to cortex on T1 and T2 sequences and shows intense, homogeneous enhancement post-contrast with a prominent dural tail. There is mild localized mass effect on the adjacent left temporal lobe, but no significant surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Left sphenoid wing dural-based mass highly characteristic of a meningioma. No acute mass effect or herniation is identified.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates severe shortening of all long bones of the upper and lower extremities, consistent with micromelia. The fetal thorax is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, while the abdomen is protuberant, raising high concern for pulmonary hypoplasia. The skull shows mild frontal bossing.

Evaluation of the fetal brain reveals normal development for gestational age, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.1 mm and normal sulcation. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with micromelia and narrow thorax, highly characteristic of a thanatophoric dysplasia or severe osteogenesis imperfecta. Genetic counseling and prenatal neonatology consultation are recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates marked ventriculomegaly involving the lateral and third ventricles, which is out of proportion to the degree of cerebral sulcal enlargement. There is rounding of the frontal horns and a stretched corpus callosum. Periventricular halo of high FLAIR signal is present, representing transependymal CSF migration. The aqueduct of Sylvius shows a prominent flow void.

Impression: Prominent ventriculomegaly disproportionate to cortical atrophy, highly suggestive of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence is advised.

MRI of the brain was performed using multiplanar T1, T2, FLAIR, and DWI sequences. The cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, and brainstem demonstrate normal morphology and signal intensity. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or hydrocephalus. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces are normal.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No acute intracranial process or chronic structural abnormality is seen.

Brain MRI demonstrates bilateral distension of the perioptic subarachnoid space with flattening of the posterior sclera and intraocular protrusion of the optic nerve heads. Additionally, there is partial emptiness of the sella turcica ("empty sella") and mild bilateral narrowing of the transverse venous sinuses. No space-occupying lesions or hydrocephalus are identified.

Impression: Structural findings classic for idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri). Correlation with opening pressure on lumbar puncture is advised.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. The fetal brain shows appropriate configuration with a thin subplate and early parieto-occipital fissure development. The lateral ventricles are normal, measuring 6.2 mm at the atrium.

The spinal canal and cord are normal. Impression: Unremarkable 22-week fetal MRI with normal intracranial structures.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals a significant lumbosacral neural tube defect. There is a prominent myelomeningocele sac projecting from the posterior elements of the lower lumbar spine, measuring 2.4 cm. An associated Chiari II malformation is visualized, with caudal displacement of the cerebellar vermis and medulla through the foramen magnum. The lateral ventricles are dilated, with atrial diameters measuring 12.8 mm.

The brain sulcation is early and appropriate for 22 weeks. The fetal chest and abdomen are otherwise normal. Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly. Consultation with fetal therapy and neurosurgery is advised.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a bicuspid aortic valve (fusion of the right and left coronary cusps) with restricted systolic opening. Velocity mapping across the aortic valve demonstrates a peak velocity of 3.8 m/s, consistent with moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis. There is mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septal thickness 1.3 cm) and dilation of the ascending aorta measuring 4.1 cm.

Impression: Congenital bicuspid aortic valve presenting with moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis and associated ascending aortic dilation. Preserved LVEF at 58%.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach and several loops of small bowel have herniated through a posterior left diaphragmatic defect into the left hemithorax. This herniation causes a significant mediastinal shift to the right, compressing the fetal heart and severely restricting the development of the left lung. The observed lung-to-head ratio (LHR) is reduced.

Fetal brain anatomy and ventricles are normal, with an atrial measurement of 5.5 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with severe mediastinal shift and pulmonary hypoplasia. Close monitoring is recommended.

Fetal MRI performed at 23 weeks 3 days gestation reveals a complete absence of both kidneys in the renal fossae. The adrenal glands are present but lie flat along the posterior abdominal wall (laying-down adrenal sign). There is severe oligohydramnios (anhydramnios), which limits resolution but is clearly demonstrated by the lack of amniotic fluid signal. The fetal bladder is not visualized, indicating absence of fetal urine production. The fetal lungs are small, and the chest is narrowed, suggesting secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and signs of pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence).

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked dilatation of the left ventricle with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume of 185 mL/m² and severely depressed systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 28%. There is global hypokinesis of the left ventricle without segmental wall motion abnormalities. No significant late gadolinium enhancement is identified to suggest myocardial scarring or focal necrosis.

Impression: Severely dilated left ventricle with global dysfunction, highly consistent with peripartum cardiomyopathy in this postpartum patient. No evidence of myocardial infarction or focal fibrosis.

Brain MRI shows a crescentic extra-axial fluid collection along the right frontoparietal convexity measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal thickness. The collection is hyperintense on T2 and iso-to-hyperintense on T1, suggesting a subacute to chronic subdural hematoma. There is substantial mass effect with partial compression of the right lateral ventricle and 8 mm of leftward midline shift.

Impression: Large subacute to chronic right frontoparietal subdural hematoma with significant mass effect and midline shift. Neurosurgical evaluation is indicated.

Postpartum brain MRI demonstrates diffuse, smooth, pachymeningeal (dural) enhancement after gadolinium administration. There is mild sagging of the brainstem, inferior displacement of the optic chiasm, and engorgement of the dural venous sinuses, with mild bilateral subdural fluid collections. No parenchymal focal lesions or infarcts are identified.

Impression: Diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement and sagging brainstem, characteristic of intracranial hypotension (often secondary to post-lumbar puncture headache or spontaneous CSF leak). Clinical correlation with orthostatic headache is advised.

MRI of the brain reveals marked enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, with disproportionate narrowing of the sulci at the high cerebral convexities (DESH pattern). There is prominent rounding of the frontal horns and bowing of the corpus callosum. Mild transependymal flow of CSF is visualized. The fourth ventricle is mildly enlarged.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal enlargement, highly suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). Clinical correlation with gait, cognitive, and urinary symptoms is suggested.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates completely normal cardiac architecture and ventricular function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, with an end-diastolic volume index of 70 mL/m². The right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%, with an end-diastolic volume index of 66 mL/m². No regional wall motion abnormalities or wall thinning are noted.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no evidence of myocardial necrosis, scarring, or infiltration. T1 and T2 mapping values are within normal reference ranges. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular size and function, and no evidence of tissue-level pathology.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 32-year-old postpartum female presenting with acute shortness of breath. The left ventricle is severely dilated with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 122 mL/m2. There is global hypokinesis of the left ventricular free wall and septum. The calculated left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is severely depressed at 28%. No focal areas of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are identified to suggest myocardial scar or infarction.

Impression: Clinical and imaging findings are highly consistent with peripartum cardiomyopathy. Markedly reduced systolic function and left ventricular dilatation are noted without evidence of myocardial fibrosis.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks 5 days gestation demonstrates normal third-trimester anatomical development. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, with advanced operculization and complex sulcation patterns, including well-defined central and precentral sulci consistent with late third-trimester transition. The lateral ventricles are slender, with the atria measuring 6.0 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum and brainstem are morphologically normal. The cisterna magna is clear, measuring 5.9 mm, with an intact cerebellar vermis.

Fetal soft tissues, facial features, long bones, spine, and intra-abdominal viscera are within normal limits. Normal amniotic fluid volume and posteriorly located fundal placenta are noted. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate brain development and normal anatomy.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, spleen, and several loops of small bowel have herniated into the left hemithorax, resulting in a severe mediastinal shift to the right. The left lung is severely compressed and barely visible, while the right lung is also compressed with a measured lung volume below the 5th percentile for gestational age, suggesting high risk for pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain shows normal biometry and normal ventricular measurements (6.0 mm).

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with severe mediastinal shift and signs of severe bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia. Close multidisciplinary monitoring is indicated.

Brain MRI and MRA of the circle of Willis were performed for screening due to a strong family history of intracranial aneurysms. There is no evidence of saccular aneurysm, arteriovenous malformation, or other vascular abnormality. The brain parenchyma is normal with no mass lesions, ischemia, or hemorrhage.

Impression: Normal MR brain and MR angiogram of the head. No intracranial aneurysms or vascular malformations are identified.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation demonstrates a Dandy-Walker variant. There is mild to moderate hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, resulting in a keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and an enlarged cisterna magna. The posterior fossa CSF space is moderately dilated, but the tentorium and torcular herophili are not elevated. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits (atrium 7.5 mm).

Cerebral cortical sulcation is completely appropriate for 33 weeks gestation. No other structural defects are identified. Impression: Fetal Dandy-Walker variant (cerebellar vermian hypoplasia) with enlarged posterior fossa space, without supratentorial ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The splenium is completely absent, while the rostrum and body appear intact. This is associated with mild asymmetric ventriculomegaly; the left ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right ventricular atrium measures 8.5 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 31 weeks.

No other developmental brain defects are identified. The fetal thorax and abdomen are unremarkable. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild left ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with the posterior body and splenium absent. There is associated mild ventriculomegaly with the occipital horns measuring 11.8 mm. The anterior aspects of the corpus callosum are preserved. Cortical gyration is appropriate for 31 weeks.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum and mild colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks 3 days gestation reveals semilobar holoprosencephaly. There is partial fusion of the cerebral hemispheres anteriorly, with a single, large monoventricle and partially fused thalami. The corpus callosum and cavum septum pellucidum are absent. The sulcation pattern of the existing cerebral tissue is abnormal and simplified. Facial structures demonstrate mild hypotelorism but no clefting.

The fetal spine, chest, and abdomen are unremarkable. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Semilobar holoprosencephaly characterized by a monoventricle, fused thalami, and absent corpus callosum.

MR imaging of the brain and craniocervical junction reveals cerebellar tonsillar ectopia, with the tonsils projecting approximately 7 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. There is crowding of the craniocervical junction with effacement of the surrounding CSF spaces. No evidence of syrinx formation is noted within the visualized cervical spinal cord.

Impression: Chiari I malformation, characterized by 7 mm of cerebellar tonsillar descent. No cervical syrinx or associated hydrocephalus.

Cardiac MRI of a 29-year-old female in her third trimester of pregnancy (34 weeks) presenting with progressive dyspnea and lower extremity edema. The study reveals mild biatrial and left ventricular dilatation. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is elevated at 105 mL/m2. Cine imaging demonstrates global left ventricular hypokinesis with a calculated ejection fraction of 38%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality or myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging. No late gadolinium enhancement is identified, which is consistent with a non-ischemic etiology.

Impression: Left ventricular dysfunction and mild chamber dilation, highly suggestive of peripartum cardiomyopathy. Continued close clinical monitoring and postpartum follow-up are recommended.

Dedicated imaging of the sella turcica demonstrates a hypoenhancing, well-circumscribed lesion measuring 5.5 x 4.8 mm within the left lateral aspect of the anterior pituitary gland. There is mild tilt of the pituitary stalk to the right, but no compression of the optic chiasm. The cavernous sinuses are bilaterally symmetrical and clear of invasion.

Impression: Left-sided pituitary microadenoma, correlating with clinical presentation of amenorrhea and elevated prolactin levels. No mass effect on the optic chiasm or cavernous sinuses.

MRI of the brain demonstrates patchy, bilateral, relatively symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensities primarily localized within the subcortical white matter and cortex of the parieto-occipital lobes. There is no evidence of restricted diffusion on DWI/ADC sequences, pointing toward vasogenic rather than cytotoxic edema. No mass effect, midline shift, or acute intracranial hemorrhage is observed. The ventricular system and basal cisterns remain within normal limits.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES), particularly in the clinical context of postpartum preeclampsia. Correlate clinically with blood pressure monitoring and neurological status. No acute cerebral infarction is identified.

High-resolution cardiac MRI demonstrating normal biventricular dimensions, wall thickness, and systolic function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of focal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are identified. Valvular structures appear morphologically normal with physiological trace regurgitation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study showing no structural, functional, or tissue characterization abnormalities.

Dedicated pituitary and brain MRI demonstrates a well-circumscribed, solid mass arising from the adenohypophysis, measuring 1.4 x 1.2 x 1.1 cm. The lesion demonstrates intermediate signal on T1, high signal on T2, and heterogeneous enhancement post-contrast. There is mild superior extension into the suprasellar cistern, but the optic chiasm is not compressed and remains structurally intact.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with mild suprasellar extension. No direct compression of the optic chiasm is observed.

A 24-year-old female was referred for cardiac MRI screening due to a strong family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Imaging demonstrates entirely normal left ventricular wall thickness (maximum 9 mm in the septum) and normal chamber volumes. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 63%. There is no evidence of systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, and no late gadolinium enhancement is present.

Impression: Normal screening cardiac MRI with no phenotypic evidence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or structural myocardial disease. Continued clinical surveillance is recommended based on genetic status.

Brain MRI demonstrates cerebellar tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum measuring approximately 7.5 mm. The cerebellar tonsils are pointed (peg-like) in morphology. There is mild effacement of the CSF spaces at the craniocervical junction. The ventricular system is normal in size and configuration, and no cervical syrinx is noted on the visualized cervical spine sequences.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7.5 mm of tonsillar ectopia, without evidence of associated hydrocephalus or syringomyelia on current imaging.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows completely normal fetal brain development. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, with the lateral ventricles measuring 6.1 mm at the level of the atrium. The corpus callosum is fully formed and appropriate in thickness. The cortical sulcation is highly appropriate for 32 weeks, displaying well-demarcated parieto-occipital, central, and cingulate sulci, along with advanced operculization of the Sylvian fissures.

The posterior fossa, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, is morphologically normal. Visualized fetal chest, abdomen, pelvis, and musculoskeletal structures show no abnormalities. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating completely normal, age-appropriate intracranial development and sulcation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 36-year-old female with a history of breast cancer treated with anthracycline-based chemotherapy, presenting with progressive fatigue. The left ventricle is moderately dilated with global hypokinesis. The left ventricular ejection fraction is significantly reduced at 35% (previously 55% prior to therapy). T2 mapping values are normal, and late gadolinium enhancement is negative, indicating the absence of macroscopic myocardial scar.

Impression: Moderate non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, consistent with anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity. There is no evidence of myocardial scar or active myocarditis on tissue characterization.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals severe, near-complete oligohydramnios, significantly limiting fetal movement and image resolution. Both fetal renal fossae are empty, and there is no visualization of the fetal kidneys or urinary bladder, consistent with bilateral renal agenesis. The fetal lungs are severely compressed, and the thorax is narrow, indicating advanced pulmonary hypoplasia. Intracranial structures, including the brain parenchyma and ventricles, are intact but compressed.

The musculoskeletal system demonstrates severe crowding artifacts. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe oligohydramnios and severe secondary pulmonary hypoplasia, compatible with Potter sequence.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates normal structural development. There is symmetric opercularization of both sylvian fissures, and the parieto-occipital and calcarine sulci are well-defined, appropriate for 29 weeks. The lateral ventricles are within normal parameters, with the atrium measuring 6.5 mm symmetrically. The midline structures, including the corpus callosum and pituitary, are unremarkable.

No extracranial soft tissue anomalies, cardiac abnormalities, or bowel dilations are observed. Amniotic fluid is normal. Impression: Normal fetal brain and bodily development at 29 weeks gestation with no abnormalities identified.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 35-year-old female at 32 weeks gestation with a known congenital bicuspid aortic valve and clinical suspicion of worsening stenosis. There is a bicuspid aortic valve with fusion of the left and right coronary cusps. The valve leaflets are moderately thickened and calcified with restricted opening. Velocity-encoded imaging across the aortic valve reveals a peak velocity of 3.4 m/s, translating to a peak gradient of approximately 46 mmHg. Left ventricular wall thickness is mildly increased (12 mm) and systolic function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 58%.

Impression: Moderate aortic stenosis associated with a congenital bicuspid aortic valve in a third-trimester pregnant patient. Left ventricular systolic function remains well-preserved without evidence of decompensation.

Cardiac MRI was requested as a baseline assessment during cardiotoxic chemotherapy for breast cancer. Left ventricular dimensions and wall thickness are normal. The left ventricular ejection fraction is completely preserved at 61% (baseline was 62%). No regional hypokinesis, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with well-preserved biventricular size and function. No evidence of chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity at this time.

Dedicated thin-section MRI of the pituitary gland and hypothalamus demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology. The pituitary gland is symmetric, measuring 6.2 mm in height, with an upright infundibulum and preserved posterior pituitary bright spot. No focal hypoenhancing lesions are noted post-contrast.

Impression: Normal MRI of the pituitary gland and hypothalamus. No evidence of pituitary microadenoma or stalk lesion in this patient presenting with hyperprolactinemia.

Cardiac MRI for surveillance in a patient with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot demonstrates severe, free pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 44%. There is moderate-to-severe dilatation of the right ventricle, with an indexed RV end-diastolic volume (RVEDVI) of 152 mL/m². The right ventricular systolic function is mildly reduced (RVEF 42%). The left ventricle demonstrates normal size and function (LVEF 58%). No significant RV outflow tract obstruction is observed.

Impression: Severe pulmonary regurgitation leading to moderate-to-severe right ventricular dilatation and mild right ventricular dysfunction, typical of late post-repair Tetralogy of Fallot.

MRI of the internal auditory canals and brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed, enhancing, ice-cream cone-shaped mass measuring 1.6 x 1.2 cm centered in the left cerebellopontine angle, extending into the left internal auditory canal. The mass causes widening of the canal and exerts mild mass effect on the adjacent brainstem.

Impression: Left vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma). High-resolution follow-up or neurosurgical evaluation is advised.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial and systemic anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate sulcation and opercularization for 27 weeks. The ventricular system is symmetric with lateral ventricular atrial widths measuring 6.0 mm.

No fetal anomalies are visualized in the chest or abdomen. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with normal lateral ventricular size and age-appropriate sulculation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular dimensions, myocardial wall thicknesses, and systolic function. The calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 65%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or perfusion defects are present. Post-contrast late gadolinium enhancement images show no evidence of focal myocardial scar, infiltration, or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular size and biventricular function with no evidence of myocardial injury, scarring, or active inflammatory process.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a large multicystic mass in the left renal fossa, consistent with a unilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The left kidney is non-functional and replaced by multiple non-communicating cysts. The contralateral right kidney is normal in size, position, and parenchymal signal, showing compensatory hypertrophy. Amniotic fluid volume is completely normal.

The fetal brain demonstrates normal sulcation and gyration. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.5 mm bilaterally. Impression: Unilateral left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK) with a normal, hypertrophied right kidney and normal amniotic fluid. Fetal nephrology follow-up is recommended.

MRI evaluation of the brain shows completely unremarkable brain morphology. No evidence of space-occupying lesions, subarachnoid or parenchymal hemorrhage, or focal white matter signal abnormalities is present. The extra-axial spaces and cisterns are clear. Pituitary gland and optic chiasm appear normal for age.

Impression: Normal MR scan of the brain. No acute pathology, thrombosis, or intracranial lesion seen to explain the patient's severe postpartum headache symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced sulcation appropriate for late third trimester. Secondary and tertiary sulci are clearly visible, including well-defined central and parieto-occipital sulci. The lateral ventricles measure 6.5 mm bilaterally, and the corpus callosum is fully developed and normal in thickness. Cerebellar hemispheres and vermis are robust and without anomaly.

Fetal organs and limbs are normal; amniotic fluid volume is completely adequate. Impression: Unremarkable third-trimester fetal MRI showing normal, age-appropriate cortical maturation and normal visceral anatomy.

Cardiac MRI performed to evaluate acute chest pain radiating to the back, worse when supine. There is a circumferential, moderate pericardial effusion measuring up to 1.6 cm in maximal thickness adjacent to the right ventricular free wall, without definitive features of cardiac tamponade. The pericardium is thickened (4 mm) and demonstrates intense late gadolinium enhancement and hyperintensity on T2-STIR, indicating active acute inflammation. Biventricular size and function are preserved with an LVEF of 58%.

Impression: Acute pericarditis with moderate pericardial effusion and prominent pericardial thickening and enhancement. No current MRI evidence of ventricular diastolic collapse to suggest tamponade.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a 45-year-old female. There is asymmetric, marked hypertrophy of the basal-to-mid anteroseptal wall, measuring up to 21 mm during end-diastole. Dynamic cine imaging demonstrates systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve leaflet, resulting in moderate mitral regurgitation and transient left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with a visible flow void. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 74%.

Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy, mid-myocardial hyperenhancement at the RV insertion points and within the hypertrophied anterior septum. Impression: Phenotypic findings of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant septal hypertrophy, SAM, and associated focal myocardial fibrosis.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 26-year-old pregnant patient (22 weeks gestation) with suspected left ventricular non-compaction. There is prominent trabeculation of the left ventricular apex and lateral walls, with a non-compacted to compacted myocardial thickness ratio of 2.4:1 at end-diastole. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is slightly elevated, but the global ejection fraction is preserved at 56%. No late gadolinium enhancement is present. Right ventricular morphology is unremarkable.

Impression: Structural features consistent with Left Ventricular Non-Compaction (LVNC). Global systolic function remains preserved, indicating good compensation during gestation.

MRI of the brain in a pregnant patient showing a normal pituitary gland with physiological enlargement typical of third-trimester gestation. Pituitary height is 9 mm with a slightly convex superior margin. Optic chiasm and cavernous sinuses are completely normal and free of compression. Brain parenchymal signal is normal.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain with physiological gestational pituitary enlargement. No pathologic mass or optical pathway compromise is present.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 25-year-old female with a newly diagnosed murmur. There is a large defect within the mid-atrial septum measuring approximately 24 mm in diameter, consistent with an ostium secundum atrial septal defect (ASD). Phase-contrast flow quantification demonstrates a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1:1. The right ventricle is moderately dilated (RVEDV 140 mL/m²) demonstrating mild volume overload and hyperkinesis, though RVEF remains preserved at 58%. The left ventricle is normal in size and function (LVEF 63%).

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt (Qp:Qs = 2.1) and secondary right ventricular volume overload. No evidence of pulmonary arterial hypertension is suspected on these sequences.

Brain MR imaging reveals normal morphology and signal intensity of the cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, and brainstem. The ventricular system, cortical sulci, and basal cisterns are unremarkable. No abnormal areas of restricted diffusion, parenchymal hemorrhage, or pathological enhancement are visualized.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular abnormalities are identified to account for the patient's episodic dizziness.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising within the right cerebellopontine angle, measuring 1.8 x 1.4 x 1.3 cm. The mass extends into and widens the internal acoustic canal, exhibiting strong homogenous enhancement. The brainstem is slightly compressed without signal change. Left internal acoustic canal is normal.

Impression: Right vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) with mild mass effect on the adjacent brainstem and cerebellum. ENT and neurosurgical follow-up is recommended.

A baseline cardiac MRI was performed on a 62-year-old female prior to initiating cardiotoxic chemotherapy for newly diagnosed breast cancer. Cine images show normal left ventricular internal dimensions, geometry, and wall thickness. Left ventricular global systolic function is well-preserved, with an ejection fraction of 62%. The right ventricle is normal in size and demonstrates normal systolic function (RVEF 55%).

No evidence of late gadolinium enhancement, focal myocardial edema, or pericardial fluid collection is seen. Impression: Normal baseline cardiac MRI study demonstrating preserved biventricular systolic function and no structural abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI was executed for atypical, exertional chest discomfort. Analysis of the left and right ventricles shows normal end-diastolic volumes, normal wall thickness, and preserved global systolic function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 65%. Dynamic perfusion imaging during pharmacologic stress (regadenoson) reveals no inducible myocardial perfusion defects. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is entirely negative for focal scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with no evidence of myocardial ischemia, prior infarction, or structural myocardial disease.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced development of the fetal brain. Deep tertiary sulci are well-formed and appropriate for late gestation. The ventricular atria are small and symmetric, measuring 5.5 mm on both sides. The brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are fully mature and show no evidence of focal parenchymal lesions or hemorrhage.

The lungs are well-expanded with fluid, and the abdominal organs and spine are completely normal. The maternal placenta and amniotic fluid levels are unremarkable. Impression: Completely normal third-trimester fetal MRI study with age-appropriate brain development.

MR sequences demonstrate prominent FLAIR hyperintensity within the basal cisterns, Sylvian fissures, and cerebral sulci, consistent with acute subarachnoid hemorrhage. Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) demonstrates a 5 mm focal out-pouching at the anterior communicating artery, oriented anteriorly.

Impression: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage secondary to ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Immediate neurosurgical consultation is required for endovascular coiling or surgical clipping.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal brain parenchyma with preserved gray-white matter differentiation. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for age. No abnormal extra-axial fluid collections or pathological contrast enhancement are observed after gadolinium administration.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No evidence of demyelinating disease, mass lesion, or structural pathology to account for the patient's sensory symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation performed due to poor visualization on fetal ultrasound. Multisequence MR imaging shows normal cerebral development with appropriate progress of the parieto-occipital and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.5 mm bilaterally, and the corpus callosum is intact and normal in thickness. The posterior fossa shows a well-formed cerebellum and normal cisterna magna.

Fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and bladder are within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation. No intracranial or extracranial anomalies are identified.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks 5 days gestation. The posterior fossa demonstrates mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis. The fastigium is elevated, and there is a keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna. The cisterna magna is moderately prominent, measuring 11.5 mm. The bilateral cerebellar hemispheres are normal in volume. The supratentorial brain is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.8 mm.

No other congenital anomalies are visualized. Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (isolated inferior vermian hypoplasia) with mild prominence of the cisterna magna.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrates normal gray and white matter differentiation. There are no areas of restricted diffusion, intracranial hemorrhage, or pathologic extra-axial fluid collections. The ventricles and basal cisterns are normal in caliber. No abnormal enhancement is seen following contrast administration.

Impression: Normal MR brain scan. No structural brain pathology or underlying cause for the patient's headaches is identified.

Brain MRI demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense intra-axial lesion centered within the white matter of the left frontal lobe, measuring 3.1 x 2.4 cm. No significant mass effect, midline shift, or associated vasogenic edema is visualized. MR spectroscopy shows a mild increase in the choline-to-creatine ratio.

Impression: T2/FLAIR hyperintense non-enhancing frontal lobe lesion, most consistent with a low-grade glioma (e.g., astrocytoma). Direct clinical comparison with prior imaging or tissue biopsy is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The right hemidiaphragm is deficient, with herniation of the right lobe of the liver, gallbladder, and loops of bowel into the right hemithorax. This has caused severe compression and leftward displacement of the heart and mediastinum. Fetal lung volumes are significantly reduced.

The brain shows normal sulcation patterns for 29 weeks. The lateral ventricles are normal, with an atrial measurement of 5.8 mm. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation, severe mediastinal shift, and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks gestation for suspected ventriculomegaly on prenatal ultrasound. The brain parenchyma shows age-appropriate development with normal migration and early primary sulcation patterns. The ventricular system is normal in size, with the bilateral lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.5 mm and 6.8 mm, well within the normal limit of less than 10 mm. The corpus callosum is intact and fully visualized, and the posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, appear normal.

Fetal thoracic, abdominal, and spinal anatomy are visualized and unremarkable. No evidence of congenital diaphragmatic hernia, spinal dysraphism, or renal anomalies. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body MRI at 22 weeks gestation, with normal ventricular atrial measurements and no structural anomalies identified.

Cardiac MRI shows an area of significant transmural thinning and akinesis of the left ventricular anterior wall and apex. Delayed post-contrast imaging demonstrates extensive, near-transmural late gadolinium enhancement in the LAD coronary artery territory, involving approximately 85% of the wall thickness in the apical septum. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is elevated, and the LVEF is depressed at 35%.

Impression: Ischemic cardiomyopathy with a large transmural myocardial infarction in the anterior wall and apex (LAD territory). Substantial non-viable myocardium is present within the infarct zone.

Brain MRI was obtained utilizing standard multiplanar sequences. The brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology without evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are unremarkable and symmetric, with no signs of hydrocephalus or intracranial hypertension. Major vascular flow voids at the skull base are well-preserved.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural or vascular abnormality identified to explain the patient's severe postpartum headaches, which may be tension-related or post-dural puncture related if clinically applicable.

A 34-year-old female with a history of palpitations underwent cardiac MRI for comprehensive structural evaluation. The left and right ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and mass are entirely normal. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 60%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or delayed hyperenhancement areas are detected.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study showing no structural, functional, or myocardial tissue abnormalities to account for the patient's symptoms of palpitations.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a defect in the lumbosacral spine. There is a posterior spina bifida defect from L4 to S2, with herniation of a meningeal sac containing neural elements, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Intracranially, there is descent of the cerebellar tonsils into the foramen magnum and a banana-shaped cerebellum, characteristic of Chiari II malformation. The lateral ventricles measure 11.5 mm, representing mild ventriculomegaly.

Sulcation patterns are early but normal for gestational age. Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with classic intracranial features of a Chiari II malformation and associated mild ventriculomegaly.

MR Venogram and Brain MRI demonstrate an absence of normal flow void and a hyperintense T1/T2 signal within the superior sagittal sinus and left transverse sinus, indicative of acute dural venous sinus thrombosis. There are small areas of petechial hemorrhage and venous congestion in the left parietal cortex with mild edema.

Impression: Superior sagittal sinus and left transverse sinus thrombosis with associated localized venous congestion and petechial hemorrhage. Prompt clinical management is recommended.

Cardiac MRI reveals small, residual focal areas of subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement along the lateral free wall of the left ventricle. There is no active myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, indicating a resolved or chronic phase of prior inflammation. Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 57%, and chamber sizes are normal.

Impression: Chronic, non-active phase of prior myocarditis with persistent trace subepicardial fibrosis. Overall biventricular size and systolic function are preserved.

High-resolution cine MRI sequences of the heart were obtained. Both ventricles demonstrate normal volumes, muscle thickness, and systolic function. LVEF is 61% and RVEF is 58%. The valves are thin and mobile with no significant stenosis or regurgitation. Delayed enhancement imaging is entirely negative for focal myocardial injury.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Preserved biventricular function with no evidence of myocardial infiltration, scarring, or major structural anomalies.

Cardiac MRI shows severe global dilation of the left ventricle (LVEDV 280 mL) with severe global hypokinesia. The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 22%. Mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed in the basal-to-mid interventricular septum, typical of a non-ischemic dilated etiology. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with an RVEF of 40%.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction and mid-wall septal LGE, indicative of a non-ischemic pathology.

Cardiac MRI shows marked ballooning of the left ventricular apex and mid-ventricular segments with hyperkinesis of the basal segments, manifesting a classic apical ballooning phenotype. The overall left ventricular ejection fraction is moderately depressed at 42%. There is no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement, which rules out acute myocardial infarction. Mild edema is present in the apical segments on T2-weighted sequences.

Impression: Findings are typical for stress-induced (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, likely triggered by severe peripartum stress. There is apical and mid-ventricular ballooning and systolic dysfunction, with no evidence of coronary-related ischemic scar.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral, asymmetric dilation of the lateral ventricles. The right ventricular atrium measures 13.5 mm and the left measures 14.2 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly. The cerebral mantle is thin but intact, and primary sulcation is slightly delayed for gestational age. The corpus callosum is present but appeared slightly stretched.

No intraventricular hemorrhage, subependymal nodules, or obvious neural tube defects are identified. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend serial follow-up ultrasounds and pediatric neurosurgical consultation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 58-year-old male with chronic ischemic heart disease. The left ventricle is severely dilated (LVEDV 210 mL/m²) with global hypokinesis and akinesis of the anterior, septal, and apical walls. The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 32%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging demonstrates extensive, fully transmural (>75%) scar in the anterior and anteroseptal walls from the base to the apex.

Impression: Severe ischemic cardiomyopathy with a large, transmural, non-viable anterior-septal-apical myocardial infarction. Severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction and dilation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates classic findings of rheumatic mitral stenosis. There is severe thickening of the anterior mitral valve leaflet with characteristic 'hockey-stick' diastolic bowing. Significant dilation of the left atrium is noted (volume index 68 mL/m²) with turbulent flow across the mitral valve in diastole. The calculated mitral valve area by planimetry is 1.1 cm². The left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 58%.

Impression: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with significant left atrial enlargement. Left ventricular size and systolic function are normal.

Cardiac MRI reveals patchy, non-ischemic subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the mid-to-apical lateral wall of the left ventricle. Prominent hyperintensity is noted on T2-weighted triple IR imaging in the corresponding regions, indicating localized myocardial edema. The global left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 50% with mild hypokinesis of the lateral free wall. No pericardial effusion is seen.

Impression: Imaging findings satisfy Lake Louise Criteria, highly characteristic of acute myocarditis. Mild global LV systolic dysfunction is noted.

Cardiac MRI reveals prominent asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal diastolic septal wall thickness measuring 22 mm. Dynamic cine imaging shows systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve, resulting in left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with a measured peak velocity gradient of 42 mmHg. Patchy mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the hypertrophied septal segments, characteristic of focal fibrosis. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 72%.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant septal hypertrophy, dynamic LVOT obstruction, and focal septal scarring.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation. Severe shortening of all long bones is observed, with femur and humerus lengths falling far below the 1st percentile, consistent with micromelia. The thoracic cage is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, causing severe restriction and compression of the developing lungs. There is mild ventriculomegaly with an atrial width of 9.5 mm and a prominent forehead (frontal bossing). The spine shows normal segmentation.

Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, highly suspicious for thanatophoric dysplasia or osteogenesis imperfecta type II, given the narrow thoracic cavity and severe micromelia.

Brain MRI shows multiple small, well-defined cystic lesions in the subarachnoid spaces and gray-white matter junctions. Several cysts contain a tiny, eccentric hyperintense nodule representing the scolex, characteristic of the vesicular stage of neurocysticercosis. There is minimal surrounding edema and no mass effect.

Impression: Multiple parenchymal and subarachnoid cysts with scolex, highly suggestive of active neurocysticercosis. Recommend infectious disease consultation.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a large occipital encephalocele. A midline defect in the occipital bone is identified, through which a sac measuring 3.5 x 2.8 cm herniates. This sac contains CSF and dysplastic, disorganized occipital lobe parenchyma. Significant distortion of the remaining brainstem and posterior fossa structures is observed. The lateral ventricles are dilated, with the atrium measuring 13.0 mm. Sulcation is smooth, which is normal for 22 weeks.

The spine appears intact. Visualized visceral structures are otherwise unremarkable. Impression: Occipital encephalocele with herniated dysplastic brain tissue and associated bilateral ventriculomegaly. Prognosis is guarded; pediatric neurosurgery and genetics consultation is strongly recommended.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass arising along the left sphenoid wing, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The mass is isointense to grey matter on T1 and T2 sequences and displays homogeneous, intense enhancement following gadolinium administration, with a prominent 'dural tail' sign. There is mild compression of the adjacent left temporal lobe with associated vasogenic edema, but no ventricular compression or midline shift.

Impression: Left sphenoid wing extra-axial mass, classic for a meningioma. Mild local mass effect and edema are present; neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI was performed on a 21-year-old collegiate athlete for evaluation of borderline left ventricular hypertrophy on electrocardiogram. The study demonstrates mild, symmetrical biventricular dilation. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 108 mL/m2 with a normal ejection fraction of 58%. The maximal left ventricular wall thickness is 11 mm throughout. Right ventricular volume is similarly increased (RVEDVI 112 mL/m2) with preserved systolic function (RVEF 55%). No late gadolinium enhancement or T1/T2 mapping abnormalities are identified.

Impression: Physiologic cardiac remodeling consistent with an athletic training phenotype (athlete's heart). No structural or tissue characteristics of hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy are identified.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe skeletal anomalies. There is severe, symmetric rhizomelic shortening and bowing of all long bones. The thorax is narrow and bell-shaped with shortened ribs, causing secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Frontal bossing of the skull is prominent. The ventricular atrium measures 6.4 mm, and cerebral cortical sulcation is appropriate for 27 weeks.

No internal organ herniations are present. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with narrow thoracic diameter and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrates bilateral, symmetric areas of high T2/FLAIR signal intensity within the subcortical white matter of the occipital and parietal lobes. No restricted diffusion is observed on DWI/ADC mapping, and there is no evidence of acute hemorrhage or mass effect. These findings are highly characteristic of vasogenic edema in the setting of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES).

Impression: Symmetric parieto-occipital white matter changes consistent with posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), clinically correlating with the patient's postpartum presentation. Close clinical monitoring and blood pressure control are recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates inferior displacement of the cerebellar tonsils below the level of the foramen magnum by approximately 7.5 mm. The tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is associated crowding at the craniovertebral junction. Cine cerebrospinal fluid flow imaging reveals diminished flow at the posterior aspect of the foramen magnum. No syrinx is noted in the cervical spine.

Impression: Chiari I malformation. There is posterior craniovertebral junction crowding, but no cervical cord syrinx is visualized.

Cardiac MRI reveals dilatation of the right ventricle with multiple microaneurysms and regional dyskinesis of the right ventricular free wall (the 'triangle of dysplasia'). The right ventricular ejection fraction is depressed at 38%. T1-weighted imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrate extensive transmural fibrofatty replacement in the right ventricular free wall and patchy enhancement in the left ventricular apex.

Impression: Morphological features and functional changes highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC). Further clinical correlation with electrocardiographic and familial risk history is indicated.

Brain MRI with dedicated pituitary views reveals a well-circumscribed, solid mass expanding the sella turcica and extending suprasellarly. The lesion measures 1.8 x 1.4 x 1.5 cm and causes superior displacement and compression of the optic chiasm. There is no invasion into the cavernous sinuses, but the normal pituitary gland is compressed along the posterior sella.

Impression: Pituitary macroadenoma with suprasellar extension and optic chiasm compression, clinically significant given potential visual field deficits.

Fetal MRI obtained at 32 weeks 0 days gestation. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal sulcation and gyration appropriate for 32 weeks, with prominent central and lateral sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and normal in size, with atrial measurements of 5.8 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum is fully formed and normal in thickness. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are within normal limits.

The fetal chest displays normal, well-aerated lung parenchyma. Abdominal viscera and spine are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate central nervous system development.

Brain MRI demonstrates an ill-defined, non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintense infiltrative lesion centered in the right temporal lobe, measuring approximately 3.5 x 2.8 cm. There is minimal mass effect on the right lateral ventricle temporal horn and no associated vasogenic edema, restricted diffusion, or necrosis.

Impression: Infiltrative intra-axial lesion of the right temporal lobe, highly suspicious for a low-grade glioma (such as astrocytoma). Recommend magnetic resonance spectroscopy and neurosurgical referral.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation evaluated for suspect ultrasound findings. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate appropriate and symmetric development, with normal sylvian fissure formation and early parieto-occipital sulcation patterns matching the stated gestational age. The ventricular system is normal in size, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles measuring 5.8 mm. No structural midline abnormalities are seen; the corpus callosum and cavum septum pellucidum are present and structurally intact.

Fetal thoracic, abdominal, and spinal anatomy are well visualized and unremarkable. Normal amniotic fluid volume. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body development for 22 weeks, with no MR evidence of central nervous system anomalies or ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI demonstrates a well-defined zone of restricted diffusion involving the right insular cortex and frontoparietal operculum, with corresponding hyperintensity on DWI and hypointensity on the ADC map. Mild gyral swelling and local sulcal effacement are noted in the affected territory, consistent with acute to subacute infarction in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) distribution.

Impression: Acute to subacute ischemic infarction in the right MCA territory. No hemorrhagic transformation is observed on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI).

Brain MRI reveals a non-enhancing, ill-defined infiltrative mass in the left frontal lobe white matter, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.8 cm. The lesion is hyperintense on T2/FLAIR and hypointense on T1-weighted images, with minimal mass effect and no restricted diffusion or surrounding edema. No significant enhancement is seen following gadolinium administration.

Impression: Left frontal lobe intra-axial mass, characteristic of a low-grade diffuse glioma (e.g., astrocytoma). Close follow-up or tissue biopsy is recommended for definitive histological diagnosis.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with previously repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. The right ventricle is severely dilated, with an indexed end-diastodial volume of 165 mL/m². Quantitative flow analysis reveals severe, free pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 46%. The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 42%. The left ventricle is normal in size with preserved function (LVEF 58%).

Impression: Status post repaired Tetralogy of Fallot with severe pulmonary regurgitation and severe right ventricular dilation. These findings meet criteria for consideration of pulmonary valve replacement.

Cardiac MRI assesses myocardial viability in a 58-year-old male with a history of prior anterior myocardial infarction. The left ventricle is dilated with a thinned, akinetic anterior and apical wall. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) reveals transmural (>75% wall thickness) hyperenhancement of the mid-to-distal anterior wall and apex, consistent with non-viable scar tissue in the LAD distribution. The calculated LVEF is severely depressed at 38%.

Impression: Severe ischemic cardiomyopathy with non-viable anterior and apical myocardial scar tissue. Depressed left ventricular systolic function with global and regional wall motion abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate highly mature, complex sulcation and gyral formation appropriate for 34 weeks. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.2 mm symmetrically, with no ventriculomegaly. All midline structures, including the corpus callosum and septum pellucidum, are completely normal. Fetal lungs and abdomen show no structural abnormalities.

Impression: Reassuring fetal MRI with normal neurodevelopmental maturity and normal ventricular anatomy for gestational age.

Brain MRI was acquired for the evaluation of persistent non-specific dizziness. Imaging demonstrates normal intracranial anatomy. There is no evidence of acute infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, demyelinating plaques, or mass lesions within the cerebrum, brainstem, or posterior fossa. The internal auditory canals are symmetric and normal.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No central cause for the patient's dizziness, such as vestibular schwannoma or cerebellar stroke, is identified.

Fetal MRI performed at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal singleton fetus. The early sulcation pattern of the brain, including the insular cleft and sylvian fissure, is completely appropriate for 20 weeks of development. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with an atrial diameter measuring 5.2 mm. The posterior fossa structures, corpus callosum, and spine are intact.

All other thoracic, abdominal, and musculoskeletal structures appear normal. Amniotic fluid is within normal range. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation with no structural abnormalities or developmental delays identified.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced and symmetric fetal brain development. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrium measuring 6.8 mm. The corpus callosum is fully formed and has a normal thickness. The cortical gyration is highly complex, displaying well-developed secondary and tertiary sulci appropriate for 36 weeks.

The posterior fossa, face, neck, spine, and trunk demonstrate normal anatomy. There are no signs of fetal masses or diaphragmatic defects. Impression: Completely normal, unremarkable fetal MRI study at 36 weeks gestation showing expected advanced brain maturation and healthy organ development.
